To put it into words, it would be for a very long time.

He cautiously pried up the floorboards, making sure not to damage anything, knowing he’d
face a lifetime of scolding from a maid who was just waiting for him to slip up.

What he discovered was essentially a stash of alcohol, specifically wine.

“Wine?” he exclaimed, reaching for a bottle that was sealed and had a light layer of dust on
it. He wasn’t an expert, but it looked authentic to him.

“I heard Roswaal’s grandmother was a heavy drinker; this must be her secret stash,” she
remarked.

“Roswaal’s grandmother? Oh right, you did mention her…” he trailed off, his thoughts
drifting to Roswaal’s unnatural Od. They were essentially a person’s soul, and his felt off, as
if it didn’t belong to him.

‘Did his grandmother transfer her soul to him? Is the Roswaal we’re talking to the same as
his grandma?’ The thought sent chills down his spine.

“Are you going to drink that? I didn’t take you to be the alcoholic type, but you are hopeless,
so it’s a given,”

“I’m not an alcoholic! I just enjoy a drink now and then,” he replied, still inspecting the
bottle.

“Since it belonged to Roswaal’s grandmother, it’s technically his property. You shouldn’t
drink it,” she warned him.

“Come on, do you have to act like I’m some depressed adult who can’t get his shitty life
together? I’m not going to drink it!” he exclaimed, feigning outrage.

The door creaked open, and the sound of silver bells drew their attention.



“There you are you two,” Emilia said as she appeared in the doorway, dressed in a blue and
white outfit with a blue miniskirt, white stockings, and black shoes.

“What are you both doing?” she asked, stepping closer.

“Barasu was just sharing his sad life story and all the struggles he’s faced. Honest and kind
Ram was advising him against turning to alcohol, even if this hopeless man's life is
miserable,” Ram said, shamelessly lying to Emilia.

“Subaru…” she looked at him with concern in her eyes, much to his annoyance. “I know life
has been tough for you since your parents died but I promise that Puck and I will help you get
back on track!” she said with a reassuring smile.

“My life isn’t hard! She’s just lying to you!” he snapped.

“O-oh, I see…”

Subaru sighed, what did he expect? Ram would be a nuisance for a while.

“Anyway, Emilia, do you enjoy drinking?” he asked the half-elf.

“Ah, no, I’ve never had alcohol before,” she replied, shaking her head.

“You haven’t? Oh, that’s too bad; you’re missing out on a lot,” he said.

“Trying to turn Emilia-sama into an alcoholic? What a disgusting and shameful man you
are,” Ram remarked in her usual tone.

“I’m not! Jeez, Rammy, You were going to have to wake up eventually, even if it’s cold
today, you know?” he retorted.

“Hmph.”

“Speaking of cold weather…” he said, glancing at Emilia. “Aren’t you cold in those clothes?
They don’t seem very warm…”

Emilia's expression shifted to one of panic. “Cold? What cold? Honestly, don’t you think it’s
super hot today?” She exclaimed, fanning herself with her hand.

“It’s reeeeeally hot today; I’m sweating a lot here!”

“…Right.”

“Anyways. I’d love to talk more, but I’ve got things to take care of. see you later, Subaru!”
She ran away as if she were on fire.

“Wow,” he remarked once she was out of earshot. “Emilia is definitely the worst liar I’ve
ever encountered; it’s kind of cute,” he added.

Ram shot him a scathing look. “Tch, pervert.”



“I’m not!”

 

---------------------------------

 

The day continued on as usual, with him, Ram, and Rem tidying up the mansion. Later, he
bumped into Beatrice and greeted her, but she promptly shooed him away.

Eventually, the day turned into night and Subaru settled into bed, ready to call it a night.

‘It’s getting colder than it was in the morning,’ he mused, noticing that the amount of red
mana had risen since the day began, making the atmosphere cooler.

‘I haven’t seen Emilia or Puck, so I’m betting they’re behind this,’ he concluded simply.

They were the only ones with fire attributes, and Roswaal wasn’t emitting any fire mana, so it
had to be them.

“Well, whatever. I’ll just try to sleep it off; hopefully, it’ll be sorted out by tomorrow.”

Just to be safe, he activated his infinity, which should help filter out the cold and keep him
comfortable, and reinforced himself with cursed energy as insurance.

Then, he drifted off to sleep.

Chapter End Notes

This is the first part of the Memory Snow OVA, it's a pretty long one so I have split it
into two.

Enjoy.



Chapter 15: Arc 2.5 - Puck’s Mating Season
Chapter Notes

Some important stuff came up, so the Memory Snow section will be cut down to three
parts. Actually, we might as well count this as a mini-arc in and of itself.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

“What the fuck is this?!” 

Subaru sat on his bed, utterly shocked by the sight in front of him. He never imagined
anything like this could happen.

His entire room was encased in ice.

Everywhere he looked—from the bed to the desk, the closet blocking the door, the curtains,
the windows, and even the walls and ceiling—everything was covered in a thick layer of
frost. Even the blanket he had wrapped around himself was frozen solid.

‘It was just a bit chilly yesterday! How did it get like this?!’ he thought, feeling thankful that
he had put on his insurance before going to sleep; otherwise, he would have turned into a
popsicle by morning.

He surveyed the room with his Six Eyes, noticing a significant increase in the red mana in the
air, nearly three times what it had been the day before.

His mind quickly turned to the culprits behind this chaos, and he knew exactly who it was,
‘Emilia! Puck! You two have gone too far?!’ he thought, filled with anger. 

He then stomped his way to the door, after breaking the ice around the lock with a cursed
energy bullet, he stepped outside.

He was immediately greeted by the blue-haired oni-maid with a bowl cut. “Subaru-kun!
You’re awake!” she exclaimed, rushing toward him.

She was dressed in her maid outfit, which covered most of her body, including her chest, and
she wore blue gloves—This was the winter maid outfit she had mentioned yesterday.

“Remmy! Thank goodness you’re here! Where is everyone? Are they okay?!” he asked,
glancing around at the frozen mess on the floor.

Rem looked pleased that he was concerned for her and replied, “They’re all awake, Subaru-
kun. Rem was going to wake you up sooner, but Nee-sama was feeling especially cold today,
so I had to warm her up!”



Subaru just stared at her, and the image of Ram and Rem cuddled together under a blanket
popped into his mind—

‘Great, that image is going to stick with me for a while,’ HE made a disgusted face.

“Dammit, Remmy! I didn’t need to know that!” he exclaimed in outrage.

“You're right! Rem is so sorry. Rem should have come to warm you up earlier! ALso, If you'd
like, Rem can make you some tea!

"That's even worse! Did you even hear what I just said? And yes, I would love some tea, you

"Ugh, don’t distract me! Remmy, we need to have a meeting. I have an idea of who's
responsible for this chaos, so please gather everyone in the mansion and bring them to the
living room. We need to get to the bottom of this!"

"Hai, Subaru-kun!"






---------------------------------

 

“Well, well, weeeeell! My dear Rem mentioned you were having an urgent meeting. What's

“Do I really have to say it? Just look around you!”

Roswaal stepped into the mansion's living room, which was covered in ice, just like

taking care of her sister Ram, who was shivering under a blanket.

“Oh dear, it’s not that urgent, Subaru-kun. It’s just a bit of ice and cold,” Roswaal said
nonchalantly

“Not urgent? Look at poor Ram! She’s freezing!” Subaru exclaimed, pointing at the shivering
oni.

“Ram was perfectly fine in her bed until that scoundrel poisoned my sister and forced her to

infuriating. Are you even human?” she said, trembling.

“Now, now, it’s not my fault some people can handle the cold better than others. Like a
certain Oni, for example.”

“How can someone as hopeless as Barasu handle a cold like this? Achoo!”



“Because I’m built different.”

“That doesn’t—Achoo!” She sneezed into Rem’s waiting tissue.

“Don’t worry, Nee-sama! Rem will take care of your sneezes!” she said cheerfully.

“Hmmm, you might have a point. This situation has definitely spiraled out of control,” he
remarked casually.

“I assume you know who’s behind this mess, which is why I called this meeting to begin
with,” he continued.

“Of course, through the process of elimination, we already know who the culprit is, right?”

Subaru glanced around. ‘Only four of us are here: me, Ram, Rem, and Roswaal. Emilia,
Puck, and Beatrice are missing…’

“I suspect Puck and Emilia are responsible, but is Beatrice involved too?” he inquired.

“Absolutely! Puck and Beatrice are quite close. If something were to happen because of
Puck, she would definitely be informed and would act accordingly as well.”

“Wow, I didn’t expect her to be involved too. So, how’s Arlam Village holding up? I doubt
they can deal with this extreme cold…” he remarked, recalling their situation. A sudden drop
in temperature could be really damaging, especially for their crops and animals.

“You don’t need to worry, Subaaaaaru-kun. This cold is only affecting the mansion and its
vicinity. The village is completely safe.”

“Really? Why’s that?”

“It’s thanks to the hard work of two individuals who are making sure it doesn’t spread.”

“Seriously?! They’re doing that and we’re over here suffering in silence! I can’t accept this!
Rem, get your lazy bum of a sister up, and Roswaal, you’re coming too! We need to have a
talk with that naughty Half-elf and her sassy cat!”

“Tch, handle it yourself, scum. Ram is perfectly fine right here—”

“As you wish, Subaru-kun! Come on, nee-sama, let’s go!” Rem interrupted Ram, lifting her
up and moving along with Subaru, much to Ram’s anger.

They soon arrived at the door leading to Emilia’s room, where they could hear the howling
wind from inside.

‘Nowhere to hide, Emilia. We got you cornered,’ He smirked, signaling Roswaal to take the

“Pardon the interruption at this hour, Emilia-sama. Do you have a moment? We’d like to

“Roswaal?!” Emilia exclaimed, clearly taken aback. She began to panic, “Uh—Um—e—just

Roswaal gestured for Subaru to take over. He called out, “Emilia, just come out already, the

“Jig? What jig? Is he your friend? Hi, Jig! Nice to meet you, I’m Emilia, just Emilia!” Emilia

“Emilia-sama, your talent for lying is as impressive as Barasu’s cooking skills,” sadly, it

“Now, Emilia, let’s stop playing around. Where’s Puck? I just want to have a word with him,”

“It’s alright, Lia. There’s no point in hiding it any longer,” a high-pitched voice chimed in

“No, you weren’t,” Subaru interjected as he stepped beside her to get a glimpse of the culprit.
On a tiny rug, resting his head on a comically small pillow and covered by a little blanket,

Subaru took notice of the torrents of red mana flowing from him into the atmosphere. There
was no longer any doubt about who’s behind this mess.

Puck innocently smiled and said, "I’m sorry for the trouble I caused. Please don’t be mad
with Emilia and Betty; they were just trying to help me out."

“Yeah, no.”

 

---------------------------------

 

The residents of the mansion were gathered in the dining room, with Roswaal occupying his

Everyone's attention shifted to Puck, with Ram giving him her most intense glare.

“A what now?” Subaru inquired.

“A magic release period. It’s something that only affects magical beings like me,” Puck

“So all that mana release is because you’re looking for a wife? Wow, why didn’t you say

“I’m not an animal, so I don’t have a mating season! That’s a really rude thing to say!” he

“…You are literally a cat, though.” Subaru replied flatly, while Emilia giggled at the

“Just take it easy, Puck. You know how Subaru loves to joke around,” she said, having been

“Hmph, it’s typical for Subaru to be rude to others, even if he calls it a ‘joke’,” Beatrice

“Really now, at least Puck and Emilia offered apologies, but did we hear anything from you?
Nope. Nothing at all. So much for you, miss ‘Manners’”

Beatrice huffed even more, “Betty has no reason to apologize. She was simply looking out
for her Bubby, infact.”

Realizing that arguing with Beatrice would lead nowhere, Subaru shifted his focus back to
Puck.

"So, what’s the deal with this ‘Magic Release period’?" he inquired. He could probably use

"Well, you know how a gate holds your mana? Sometimes, that mana accumulates beyond its

"Some?! You call this 'some'?" he exclaimed, waving his arms at the frozen furniture. After

"What about you all? Have you experienced this Mati–I mean, Magic Release period? Or is it

"Talented magicians experience it, like meeeee," Roswaal stretched out the words. "In my

‘Eh? Why is he... Never mind, I don’t want to know,’ he thought, shivering at the image.

"Nee-sama and I don’t have it; we’re not skilled enough in magic," she replied.

“Betty manages the surplus mana by keeping her door-crossing spell active, I suppose.
Unlucky for her, some pest always finds her, so Betty has to put in more mana than usual."
Beatrice chimed in with a jab at our favorite sunglasses-wearing butler.

"I'm not a powerful magic user either, so no, I don’t have it," she said, leaving Subaru

"Hey, Puck, weren’t you nearly out of mana when we rescued those kids? Why do you need

"Well... you know how spirits can draw mana from the air to cast spells? Contracted ones can

"Two days."

"Two days?! By the time you're done, you'll have to deal with Ram's frozen body," he said,

"Ram will not—Achoo!"

Emilia said, “Um, how about we find something to do to keep ourselves occupied? I’m really

Subaru was lost in his thoughts and didn’t notice her at first, but then a lightbulb went off in

“Impressive as always, Subaru-Kun! You have my admiration!”

“Okay, you heard her! Let’s go!”

"Yeah, I guess so. What should we do, Subaru? What should we do..." he mumbled the last

mansion, pour water into the bath and heat it up! We could make a hot spring to get us
through this!"

“Impressive as always, Subaru-Kun! You have my admiration!”



"You said that before, but whatever, let’s go!"

"As much as Ram would love to help, that’s not an option." Ram decided to be the party

‘This is even worse than finding my whole room frozen,’ he thought, his face twisted in sheer

“That would be me, Subaru-Kun! I made it just for you because I know how much you love

“I noticed how you kept adding it to everything you ate, so I thought I’d surprise you with a

“As you wish, Roswaal-sama.”



“Um, maybe we could think of something else while we wait for Puck’s Mana release to
finish?” Emilia suggested from the side.

Subaru pondered this, ‘What can we do… everything here is frozen, so our options are
limited. Ros-ros doesn’t want to go camping, and with the rain… Wait, it’s raining right now,
and it’s so cold that ice is forming, which means…!’

“I’ve got it! I know how we can pass the time and get through this mess!” he declared.

“Oh! Does subaru-kun have one of his genius ideas! Rem wants to hear it!” She said

“With how cold it is, the rain outside is bound to turn into snow! Once that happens, we

seemed excited about the prospect.

“Impressive as always, Subaru-Kun! You have–”

“Rem, shut up! Every time you say that, things go horribly wrong!”

Chapter 16: Arc 2.5 - King Of The Castle
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

A group of villagers meandered along the dirt paths, making their way toward a grand
mansion that loomed in the distance, having received a personal invitation from their lord.

These were the residents of Arlam Village, on their way to the estate of Roswaal L. Mathers,
the court mage and their feudal lord.

Typically, an invitation from a lord would stir feelings of apprehension and worry among the
peasants, but today, they were filled with anticipation and optimism.

Their opinions had changed considerably after a few of their children, who went messing
were rescued by workers and a candidate for the throne.

There were two individuals they felt especially grateful towards.

Initially, they had been fearful and uncertain about the Silver-Haired Half-Elf, but that had
changed after she healed their children from the Wolgram curse.

Then there was the butler, who had bravely entered the forest and saved those children after
quickly defeating an entire pack of Wolgram.

Indeed, the lord's popularity among the villagers had never been higher.

A short girl with radish-colored hair and a red ribbon in her hair walked through the crowd of
villagers. This was none other than Petra Leyte, one of the children who had been rescued.

She walked alongside her friends—Mild, Meina, Cain, Dine, and Lucas—who were all the
children that were rescued.

“Hey, Petra!” Meina called out, the only girl in the group. “Are you excited to find out why
Roswaal-sama invited us? Do you think we’ll get to see Subaru again?”

“Yes! I really hope so! And I can’t wait to see Emilia again; she was so much fun to be
around.” Petra replied. After their rescue, the butler and the half-elf would sometimes play
with the kids, and Petra was eager to see Puck again, his fur was so soft and fluffy.

“But there is something I don’t understand,” Lucas chimed in. “Why do we have to wear
winter clothes? It’s so warm here!”

When they received the invitation to the mansion, the message was vague, only mentioning a
day of fun and the need for winter attire.

“Well, I’m sure they have a good reason…” Petra began, but her words trailed off as she
heard a gasp from the front, the whole group stopping in their tracks. She and the other



children rushed forward to see what was happening, and what they discovered was
astonishing.

A massive dark cloud loomed over the lord's mansion, softly showering it with delicate
snowflakes. The mansion and its surroundings were blanketed in snow, forming a circular
pattern, almost as if they were encased in a glass bottle.

What truly amazed them was the enormous wall-like structure in the front yard, complete
with towers at the corners, and a grand building behind it.

To their astonishment, everything was made of ice.

It was, in essence, an ice castle.

The villagers stood in awe, a mix of shock and wonder on their faces. The children, in
particular, were bubbling with excitement at the sight of such a magnificent spectacle.

Petra exclaimed, her eyes sparkling with wonder, “Wow! It’s sooooo beautiful!”

Lucas chimed in eagerly from the side, “I know, right? I can’t wait to go inside!”

The villagers made their way in, and as they stepped over the threshold where the snow
began, the warm air shifted to a chilly breeze.

In front of them stood a grand ice sign that read, “Do you wish to discover the marvels of
WindSpire Castle? If so, step right up to the gate!”

The villagers gathered at the enormous gate, crafted entirely from ice and adorned with
intricate designs.

“Wow! It’s even more amazing up close!”

“I want to see! I want to see! I can’t wait to see the inside!”

“I wonder if I could keep it! I want to be a princess,” the children exclaimed, their excitement
palpable. The adults shared in their enthusiasm, their initial confusion giving way to awe at
the spectacle.

Suddenly, a loud noise caught their attention, and they looked up to see none other than
Natsuki Subaru, the heroic butler who had saved the village’s children during that fateful
incident.

Dressed in his usual butler attire, he wore a regal cape and a crown, both were made of ice
and snow.

“Greetings, everyone! I’m thrilled you all made it here!” he called out. The children,
especially Petra, beamed at the sight of their hero.

He was just as cool as the stories they had heard—fearlessly diving into the forest, defeating
a pack of Wolgram in a single blow, and heroically bringing the children back home.



He seemed like a character straight out of their favorite tales.

And there was also the kind Half-Elf who had helped them, even if they were a bit wary of
her at first.

Now that Petra thought about it, they truly made a heroic pair.

“I'm sure you all have questions! Why is there a massive black cloud hovering above us?
Why is the entire mansion covered in snow? And why is there an ice castle?” he exclaimed.

"Well, due to some... unfortunate circumstances," he said, pausing to glance to the side for a
moment, "We found ourselves in this situation. So, we decided to make the best of it and
create this ice castle, inviting all of you to come and enjoy it!"

This announcement thrilled the villagers even more; they were used to seeing plain wooden
cottages, so the sight of such an extraordinary and seemingly impossible structure was
exhilarating.

"That's right! For the entire day, you can experience this magnificent castle and all its
splendor, so please, sit back, relax, and have a great time!" he shouted like a sports
announcer, and the crowd erupted in cheers.

"Okay, you can open the gate now," he instructed, and the gates began to transform slowly,
surrounded by swirling wisps of blue and white, reshaping themselves to allow entry.

Inside, they were greeted by a breathtaking sight. The yard was vast and covered in snow,
featuring cobblestone-like ice paths, ice bridges, and a garden filled with ice plants. There
was also a fenced open area with ice boots that had Ice-like blades on the bottom.

The children were particularly drawn to a series of tube-like tunnels that twisted and turned
before opening at the bottom.

Additionally, there was a bunch of open ice-like fences with two seats connected by an ice
chain at the top.

They had no idea what those were, but their childish instincts urged them to go there and play
until they were exhausted.

"Before you all head off," Subaru called out, grabbing their attention once again, "The castle's
interior is open for everyone to explore, and it’s beautifully decorated just for you!"

"And I have two more things to share," he said, raising two fingers. "There are about ten
coins hidden around the place, and the first person to find one will win a special prize from
me! And remember," he puffed out his chest, "be sure to show your appreciation to your king
for this wonderful day!"

The villagers, filled with excitement, exchanged glances before shouting together, 

”””Thank you so much, King Subaru!”””








---------------------------------

 

Puck floated beside Subaru and remarked, “I never thought of you as a speech-giver,
Subaru.”

Subaru straightened up, saying, “It’s ‘King Subaru’ now, and I do have a talent for public
speaking.” He observed the villagers milling about the castle—some heading straight inside,
children rushing to the slides he had set up, while others wandered into the frozen garden.

“Isn’t it beautiful?” Puck said, “I must admit, I’ve never pushed this far with fire magic
before. You always find ways to amaze me!”

This was indeed Subaru’s idea. Since Puck still had some excess mana he needed to expel,
Subaru thought it best to channel it into something creative, leading to the idea of
constructing an ice castle.

“Of course, you’ve caused us quite the trouble these past few days, so consider this your

“Come onnnn, I said I was sorry, okay?” Puck protested.

This entire endeavor served two purposes: to help Puck expend his excess mana and to check

“Let’s head down and see how everyone is doing,” Subaru suggested, leaping down

Behind a counter, there was a makeshift bar where the oni-maids, Ram and Rem, were

Rem lit up with a smile as Subaru approached, “Subaru-ku—”

Subaru cleared his throat loudly, prompting Rem to quickly correct herself, “King Subaru-

He nodded in satisfaction, “That’s right! Make sure to address me properly; it’s all about

Since he came up with the idea, Subaru had insisted that everyone refer to him as “King
Subaru,”

He glanced at Ram, who scoffed and looked away, “Hmph, trash Barasu has no dignity if he
has to ask others to indulge his fantasy.”

“Rammy, we call that ‘roleplaying.’ It has nothing to do with pride or anything like that,” he

“Hmph,” she replied, unimpressed.

“Well, keep serving the drinks, peasant. Grand vizier Puck, let’s go check on your daughter,”

Subaru then made his way to the ice-skating ring, where he spotted the person he was looking

He introduced the sport to the mansion yesterday, and it turned out to be a huge success,

Though she might never admit it, he could tell she was having fun working alongside them.

Seriously, the amount of tsunderes they have at the mansion is ridiculous.

Being linked to a monster that had devoured the world 400 years ago and facing such
isolation was incredibly unfair in his eyes.

“But then you showed up.” Her eyes sparkled as she looked at him. “You came, and
everything changed. Ram and Rem are nicer to me now, and the villagers don’t despise me

“So Subaru, thank you for coming into my life and making me sooooo happy.”

Her smile was bright, cheerful, and warm—just like the one she had when he first expressed
his desire to befriend her.

Subaru felt his cheeks heat up as well; a wave of warmth and nervousness washed over him.

Which had never happened to him before with anyone else, let alone a girl.

“Y-you're welcome… Emi.”

“Emi?”

“It’s just a nickname. Do you like it?”



“I do… Can I call you Soubie?”

“Absolutely not! That name is horrible!”

They burst into laughter once more, returning to their stargazing, where silence spoke louder
than words.

From that day on, a thought would enter Subaru’s mind whenever they were together.

‘Being this close and genuine with Emilia… I love it.’

Chapter 17: Arc 3 - The Capital’s Emissary
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Two weeks have gone by since Subaru dubbed the previous mansion-freezing event as the
“Puck's Mating Incident,” much to the annoyance of the great spirits and the amusement of
everyone else.

Fortunately, during these two weeks, nothing particularly exciting or noteworthy occurred,
allowing Subaru to settle into a comforting routine.

He would rise with the dawn, complete some light chores around the mansion, prepare
breakfast alongside the twins, wake everyone up to serve the meal, and enjoy it once they
finished. Afterward, he’d return to chores, take a thirty-minute break for whatever he pleased,
prepare lunch, serve it, and eat afterward. followed by more chores, another thirty-minute
break, and then he’d prepare and serve dinner. Once dinner was done, he would eat and then
would have the rest of the evening free for activities like reading, stargazing, or watching
Emilia communicate with the minor spirits.

While some might find this routine dull, Subaru embraced it with open arms.

It was a far cry from the days spent hunting Cursed Spirits or dealing with smelly old men.

However, he did miss the fun times with his cousin, Satoru. Sometimes, he wished Satoru
were around so they could hang out and engage in some tomfoolery together.

Though Subaru felt lonely back home, he was grateful to have friends here: Rem, Ram,
Emilia, Puck, and Beatrice—who would certainly deny it with all her being.

Currently, he was in his personal room, shirtless, staring at his mirror with his sunglasses on
the drawer beside him.

"Ah, and who might this handsome, sexy gentleman be, hmm~" he mused, striking a pose
and admiring his physique.

He stood tall and lean, embodying the athletic build. Not overly bulky, but just muscular
enough to showcase a toned and agile form. And that six-pack? The crowning glory of his
physique.

However, beyond the ego boost Subaru was experiencing, there was another reason for his
actions, one tied to magic.

In just two weeks, Subaru's mana reserves had nearly tripled, and his gate was also expanding
and strengthening to keep pace. 

If his gate had once been the size of a baby bottle, it was now comparable to a coffee cup—a
remarkable improvement.



Naturally, Puck and Beatrice were astonished by his progress, even labeling him as someone
with an unnatural talent for magic, an anomaly, to be precise.

They weren't wrong; he had been considered an anomaly in his original world as well.

What they didn’t realize was that Subaru had been casting spells relentlessly, nearly emptying
his gate, with any fatigue or drowsiness easily remedied by his reverse cursed technique.

When it came to spells, he could confidently say he is considered an expert at "Shamak," to
the extent that he could manipulate its properties. For instance, he could reduce the spell's
radius in exchange for making it thicker and more potent. Plus, the cost of casting it had
significantly decreased for him.

Be that as it may, he was far from the Experienced Great Spirit of Yin

On that note, just yesterday, he had learned a new spell called "El Shamak," a more
powerful version of Shamak. Instead of a fog-like black cloud that caused sensory disruption,
this spell made it harder for the target to control their own body.

He’s been having a blast learning magic, and unlike back home, he can take his time with it,
practicing whenever and wherever he likes. There are no pressures or expectations hanging
over him.

Unfortunately, he couldn’t cast his new spell without a target, and he was hesitant to
experiment on any of his friends or spirits, even when Rem offered to be the test subject,
reassuringly saying, “Subaru-Kun shouldn’t worry! Rem has faced tougher challenges and
can handle it!”

Still, he was terrified of Ram’s potential reaction when she eventually found out, so he
decided against it.

Before the magic lesson wrapped up, Puck-sensei mentioned something called the “Flow
Method,” which allows one to enhance their physical abilities and strength by utilizing Mana.
It was, essentially, a version of Cursed Energy Reinforcement.

‘Puck said that it requires a lot of training and patience to master, and since he’s a spirit, he
doesn’t know how to do it,’ he mused, a smirk creeping onto his face, ‘but, that’s why I have
the six eyes for this,’ he thought, feeling grateful for such a cheat ability.

He got to work, using his Six Eyes to scan his body, focusing intently on his gate as he
gradually opened it. This time, he managed to control the mana without it bursting out like a
geyser, all thanks to his training.

Instead of casting a spell, Subaru did what he usually did with his cursed energy: he made it
flow throughout his body.

With careful precision, Subaru guided the mana as it moved through him. He observed
intently with his Six Eyes as the mana gradually filled his body, enveloping him from head to
toe.



He could already sense the effects; he felt invigorated and stronger, much like when he used
cursed energy, and he noticed that his mana was slowly depleting as he maintained the flow.

‘So it’s just like cursed energy; I need to keep a steady flow to reinforce my body,’ he
thought.

And Just like cursed energy, the more mana he added, the stronger he became, and that’s
exactly what he did. He ramped up the mana flow, which in turn enhanced his body even
further, albeit at the expense of more mana consumption.

In a brief moment, he had already used up about a quarter of his mana, due to his relatively
limited reserves.

But just as he was about to halt the flow, a thought struck him—one he had after his initial
lesson with Puck-sensei.

Could he merge both Cursed Energy and Mana?

‘Let’s find out, shall we?’ he thought with a smirk, reaching for the longer, more familiar
rope that was his cursed energy.

As the cursed energy began to flow, something… Interesting happened.

The black hue of the mana and the blue shade of his cursed energy intertwined in the center
and… fused together.

It resembled the act of weaving two different colored threads, intertwining and blending, with
the colors bleeding into one another.

The result was a dark blue that spread like wildfire throughout his body, enveloping him in a
small yet noticeable dark blue aura.

“Wow,” he murmured, completely astonished by this turn of events. Subaru felt… different.
Lighter, quicker, stronger—similar to the sensation he experienced when he pushed his
cursed energy reinforcement to its limits.

He quickly assessed this new energy—no, it wasn’t entirely new. Subaru was so familiar with
cursed energy that he could recognize it in an instant. The fundamentals of this magic was
rooted in Cursed Energy, he was certain.

This wasn’t a new form of magic; it was cursed energy, but transformed.

All of this analysis and observation took place in the blink of an eye, thanks to the Six Eyes.

Then, in an instant, it erupted. The aura surged wildly around him, almost like adding oxygen
to a flame.

And with it came excruciating pain.



Subaru let out a pained grunt, trying to hold it in. He collapsed to the ground, twitching and
writhing as his muscles spasmed.

Subaru quickly paused the flow of mana and cursed energy, and just like that, the new cursed
energy ceased, taking the pain with it shortly after.

He laid on the ground, breathing heavily as he tried to regain his bearing. ‘What the hell was
that…? It just went haywire so fast…’

Everything had happened in an instant; one moment he was analyzing it, and the next, he was
overwhelmed by pain.

Rising to his feet, he continued to use Reverse Cursed Energy to ease his sore muscles. To be
honest, this was the most intense pain he had ever experienced, which was saying a lot given
his previous line of work.

‘I need to do more experiments to understand what went wrong,’ he thought.

He still had nearly half of his mana left, and his cursed energy reserves were holding up well.

Just as he was about to try again, a knock on his door interrupted him.

“Subaru-kun, are you awake?” Rem's voice called from outside.

“Remmy? Yeah, I’m awake. What’s going on?” he replied.

“Guests have just arrived, and as the butler, you need to come down and greet them.” Rem
stated, her tone quite formal.

‘If Rem is speaking like that, this must be important,’ he thought.

“Alright, I’ll be right there. Just let me get dressed,” he said, heading over to put on his butler
attire.

'Cursed Mana… I’ll call it that. I’ll research more into Cursed Mana later.’

With that, he got dressed and followed Rem out of his room.

“I guess this is it,” Emilia’s voice chimed like a silver bell.

“Yeah, it looks like quite the crowd is here,” he replied, scanning the room.

“Well, Subaru-kun, you can stand over there,” Roswaal indicated towards the knights.
“Emilia-sama, please proceed to the front; the conference is about to start.”

“Understood,” she replied, glancing at Subaru, who offered her an encouraging nod. No
words were necessary as they took their positions—Subaru standing awkwardly among the
knights, while Emilia joined two other women at the front.

He concentrated on the woman dressed in military outfit. Her dark green hair cascaded to the
middle of her back, tied neatly with a white ribbon. A sword hung at her hip, complementing
her dark purplish-blue outfit. She exuded confidence and had impressive mana reserves, with
wind as her magical affinity. Additionally, she possessed the Divine Protection of Wind
Reading, granting her the ability to perceive invincible truths, read people's emotions, and
detect falsehoods.

‘Wow, a walking lie detector—that’s pretty neat!’

Next, his gaze shifted to the shorter woman beside her. She wore a flowing white dress and a
fluffy hat perched atop her long purple hair, which reached her hips. While she had the yang
magic attribute, what truly caught his attention was her gate. It was in a constant state of
expansion and contraction, reminiscent of breathing.

He quickly deduced that she had a defective gate, as Beatrice had once explained to him.
From what he could see, her condition meant her gate struggled to replenish mana from the
air, potentially leading to mana deficiency.

Having experienced something similar briefly, he knew firsthand how troublesome that could
be.

Then something else piqued his interest: the woman wore a scarf draped over her shoulders
that looked like a white rug-fox. While others might overlook it as just an accessory, Subaru
saw something interesting about it.

An Od.

The scarf was a spirit, and its Od resembled that of Beatrice and Puck, yet fundamentally
different from the minor or the quasi-spirits he sensed from Julius.

‘Hmm, those three share similar Ods, which is different from the other spirits I have seen
before.’



Interestingly, this spirit didn’t seem particularly powerful, as she lacked the abundant mana of
Beatrice or Puck. Moreover, he sensed no contract between the two. Which shed light on
what type of relation those two share.

“What a pleasent surprise! To see you here of all places, Subaru-san.” A youthful voice rang
out, pulling Subaru from his thoughts and drawing his attention to the front.

It was none other than Reinhard Van Astrea, the legendary Sword Saint.

‘Eh? He was here the whole time? This guy keeps appearing out of nowhere! Is he some kind
of shinobi or what?’ he though, Before focusing on Reinhard

He quickly flashed a grin, “Hey, Reinhard! How’s it going, my friend?” he asked.

“I’m doing quite well, thank you. It’s truly a pleasure to see you again, Subaru-san,”
Reinhard replied.

Subaru shook his head as he spoke, “Reinhard, buddy, what with the ‘san’? Just call me
Subaru. We’re friends, so no need to call each other with honorifics.”

Reinhard’s eyes slightly widened for a moment before he smiled gently. “O-of course… In
that case, I’ll call you Subaru, as you prefer.”

Subaru nodded, returning the smile, “That’s the spirit, buddy! There is no such thing as
formalities among friends,” he added.

“I suppose you’re right. I noticed you came with Emilia-sama. Honestly, I had a hunch you’d
be here once I learned she was coming,” Reinhard said.

“Well, I wouldn’t be here if Emilia hadn’t invited me; I’d probably still be at the Mathers’
estate cleaning the basement or something,” Subaru replied.

Then he adopted a slightly serious expression, “say, Reinhard, I’ll be frank with you—Felt is
the fifth candidate, right?” he whispered, lowering his voice.

Reinhard visibly flinched, his eyes widening in surprise. “H-how did you—”

“When she was handing over the insignia, I noticed it glowed for a moment. Plus, Emilia
explained to me how a candidate is chosen for the throne. So, I just put two and two
together,” he concluded with a smug grin.

Reinhard kept opening and closing his mouth like a fish out of water, clearly at a loss for
words, before he sighed and smiled in acceptance.

“I see that there’s no need to keep it a secret then. Yes, Felt-sama is indeed the fifth
candidate. Should I assume you think this meeting is to officially start off the race?” Subaru
nodded in agreement with Reinhard’s statement.

“Honestly, you’re quite something, Subaru.”



“Tell me about it.” he chuckled

While they were chatting, Subaru glanced at Reinhard, relieved that the mana levels were
much lower than before, so he wasn’t blinded like he had been earlier.

His gate was defective, similar to the purple-haired girl’s, but in his case, it was sealed tight,
only allowing mana to flow in rather than out. As for his Od, it was cluttered with divine
protections that made Subaru want to pull his hair out.

‘Who needs this many divine protections anyway?! There are like, three hundred of them!’ he
exclaimed as he looked at some of them.

At that moment, the fourth candidate entered the throne room, and it was none other than the
arrogant girl he had met the day before: Priscilla Barielle.

Along with her came three more familiar faces: Felix, Julius, and Al.

“Hiya! Subaru-kyun!” Felix greeted, flashing a peace sign.

“Oh, it’s just you, cat-ears,” Subaru replied, sounding unenthusiastic due to having been
tricked by him earlier—and the whole sniffing incident.

“Cat-ears?” Felix repeated, his ears perked up. “Ahh, was Subawu-kyun charmed by Ferris-
chan? It’s only natural, fufufufu~” He covered his mouth and giggled.

“Ah, so you fell for Felix's deception too. If it helps, Subaru, you’re not the only one,”
Reinhard tried to comfort Subaru, which only made it worse.

“I have no idea what you’re talking about; it’s just a fitting nickname for the cat,” he quickly
retorted, much to Felix’s delight.

“Fufufu~ Ferris-chan won’t mind being called that if it’s coming from Subaru-kyun.”

Subaru quickly then turned to his isekai brother, who looked even more out of place than he
did.

“Hey Al, great to see you, buddy. Are you a knight or something?”

“Me? A knight? Nah, that’s a bit too grand for a middle-aged guy like me. I’m just someone
the princess picked up, that’s all,” he replied with a casual shrug.

“Really? You don’t seem like ‘just a guy’ to me,” Subaru commented.

Al simply shrugged again.

Subaru then examined Al again, this time noticing something strange.

There was something dark, almost tar-like, clinging to his Od as if it were stuck there.



It felt wrong, deeply wrong. Like something that contradicted everything. Something that
shouldn’t be there.

Something vile, something repulsive, something that—

‘W-why can’t I see it?!’ Subaru froze, completely shocked as he was met with something
impossible.

His Six Eyes… had failed to understand what he was seeing.

No, it felt like they couldn’t comprehend it.

'This… T-this is impossible!' His six eyes, the "Eyes of the All-Seeing God," allowed him to
understand all phenomena down to their mechanics, like having the internet and all it's
knowledge in your head.

So for it fail when it clearly worked in this world was...

Terrifying.

“Hey man, you’re kinda staring. Is everything okay?” Al’s question snapped him out of his
daze, and he realized Al and some knights were watching him.

“A-ah, sorry Al, I’m just not feeling well today,” he said, adjusting his sunglasses.

“It’s cool, but please don’t do that again; it freaks me out,” Al replied, and Subaru nodded
stiffly before looking ahead again.

He hadn’t had any reason to dislike Al, as he had been polite and was the only person he
knew in a similar situation as him. But with this new revelation, he chose to be cautious
around him from now on.

He caught a loud cough coming from Marcos. “If I could have your attention, I’m Marcos,
the leader of the imperial Knights, and I’ll be directing today’s proceedings.”

“It all started about six months ago when King Randohal Lugunica passed away, along with
his entire lineage, leaving the throne—”

“Now, hold ‘n a minute, will ya’?” A gentle female voice interrupted; it was the lady with the
spirit.

“I understand you want to put ‘n good show ‘ere, but as we say in Kararagi, 'Time is money',”
she said, catching Subaru off guard.

‘She’s speaking in the Kansai Dialect here?! No way!’ he thought, utterly astonished.
Regaining his composure, he realized, ‘No… Al was isekai’d here, so it makes sense that
someone else brought it along.’

“I agree,” 



Marcos turned to the speaker, “Crusch-sama, is it appropriate for the head of House Karsten
to say such a thing?” 

“While formalities are important, I believe it’s imperative that we need to get to the point
quickly and understand why we are gathered here,” she replied. Then, with a slight smirk, she
said, “Naturally, I have a general idea.”

“Oh, so you’re already aware of the purpose of this meeting?” asked one of the council
members, an elderly man with a long beard.

“Yes, Miklotov-sama. It’s for a drinking party, right?”

Subaru had to suppress a facepalm.

"We'll be facing each other as rivals, but by sitting together and drinking, we'll get to know
one another better," she said with an understanding look on her face.

Marcos looked at her blankly, “No, that’s not it.”

‘Pfft-‘ he stifled a laugh at her. ‘How embarrassing~’

She quickly turned to the crowd, and Subaru followed her gaze to a certain mischievous cat.

“Felix. That’s not what you told me,” she said, looking a bit flustered.

“Awww, come on. Ferris-chan said ‘Maybe it’ll be a drinking party,’” he replied, his
demeanor very cat-like.

“I see,” she said, turning back to the front. “Then, with a bit of embarrassment, I retract
everything I just said.”

Subaru poked the cat demi-human to catch his attention. "You just made your lady embarrass
herself, What do you have to say for yourself, Cat-ears?" he asked.

The cat's reply? Blew the raspberry at him.

From this day onwards, Subaru prefered dogs over cats.

The purple haired lady however, “Hey now, just ‘cause Karsten backed down don’ mean that
I will. There is no need t’ explain the royal selection. We already know, right?”

She looked at Priscilla and Emilia, Emilia who went to answer. “Well, I think we should
listen—“

“Sorry, I wasn’t askin’ for yer opinion.” The purple-haired lady rudely cut her off.

Subaru was thin-lipped at this, clearly miffed at the rudeness. But then quickly smiled.

“Hey, dude, I don’t know a whole lot about the Royal Selection, So i’d like to hear the rest,”
Subaru decided to speak up, attracting everyone’s attention to him, including Marcos and the



sage council.

Marcos looked at him then Emilia. “Emilia-sama, I was told that this man is a butler under
your sponsor’s employment, have you not explained the royal selection to him?”

Emilia looked surprised at being the center of attention, but quickly stammered out and
replied, “um-Well, I did tell him, but I think you should still explain it to everyone else.”

Priscilla, in the meantime, seemed to be fed up with all this nonsense as she loudly said,
“Mineself has gotten tired of this rambling, just explain how I will win the throne, Marcos.”

Marcos looked at emilia and priscilla, then sighed. “Very well then,”

Subaru wished he could be at the front, sensing the lady’s irritation with how things were
unfolding.

Unbeknownst to him, Julius looked at the butler with a mysterious expression before looking
away.

“The reason we have gathered those qualified to be dragon priestesses is due to a prophecy
inscribed on the dragon tablet. It reads, ‘From the five chosen to lead the nation, select one
dragon priestess to form a covenant with the dragon.’”

“Five huh? I guess this is where you come in, Reinhard.” Subaru remarked to the red-haired
knight, who simply nodded in agreement.

"Indeed. Up until now, there have only been four candidates for the throne, and the royal
selection hasn't officially started yet. But today, history is going to be made" Reinhard
replied.

"Knight Reinhard Van Astrea, please step forward," the leader of the knights instructed.
Reinhard complied, kneeling on one knee and placing a hand over his heart.

"Esteemed members of the sage council, I am proud to announce that my mission has been
successfully completed." He rose to his feet.

"The fifth dragon priestess and the final candidate for the throne has been found."

As the gates swung open, three figures entered. Two of them were girls with pink hair, clearly
twins at first glance. The most significant among them was a golden-haired girl with striking
red eyes, elegantly dressed in a yellow gown that stood in stark contrast to her previously
worn ragged attire.

"Her name is… Felt-sama!"

‘Wow… Talk about one-eighty. You wouldn't guess she came from the slums if you saw her
now,’ he thought as the girl stepped forward, halting right in front of Reinhard.

"Reinhard," she said, and the knight returned her smile. What he failed to notice was the girl's
expression, which was anything but friendly.



In fact, she wore a nasty sneer.

With a swift motion, she lifted the hem of her dress and delivered a high kick aimed at the
knight's head, which he blocked effortlessly.

"I've had enough of you! You've been a pain in the ass for an entire month, and now you
make me wear this?!" she shouted at him.

"This is surprising. Was the dress not to your taste? I can get you another one if you prefer,"
Reinhard replied, gently lowering her foot. Subaru found himself torn between thinking his
obliviousness was endearing or just plain sad.

"No! That's not it! You completely missed the point!"

Emilia slightly gasped at the sight of Felt again. "Felt… it's that girl from before…" she said,
trailing off as she glanced at Subaru, who sheepishly looked away.

She huffed slightly at him. He knew and didn’t tell her! How dare he!

Subaru shifted his focus back to Felt, saying, “Wow, Felt. Even in an important event, you’re
still as feisty as ever.” She turned to him, her eyes wide in recognition.

“Wait, it’s you! What the hell are you doing here?!” she exclaimed.

He waved at her cheerfully, “Heya! It’s been a while. I must say, you look pretty in that dress
—”

Felt demonstrated why she can solo the JJK verse as she casually bypassed his Infinity and
kicked him in the face, which he blocked as well.

"Not you too! Stop blocking my kicks!" 

“Ahem,” a man cleared his throat; it was Marcos. “Felt-sama, if you’re done rekindling old
friendships, please step forward,” he instructed, and she huffed but complied.

“Fine, I’m here. Let’s just get this over with,” she replied.

“Felt-sama, I would suggest you act more lady-like, but this takes precedence.” Reinhard
handed her an insignia, similar to Emilia’s, which began to glow.

“The dragon stone has acknowledged Felt-sama as a dragon priestess and, as a result, a
candidate for the throne. I believe that the Royal Selection can begin in earnest,” Reinhard
announced, bowing slightly, followed by Marcus and the knights.

‘Finally, we can get this show on the road,’ he thought, eager for the selection to begin
without interruptions—

“I don’t agree with this,” a noble interjected. “Even if she was chosen by the dragon, her
looks and behavior are unbefitting for a ruler,” he stated.



Marcus was about to respond, but Felt jumped in first, “What, ya got a problem with me?
Suck it! I couldn’t care less what you think!” she shot back, clearly irked by the noble’s
disrespect.

“Listen here, you—”

Felt ignored his rant and turned to the council. “Hey, you old geezers, I don’t want to stick
around longer than necessary, so let’s wrap this up,” she said, causing annoyance among the
council members.

Subaru blinked at her, then smiled, thinking, ‘I really like her!’

“But Felt-sama—”

“I’m not hearing it! Just get on with it!” 

Miklotov let out a sigh, “Alright then, shall we get started? Candidates, please step forward.”

One by one, the candidates and their attendants moved ahead. Priscilla was accompanied by
her jester, Al; Crusch Karsten stood with her knight, Felix; the purple-haired rude lady was
with her knight, Julius; Emilia was alongside her sponsor, Roswaal; and finally, there was
Felt with Reinhard in tow.

“First up, we have Priscilla Barielle-sama and her attendant, Al.”

Priscilla dramatically pulled a fan from… her breasts?! and held it up to her face; Subaru
could already sense that she found the situation quite amusing.

“The royal selection is utterly pointless; I am the only one truly fit to lead this nation!” she
declared, and Subaru could hear the gasps of shock and outrage ripple through the crowd.

Subaru’s shoulders sagged at this, thinking, ‘What was I even expecting from her at this
point?’

“You all need to prostrate yourselves and serve me! I will guide this nation to greatness!”

‘…Sure, Priscilla, whatever you say,’ he sighed as the next candidate was introduced.

“Next is Crusch Karsten-sama, duchess and head of House Karsten, accompanied by her
attendant, knight Felix Argyle.”

The duchess stood tall with her hands clasped behind her, her unwavering honey-colored eyes
scanning the audience.

“I want to make one thing clear,” she stated firmly. “If I become the new ruler, the status quo
will be broken; I will break the covenant with the dragon.”

Subaru had to cover his ears against the uproar that followed; if Priscilla’s announcement was
like kicking a puppy, Crusch’s was akin to dropping a nuke.



The shouts of anger and disbelief continued, yet she stood resolute, earning Subaru’s respect
for her composure.

“Isn’t it shameful that our existence relies solely on the protection of the divine dragon?
Shouldn’t we, as a people, take charge of our own safety and ensure our freedom?” she
challenged.

“I will ensure that the dragon understands that the kingdom of Lugunica belongs to its
people. Our liberty and prosperity are in our own hands, not his.”

As she wrapped up her speech, Subaru was left scratching his head in confusion.

‘Well, I can kinda see her point. A country shouldn't rely solely on one being for its survival.
But from what I understand, the dragon is quite powerful; she shouldn't just cut ties with him
if she wants independence. Perhaps a more hands-off approach could be beneficial? Like
having a trump card, maybe?' He pondered this as the next candidate took the stage.

“Anastasia Hoshin-sama of the Hoshin Trading Company, accompanied by her attendant,
Knight Julius Juukulius.”

Anastasia looked around at everyone and started with, “I’m going to be blunt here, I’m a
greedy gal, so I want everything.”

“…Huh?” Subaru blurted out, and the rest of the audience was equally stunned.

“No amount of commercial success or material wealth is ever enough, so with this
opportunity before me, I’ve decided that I want an entire nation!” she proclaimed boldly.
Subaru stared at her in disbelief.

“Of course, just like all my possessions. I take good care of them, so if I win, I’ll make sure
to look after all of you!”

'…Great.' Now this country might end up turning into a corporate dystopia in a medieval
setting. Just fantastic.' he thought. Were those serisouly the type of people chosen by the
dragon?

'At least she's honest, I'll give her that,'

“Next up, Felt-sama and her attendant, knight Reinhard Van Astrea,”

Felt glanced around the room, clearly irritated by everything, before she spoke up. "I was
dragged into this stupid race for a stupid throne I never wanted," she began, "Then it hit me;
since I'm stuck in this shithole, I might as well make the most of it! So, once I become king,
I'm going to tear everything down!"

The reaction from Crusch was intense, but it was nothing compared to the uproar that
followed, as the entire room erupted in anger.

'Wow, Felt! You sure don't hold back, do you?' He was torn between being horrified or
impressed by her fearless attitude.



Undeterred by the chaos, she pressed on, "That's right! I hate this entire kingdom! It's all
corrupt and rotten! I'll tear it down and create a system that actually cares for the people! A
one that doesn't fill the pockets of rotton people like you!"

Subaru actually chuckled at this, which went unheard of by the outrage around him.“An
anarchist, a fucking anarchist. Felt, should I be proud or scared of you?” He could see the fire
in her eyes as she said that; she wasn’t joking.

“Sword saint!” one of the nobles shouted at the redhead. “Did you not hear what she just
said?! How can you let someone like her disrespect us like this?!”

Reinhard turned to the noble with a smile. “While Felt-sama’s words may be a bit
scandalous, I truly believe she has the nation’s best interests at heart, which is why I’ve
sworn to be her knight.”

“And I’ll make sure to work you to the death, so don’t forget that,” she retorted with a huff.

This declaration stunned everyone, including Subaru, but seeing Reinhard’s genuine
happiness, he simply shrugged it off.

After everything quieted down, they continued.

“And last, Emilia-sama alongside her sponsor, the court mage Roswaal L. Mathers.”

"Oh myyyyy, I feel terribly out of place after those knights," Roswaal remarked, standing
alongside Emilia on the stage.

Emilia then proceeded to survey the crowd, she noticed many dismissive and annoyed
glances, making her feel anxious and uneasy.

But then her gaze landed on Subaru, who gave her an encouraging thumbs up. She
remembered his reassuring words: ‘I can do this, there’s nothing to fear.’

‘I've said it many times, but I don’t think it will ever be enough—thank you, Subaru.’

With renewed determination, reminiscent of her resolve in the village, she spoke up,
“Greetings, everyone. I am Emilia, and I have  one wish: for everyone to be treated equally.” 

The crowd fell silent, genuinely listening to her, while Subaru nodded in approval.

“This nation has suffered from racial strife and prejudice, a deep-seated issue that has
lingered for far too long. It reached a boiling point fifty years ago when our kingdom was
engulfed in civil war,” she continued, her voice steady and authoritative.

“Though the kingdom emerged victorious, it came at a terrible price. Families were shattered,
children were left orphaned, and countless lives were lost. I want to change this; I want to
build a kingdom where every citizen, regardless of their background, is treated with equality.
That is my goal.” She bowed slightly to her audience.



Subaru felt an overwhelming sense of pride, like a father watching his daughter take her first
steps. He had already recognized Emilia's potential to be a great leader; she just needed
guidance and support.

That’s why he dedicated his free time to assist her with her studies, teaching her about things
beyond the pages of books.

There was still a long journey ahead, and there were many aspects she was naive about, but
these were significant first steps.

‘Well done, Emilia! You nailed that speech! I’m so proud of you,’ he thought with a smile.
His chest swelled with pride and something else.

Now, people should look over her heritage and take her more seriously—

A laugh rang out through the hall, a derisive sound coming from the same noble who had
attempted to blast felt.

“Ahaha! What’s this? The half-devil is talking about equality? The very same half-devil who
resembles the witch that almost brought ruin to the world over four hundred years ago?!” he
sneered, which only fueled the others to chime in.

“That’s right, who does she think she is?”

“As if she knows anything about this kingdom!”

“I’d rather lose my lands than be equal to some mutt!”

The nobles and mages mocked her, dismissing her efforts, and even some knights joined in
the ridicule.

Emilia just looked crestfallen at this; her resolve and determination evaporated into thin air as
she was once again mocked and hated for something she had no control over.

“This whole royal selection is a farce! First, we have a brat who wants to tear our kingdom
apart, and now a half-devil shows up?! It’s a farce!”

“It’s not nice to call a half-elf a ‘half-devil,’” Roswaal interjected, but his words fell on deaf
ears.

“I’ve kept quiet about this from the start, but it needs to be said,” one of the councilmen, a
bald man with bushy blue eyebrows, declared.

"The Astrea gives us a rebellious brat we're supposed to accept as our king, and then the
margrave supports someone who is the spitting image of the witch of envy!" he spat.

“Does anyone not see how dreadful her participation is?! She should be thrown out of here so
her filth doesn’t tarnish—”

His words faltered, caught in his throat, as he found himself unable to continue.



In fact, everyone else in the throne room—the nobles, mages, knights—who had been
mocking her now fell silent, all feeling the same oppressive weight.

It was as if they were submerged underwater, struggling to breathe or move.

Even Reinhard felt a chill run down his spine.

From the knights, a figure stepped forward, his footsteps echoing in the now silent throne
room.

With his tense posture, trembling arms, clenched fists, and gritted teeth, even if his eyes were
covered, it was clear that he was furious.

Natsuki Subaru was livid.

Chapter 20: Arc 3 - The Wrath Of God
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Natsuki Subaru stood resolutely at the forefront of the throne room, every gaze fixed upon
him, yet silence reigned supreme. The pressure in the air was so thick that no one dared to
move, as if frozen in place.

Crusch and Anastasia observed Subaru with cautious eyes. While they were mostly
unaffected by the oppressive atmosphere, as it wasn't directed at them, their instincts
screamed at them to be wary of him.

Priscilla, on the other hand, seemed entirely unfazed by the unfolding drama. A grin spread
across her face as she watched the commoner who had piqued her interest approach. 'Come
on, entertain me, show me what you will do'.

Felt, much like Priscilla, was eager for what was to come. She had been in a foul mood,
forced into this selection, forced into the ridiculous dress, forced to endure the arrogance of
nobles. But now, with Subaru stepping up, perhaps she wouldn't need to intervene at all.

Roswaal simply watched, his knowing smirk never faltering. Everything seemed to be going
well...

Emilia, snapped from her daze by the abrupt hush in the room, saw Subaru standing at the
front. She could sense his anger directed at everyone, but what truly alarmed her was the fear
radiating from the crowd. She had witnessed his power firsthand. She understood just how
formidable he was—powerful enough to...

Her eyes widened in alarm. "Wait, Subaru, don't—!"

Suddenly, as if a switch had been flipped, the tension vanished. Subaru's anger dissipated,
replaced by a smile that lit up his face. He surveyed the crowd and the sage council
surrounding him.

"You all must be some of the biggest imbeciles I've ever had the displeasure of meeting.
Disrespecting royal candidates like that... one of them could very well become your ruler
someday, you know?" He hurled his words at them without hesitation.

The nobles, council members, and knights were left gasping. The overwhelming pressure
they felt was enough to weaken their knees; some even collapsed from sheer fright.

'Pathetic'. Subaru thought. All he had done was release a fraction of his cursed energy, and
this was the result? Even the knights?

'Those people wouldn't last a minute as Jujutsu sorcerers'.



"Wait, Subaru! Please don't do anything rash!" Emilia pleaded, trying to pull him back before
things escalated.

"Emilia..." Subaru glanced at her, irritation flashing briefly across his face. Did she truly
believe he would harm anyone? Or perhaps she feared what he might become?

"Emilia, I won't hurt anyone. But what needs to be said—must be said," he assured her.
Despite the pain reflected in her beautiful amethyst eyes, he couldn't back down.

Not when his friend was being disrespected like this.

Roswaal stepped forward, fixing his gaze on Subaru. "Natsuki Subaru, this is a formal
gathering hosted by esteemed members of this kingdom. Disrespecting them can lead to
severe consequences, including execution," Roswaal stated evenly, prompting Subaru to turn
his full attention to him.

"However, I will allow you to leave unharmed if you grovel and apologize to everyone."

Subaru glared at Roswaal, his anger now focused solely on the court mage. 'Me, getting
executed? Forget that shit! Emilia was just humiliated—why aren't you saying something
about that?!'.

"Roswaal," he began, his voice sharp, "Are you sure you want to do this?"

"I will not say it again. Will you kneel and apologize?"

"Roswaal, you know me better than most. What do you think I'll choose?"

A pause. Then:

"...Very well then,"

Roswaal's incantation began, his arm rising as a gigantic fireball formed overhead.

"Al Goa!"

The fiery orb hurtled toward Subaru with intense heat, ready to evaporate him on the spot.

"No!" Emilia cried out, watching the flames rush toward him. Why wasn't he moving? He
was going to get hurt!

Just before impact, the fireball was nullified—extinguished by a blast of ice, neutralizing it in
an instant. Subaru turned to see who had intervened.

'Ah, so that was your plan, Roswaal?'. Subaru's anger morphed into something closer to
annoyance. Was Roswaal baiting him just to force Puck out? Why?

'Whatever. I can think about it later'. He thought, shaking his head.

"Thanks for the assist, Puck." Subaru nodded at the hovering Great Spirit.



"Anytime!" Puck replied cheerfully, but his expression darkened as he turned his gaze toward
the nobles and knights.

"I've heard what you all said about my daughter, and let me make one thing clear: I. Am. Not.
Happy."

With each word, the temperature dropped, causing everyone to shiver.

"The disrespect and audacity shown toward my beloved daughter is unforgivable. The only
reason I haven't turned you all into ice statues is because of Lia, so keep that in mind." He
shot a fierce glare at the crowd.

"T-this is... Your spirit... is The Beast of the End!" one of the council members finally
managed to stammer.

"Oho? So you're aware of me? Good. It seems you're somewhat educated, human." Puck's
smile was laced with malice.

"Whenever you think about hurting my dear Lia, remember who you will be dealing with.
And I will end you without hesitation."

"Puck..." Emilia whispered her father's name, unsure of how to respond.

"Hey, Puck, let me take care of this. Alright?" Subaru interjected, offering the spirit a
reassuring gesture. Puck studied Subaru for a moment before relenting.

"Fine. I'll leave this to you."

In an instant, the spirit transformed into mana, which was absorbed into her necklace.

"Now then," Subaru scanned the crowd, his focus locking onto the nobles. "Are you going to
apologize?"

His question snapped some out of their daze—especially the one who had initiated the attack.

"You dare speak to me like that?! Who do you think you are, demanding an apology from a
noble such as myself when you're nothing but a lowly peasant?! I could have you executed
right here and now!" he bellowed.

"Knights!" he commanded, gesturing toward them. "Take this disrespectful fool's head!"

The knights exchanged glances, uncertain.

Before they could act, laughter shattered the tense atmosphere.

Subaru was laughing heartily, as if he had just heard the most hilarious joke ever told. This
only served to infuriate the noble further.

"What's so funny?! Are you mocking me?! Do you find my words amusing?!" he shouted.



"Absolutely," Subaru replied, his laughter fading into a sly smile—a smile that carried the
same cold precision a predator would have before delivering the final blow.

"You ordered my execution over disrespect, yet you've committed an even graver sin."

"Really?" the noble scoffed mockingly. "And pray tell, what sin have I committed that is
worse than your lack of manners?"

"It's quite simple," Subaru explained smoothly. "You insulted Emilia by calling her a 'Half-
devil.' Do you not realize the crime you've committed?"

The noble scoffed. "I simply stated the truth."

Subaru's grin widened. "Oh, wow. You really scored zero in the intelligence department,
didn't you?"

The noble flushed with anger.

"Allow me to explain in simple terms, so even your brain can comprehend. The insignia
lights up when a potential ruler is found. The divine dragon himself chooses these candidates.
And yet you—a nobody—have mocked his judgment."

The noble recoiled, his face draining of color.

"By insulting Emilia, you have insulted the divine dragon itself."

Subaru leaned forward, his expression grave, his gaze locked onto the noble."

"So tell me, are you going to apologize?"

"Well–I–But–I mean," The man stuttered, struggling to find the right words. It was a
humiliating moment, with everyone watching him—the candidate, the councilmen, the
knights—waiting for him to respond.

"Of course, I'm not just talking about Emilia," Subaru began, then gestured to the banner of
the Kingdom of Lugunica above the throne, where the dragon was proudly displayed.

"Get on your knees, roll over the ground like a good puppy, and beg for forgiveness. Who
knows, the Lugunican church might be lenient with you."

He turned to the other nobles and knights. "This includes all of you. Don't think that just
because I'm focusing on one person means you're innocent. You've all committed the same
sin."

Subaru scanned each of them, daring someone to speak up, but they merely shuffled and
averted their gazes—just as he expected.

A loud bang echoed through the hall as a hand struck the table. One of the councilmen rose,
his aged face twisted with anger—it was the bald-headed one.



"I've had enough of this—"

Just like before, the words caught in his throat, strangled before they could escape. But this
time, it felt different.

Subaru faced the man, his expression unchanged, still smiling. But there was something new
—his right eye peeking over his sunglasses.

The overwhelming pressure from earlier surged back, and the war veteran councilman began
to experience a sensation he hadn't felt in ages: fear.

That piercing azure-blue eye bore down on him, unwavering, digging into his soul, judging
him for all his misdeeds and failures.

It was as if he was facing Od Lugunica itself.

"And you," Subaru started, emphasizing the last word. "Where do I even begin? One would
think a member of the sage council would set an example for everyone, someone wise
enough to guide this nation through tough times. But what do we have?" He scoffed.

"Some bumbling, senile fool who's lost his way, letting trivial biases and emotions cloud his
judgment." He spat. "If you can't do your job right, maybe it's time for you to step down. But
if you need more encouragement, then I might have to take matters into my own hands—"

"Subaru!"

A melodic voice, like silver bells, cut through the heavy atmosphere, snapping him back to
reality.

He stopped in his place, regaining his awareness.

He was halfway toward the trembling old man. He turned to see Reinhard poised to
intervene, then looked at her—at Emilia—at the disapproval, confusion, and something else
in her eyes.

He refused to acknowledge it. Because it stung deeply.

"Subaru, you've made your point. Please stop," she urged, her firm tone wavering slightly.

Subaru's smile faded, his lips pressed into a thin line. Silence lingered uncomfortably before
he finally spoke.

"Alright, I'll take my leave then."

He turned away and walked out of the throne room.

But as he approached the doors, he paused, his gaze shifting to his right—to the knights
watching him.



"You know, knights should embody chivalry and heroism, serving as role models who protect
the weak and uphold justice. Yet after witnessing this piss-poor excuse for an assembly, I can
confidently say that, with a few exceptions, you are nothing but a disgrace—arrogant
cowards masquerading as protectors, reveling in hollow titles while abandoning the very
principles you claim to uphold."

He let the words sink in, his eyes hidden behind his sunglasses roaming all of them.

"But what disgusted me the most is your hypocrisy: One of the royal candidates was insulted
and humiliated right in front of you, but instead of fulfilling your duty and protecting her
from the slander you all instead decided to join in on mockery. You dare to call yourselves
knights, yet not a single one of you possesses the integrity of the title you flaunt. Hypocrites
—that’s all you are, and that’s all you’ll ever be."

He spat those words and strode out of the throne room.

The insult lingered in the air as the knights glared at the now-closed golden gates, their anger
palpable. His words had struck a nerve, hitting precisely where it hurt the most.

Their pride.

Among them, a purple-haired knight fixated on the gates, his expression calm, his eyes
slightly narrowed—a skill he had honed over time.

Julius would have to take action.

"Ahem."

A man cleared his throat, drawing everyone's attention to the councilman, Miklotov
McMahon.

"Well, that was certainly... something," he began, his tone carefully measured. "You have
quite the intriguing attendant, Emilia-sama."

"..."

She did not respond. She simply remained silent.

The other candidates felt a wave of relief wash over them. Crusch let out a quiet sigh, grateful
that a confrontation hadn't erupted. Anastasia, on the other hand, was eager to move on,
already dismissing the entire ordeal as a waste of her time. Priscilla smiled in approval,
clearly pleased with how events had unfolded. Felt, meanwhile, was grinning ear to ear—
watching those stuck-up nobles get verbally torn apart was exactly the entertainment she'd
wanted.

"Now, typically, this would be the point where we conclude our meeting and officially
commence the royal selection... but an important development has arisen," Miklotov
continued, drawing the room's full attention.



"About a month ago, the Dragon Tablet revealed yet another prophecy," he announced. "The
message was rather brief and somewhat unclear. It simply read, 'The Sage has returned.'"

The knights, the candidates, the nobles—everyone momentarily froze, stunned by the
revelation.

"Pardon my interruption, Miklotov-sama," Reinhard said, bowing slightly. "But what does
this mean? Shouldn't Sage Shaula always reside in the Pleiades Tower?"

Sage Shaula was one of the three heroes who had defeated and sealed the Witch of Envy.
Legends claimed she lived in the tower built to contain her—the Pleiades Tower in the
Auguria Sand Dunes.

"We don't fully understand the meaning of the prophecy," Miklotov explained. "Our best
assumption is that the Sage has left the tower and may have come to assist us in our time of
need."

"This brings me to the next point—Reinhard van Astrea," Miklotov announced.

The knight who had his name spoken knelt in place, drawing all eyes towards him.

"You are assigned this mission. Your task is to find the Sage and bring her to us, as her arrival
could signal a period of turmoil this kingdom may struggle to face."

"As you wish, Miklotov-sama. I will work with utmost diligence to accomplish my mission,"
he replied with a bow as he rose.

"Now that everything is settled, and all candidates have shared their intentions, I hereby
announce that the Royal Selection for the forty-second ruler of the Dragon Kingdom of
Lugunica has officially commenced!"
