Chapter 45: Arc 4 - Rem’s Lesson
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

As Subaru entered the rift, like a crack in space, he found himself surrounded by a swirling,
deep blue void. The energy twisted and twirled around him, carrying him forward through
space, even though he remained perfectly still.

He idly noted that it was similar to his teleportation, at least in principle.

The sensation didn’t last long. Soon, the swirling blue gave way to an empty darkness,
swallowing everything in sight. Blinking, Subaru realized he was back in his body, staring at
the ceiling above.

‘I’m back!’ he thought, rising to his feet and brushing off his clothes. He flexed his fingers,
rolled his shoulders, and took a deep breath—he could feel everything again.

The lightness in the air he had experienced before was gone, replaced by the familiar density
of mana-rich air. A cold, heavy atmosphere settled around him, far from the warmth and
gentleness of where he had just been. Yet, somehow, this felt more natural. More right.

“Well, I guess Echidna was telling the truth,” he muttered to himself, inspecting his body for
any signs of damage—magical or physical—but finding nothing.

If his soul had been ripped from his body and he had genuinely died, that would have been
the lamest possible ending for the world’s strongest jujutsu sorcerer, right behind dying of old
age.

Unless, of course, the latter befell the Jujutsu Higher-ups or the council of senile men. Then,
it would actually be quite entertaining.

Shaking his head to clear away unnecessary thoughts, Subaru refocused. His mind retraced
the events of the last few minutes—and, more importantly, the woman he had just met.

“Echidna…”

The name lingered on his tongue, bringing an unfamiliar flavor with it, as the image of that
woman flashed in his mind.

He truly didn’t know what to think of Echidna, the Witch of Greed—what opinion he held of
her or what her true intentions were.

On one hand, he was wary and suspicious, as was only natural. After all, she was a witch—a
self-proclaimed evil one, no less.

Despite her friendly and polite demeanor, something about her felt off. It was as if she were
putting on an act, or more specifically, it wasn’t entirely genuine. And the way her behavior



changed when he called her a "Nasty Pervert" or when she was questioned about Satella
hinted at something beneath the surface.

And then there was the way she spoke. It gave him the impression that she knew him, that
she had met him before.

Which was evident by the speech about him being desirable, about how she could never
comprehend him nor predict him, felt passionate yet out of place. While he wanted to dismiss
it as the ramblings of a lonely witch, something about her words resonated with him in ways
he couldn’t quite explain.

But, on the other hand, she didn’t seem entirely deceitful. She was courteous, even going out
of her way to extend an olive branch to build trust between them.

She answered every question. Even seemed genuinely dismayed at the prospect of him
leaving.

She even helped him by lending him healing mana to stabilize the Sloth witch factor inside
him.

As Subaru walked toward the exit, these thoughts ran through his mind. The remainder of the
witch factor made a deep frown settle on his face.

If Subaru was honest, the thought of that disgusting presence forcing its way into his Od—his
very soul—made his skin crawl, his toes curl, and the hairs on his neck stand on end.

He felt utterly violated. Deeply. As though something dark and toxic had seeped into his
essence, corrupting it into something grotesque.

And then, there was the realization, the repulsive fact that he now shared something in
common with Betelgeuse, the Archbishop of Sloth of all people. That repulsive, deranged
madman. The very person he had wanted nothing to do with.

‘I still don’t understand how it happened,’ Subaru thought grimly. ‘Blue should have pulled
in the Od and destroyed it, and should’ve destroyed  the Witch Factor as well. That’s why I
aimed there in the first place.’

The sheer sight of something so repulsive—that his own Six Eyes couldn’t even comprehend
it—had compelled him to destroy it on sight.

But that plan had failed.

And now, one of those things was actively merging with him.

Maybe he should use Hollow Purple instead? That was his strongest attack, and it should
have been enough to dispose of them. He’d have to test it the next time he encountered an
archbishop.

As the mana slowly faded and the first rays of light broke through, relief flooded him. He had
to go out there, find everyone, make sure his negligence didn’t put them at risk.



And he needed to clear his mind, to see what he could do about the witch factor, and if it was
impossible to remove, make peace with the fact that he had to live with one. It was part of the
reason he had asked to leave in the first place.

Yet, regardless of whether Echidna was truly an ally or someone concealing ulterior motives,
one thing was clear.

Their conversation was far from over.

He stepped out of the ruins, squinting against the bright sunlight. The sun remained high in
the sky, indicating that he had only been inside for a few minutes at most. That meant he
hadn’t lost too much time. There was still a chance to find everyone.

Before he could set off, his eyes caught movement ahead—a flash of familiar blue hair
approaching him.

“Rem!” he called, relief surging through him at the sight of the oni-maid, who smiled warmly
at his appearance.

“Subaru-kun!” Rem exclaimed, her expression lighting up upon seeing him safe and sound.
“Rem is so relieved to finally find you—!”

She barely finished her sentence before Subaru closed the distance in an instant, sweeping her
into a tight, back-breaking hug.

“S-S-Subaru—?!” Rem stammered, shocked by the sudden and tight embrace. Not that she
minded—the color flooding her cheeks spoke volumes.

“Rem! Thank god you’re okay! I didn’t know what I would do if you were hurt,” he breathed,
clutching her tightly before finally letting go.

“How did you find me? What about Otto and Emilia? Are they with you? Were you
teleported with them? Are they safe?” he asked, hands gripping her shoulders as urgency took
over.

Rem, her face still flushed, had to blink rapidly and shake herself out of her daze before
responding.

“Rem is very familiar with Subaru-kun’s scent, so she used it to track him down,” she
explained. “Unfortunately, Rem was separated from everyone, so she doesn’t know where
Emilia-sama or Otto-san are.”

Subaru nodded along as he listened to her words. Normally, He might have questioned how
and why she knew his scent that well, but given the circumstances, he was only grateful for
it.

“It’s good that you found me, Rem. Now that you’re here, we can focus on finding the rest,”
Subaru said.

“The rest? Emilia-sama and Otto-san aren’t with you?” she asked, and he shook his head.



“No, I was looking for them until I stumbled upon this place.” He gestured toward the ruins.
“I searched inside, but they weren’t there, so I stepped outside and—well, you know the
rest.”

He omitted his encounter with the witch, just as she had asked him to. While he could have
shared it, he didn’t want to disregard her request and risk unforeseen consequences.

“That’s unfortunate, but maybe they weren’t teleported too far? Rem didn’t need to search
long before she found you. Maybe they were sent together?” Rem suggested.

“I can only hope so, Rem. I just pray none of them are hurt, or else I—” He paused, clenching
his fists as the one behind this mess appeared in his mind.

“Subaru-kun? Are you alright?” Rem asked, concerned about crossing her features as she
noticed his tense posture and anger rising.

“Rem,” he said, his tone firm, “I think this entire mess was a setup by Frederica.”

Rem’s expression shifted to confusion and concern. “A setup? What do you mean?”

Subaru continued, “Just think about it. We spent the whole day helping Frederica yesterday,
but she never once mentioned anything about the sanctuary or the barrier, until Emilia was
left alone right before we left. Doesn’t that seem strange?”

“Yes, that’s—”

“And that necklace was supposed to let Emilia pass through the barrier safely, but instead, it
knocked her out and teleported all of us away, separating us in this forest.”

“O-oh, but—”

“So tell me, Rem. Doesn’t this feel like a setup? It’s obvious Frederica has some kind of
hidden motive when it comes to Emilia. Maybe she wants to hurt her, or worse, kill her!
Think about it, Rem! And she could also—”

Subaru’s words spilled out in a relentless stream, his mind racing through every suspicion he
had about the demi-human maid. He went on and on about the possible dangers Emilia and
Otto were facing. Rem tried to interject, but with no room to speak, she opted to remain silent
and listen, though a deep frown settled on her face.

When he finally stopped, his breathing was ragged, his fists clenched tight, and a faint flush
burned on his cheeks. He had gotten more worked up the more he talked.

Once the silence stretched between them, Rem finally spoke. “Subaru-kun, Rem understands
the dangers Emilia-sama and Otto-san are facing. And Rem knows how much her hero
worries for their well being.”

Subaru opened his mouth to agree, but Rem didn’t let him.

Her eyes, usually so gentle, held an uncharacteristic disapproval.



“What Rem cannot understand, nor accept, is Subaru-kun’s fear and paranoia leading him to
rash actions and making him accuse Frederica-san without evidence, or the unjust hostility he
is showing toward her.”

Subaru felt like he had been slapped, and the worst part was that it was Rem of all people.

He could admit he hadn’t known her for long, only about a month, but never once had she
shown disapproval toward something he did.

“What—Rem… Did you not hear anything I just said? Frederica is our enemy! This is a trap!
It has to be!” he insisted, his voice edged with frustration.

But the maid simply shook her head.

“Subaru-kun, Rem understands what you are trying to convey, but will you please listen to
what she has to say?” she asked gently.

Subaru wanted to argue, but the look on her face made him stop.

“Alright, alright. You can say your piece. I promise I won’t interrupt,” he relented, and Rem
smiled in gratitude.

“Rem knows her hero is very suspicious of Frederica-san, since he has only just met her, but
he shouldn’t be quick to judge her so quickly,” she said, her voice soft but firm.

She hesitated briefly before continuing, her expression tinged with sadness.

“Isn’t that what Subaru-kun wanted Rem to learn after she foolishly attacked him? To listen
and search for the facts instead of judging and acting based on emotions alone?”

Subaru felt a lump in his throat.

She was right; this was indeed the lesson he hoped she would learn following the Mabeast
incident.

Now, however, he found his own lesson being turned back on him. He didn’t need anyone to
point out the irony of it all.

“After our home was destroyed, Rem and her sister met Frederica-san when we began
working for Roswaal-sama. She had been with us for many years. We grew up together. We
know her well.”

“Frederica-san is kind, gentle, and hardworking. She taught and guided both Rem and Nee-
sama, showing us how to be noble maids so that we could serve Roswaal-sama with the
utmost diligence and reach where we are today.”

“Rem understands that Subaru-kun has raised some valid concerns, but Rem is inclined to
believe there may be some misunderstandings rather than Frederica acting with ill intent.”



Rem gently placed a hand on Subaru’s shoulder. “Subaru-kun is worried about Emilia-sama
and Otto-san, and Rem feels the same way. But she asks him not to be rash toward Frederica-
san and to withhold judgment until he fully understands everything.”

Subaru remained silent, absorbing Rem’s words. The maid, her hand still resting on his
shoulder, searched his expression, but his face remained unreadable, his eyes concealed
behind his sunglasses.

Then, slowly, he pushed his glasses down, revealing his eyes to Rem. She felt a slight blush
creep onto her cheeks beneath the intensity of his ethereal gaze—but finally, she understood
the emotions in them.

Pride and shame.

“Look at you,” Subaru said, his voice brimming with admiration. “From the impulsive girl
who attacked me to the woman you are now. You’ve grown, Rem, and I’m proud of you.”

He rubbed her head gently, and she basked in the warmth of his words, savoring the affection
in his gesture.

“Of course, she has! Rem has learned from the best,” she replied, matching the pride in his
tone.

Subaru looked away, scratching his head. “And I guess you’re right. I kinda jumped the gun
on my accusation, didn’t I?”

He turned back to her, sighing. “Sorry, Rem. It’s just… a lot of stuff has happened to me
recently, and with little to process them, and i’m on edge because of them.”

Seeing the flicker of shame in his eyes, Rem gently took hold of his hands, guiding his gaze
back to her.

“Rem may not understand everything her hero has been through, but she will always stand by
his side to comfort him in his time of need,” she said softly, a bright smile forming on her
lips.

Then, her expression turned playful. “Now, wipe that look off your face, Subaru-kun. Rem
hates it—it doesn’t suit her hero. Let’s go find Emilia-sama and Otto-san. They still need our
help!”

Subaru matched her smile with one just as radiant, determination now the dominant feature
on his face. “You’re right, Rem! We’ve wasted too much time; let’s go!”

And so, the two of them headed into the forest in search of their friends.

Chapter End Notes



Initially, this bit was meant to be part of a larger chapter, but the heartwarming
interaction between Rem and Subaru compelled me to make it a standalone one.

And man, Rem is soooo huggable~ ^-^



Chapter 46: Arc 4 - Otto-man’s Continuous Misfortunes
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

As the carriage rolled along quietly on the dirt road, the only sound was the crunching of its
wheels against the ground. Otto Suwen, a merchant whose place in the Emilia camp
depended on the decision of an eccentric clown-noble, guided the carriage toward their
destination.

With Patrasche pulling the carriage, carrying them forward at an impressive pace, they were
fast approaching a place that made the hair on Otto's neck stand on end.

The infamous forest where those who wandered in and lost their way were never seen again.

Despite his young age and inexperience, Otto had seen his fair share of things as a traveling
merchant. He had heard countless stories, legends, and ominous warnings from superstitious
folk, each portraying this seemingly normal forest as a place of horror.

It was always the same, the tales spoke of young and foolish explorers who entered that
cursed place, never to be seen ever again.

Otto Suwen was not one to put much stock in ghost tales. While he acknowledged that some
places were genuinely dangerous—like forests filled with Mabeasts, secret hideouts of witch
cults, and lands claimed by fairies—only a few truly deserved such dire reputations. One of
those was the Auguria Sand Dunes. 

Situated in the remote eastern part of Lugunica, this area was a vast desert—so parched that
rain never fell, and so blistering that the relentless sun could take the life of anyone who
couldn't find shelter. It was so unwelcoming that no one had ever attempted to establish a
settlement there. 

Legends described it as an endless wasteland suffocated by miasma, a smell so potent that it
could drive people to insanity. Naturally, this made it a haven for Mabeasts, lurking in the
desolate dunes, ready to consume any unwary travelers. 

There were even stories of various unidentified creatures with grotesque and horrifying
appearances, wielding unconventional and unknown types of magic, roaming the sands and
slaughtering everything in their path, including the Mabeasts.

Although these tales often exaggerate, there is some truth to them, such as the fact that this
region is home to the Pleiades watchtower, a structure built where the wise Sage Shaula
resides, overseeing a seal that contains the dreaded Witch of Envy. 

As he recalled the legends and stories he had read and learned, Otto opened his mouth, and a
guttural, growling, raspy sound emerged—something akin to the noises made by reptiles.
Hearing such sounds from a human would surely make one question their sanity.



Yet for Otto is it the most natural thing, for the sounds he produced served a distinct purpose.

"Hey, Patrasche, do you feel any dangers nearby? Anything I should keep my eyes open
for?"

The running Ground Dragon turned its head slightly, its beady eye locking onto Otto. A deep
sound rumbled from its throat, one not unlike the one Otto had made.

"No, I sense no danger nearby, Merchant. You're not scared, are you?"

This was the effect of Otto Suwen's Divine Protection of Soul Language—the ability to
communicate with animals and understand them. Just like speaking to humans, his Divine
Protection allowed him to converse in a language animals could comprehend, and they
responded in kind.

And he could hear them, too. All of them. Every animal within his surroundings, their voices
blending into a chaotic tangle of incomprehensible sounds that had once overwhelmed him as
a child. It had been a difficult burden, but he had learned to overcome it.

It was an incredibly useful gift, one that Otto used for various purposes. And in this moment,
it served as reconnaissance.

Knowing what dangers lay ahead, whether it be bandits or unforeseen obstacles—was vital.
Otto was doing this to ensure the safety of everyone with him. Nothing more, nothing less.

"I'm not! I just want to know if there are any dangers ahead of us so we can prepare,
that's all!" Otto shot back, denying the false accusation.

Patrasche's gaze lingered on him, unimpressed.

"This is the tenth time you've asked me, and it hasn't been long since the first question. At
this point, you're more scared of that forest than worried about everyone else."

"I-I'm not! I told you, I just want—"

"So you won't admit it? What a wuss," the ground dragon huffed before turning her
attention back to the road, leaving Otto sighing in exasperation.

It wasn't fear! None whatsoever!

…

Okay… Maybe just a tiny bit.

But he had every right to be scared!

Just days ago, while traveling through the Mathers domain in a desperate attempt to sell off-
season oil and pull himself out of debt, he had been ambushed by witch cultists and tied to a
stake, only to be saved moments away from being burned alive. 



Even though he was alive, that incident shook him up and continued to affect him for days
afterward.

And now, here he was, heading toward the forest where people who go there never return.

How could he not be scared?

"Relax, merchant. You're worrying over nothing," Patrasche suddenly said as she pulled the
carriage forward.

"Didn't you say my rider killed someone strong? If this carriage gets attacked, he'll defend
it. So stop cowering and pull yourself together."

"…Oh. You're right, I guess..."

After his rescue and during his temporary stay at the Karsten mansion, news reached him that
the witch cult attacking Emilia's camp had been all but wiped out, along with the archbishop
who orchestrated it, defeated in battle.

The revelation left him stunned—how could it not? This was the witch cult, the same group
that had spread death and destruction for years, their presence a shadow hanging over the
world. Victories against them were rare, the last significant one being the Subjugation of the
Blight Dragon.

But at the same time, it wasn't entirely far-fetched. After all, he had been saved by the very
person who had single-handedly slain a group of cultists without breaking a sweat.

Otto was immensely grateful to him—not just for saving his life, but for giving him the
chance to escape a fate as a debt slave. Even if he had been subjected to relentless teasing and
had often found himself the butt of jokes, it didn't diminish the gratitude he felt.

And so, with the same man who had slain the archbishop sitting behind him, and with the
route engraved in his mind, Otto finally allowed himself to relax, at least a little. A rare
moment of idleness these days.

For a few more minutes, he followed the path as Frederica had instructed, listening to the
chatter inside the carriage. This time, they let him listen instead of him having to eavesdrop
like before.

He heard mention of the necklace Frederica had given to Emilia, and how she needed it to
pass through the barrier in the forest. Otto almost questioned why she required it while they
did not—but instead, he focused on Rem's explanation.

Apparently, the barrier lay somewhere within the forest, possessing the ability to make people
lose their way should they wander too close.

Otto wasn't sure how to feel about that. On the one hand, he was relieved that, in the end, the
stories were only referring to a barrier meant to keep the sanctuary safe—not some ominous
curse or mystical evil force. On the other hand, it still unsettled him. Why would such a place
need something like that in the first place?



He then learned of the name given to the woods—The Lost Forest of Kremaldy.

'What a name… It really does fit well,' Otto thought.

His thoughts were interrupted by Subaru's voice from the window.

"You heard that, Otto? People really do get lost there! Feeling nervous now?"

Otto checked the road to make sure the coast was clear before replying, "Not at all! With
Frederica-san's guidance, I'm confident we'll reach the Sanctuary without any issues."

Subaru's presence also reassured him, but he chose to keep it to himself, lest he get
relentlessly teased for being a helpless maiden in need of a hero.

There was a slight pause before Subaru responded, "Looks like you've grown a pair, Otto.
Keep it up, and I might follow up on my promise and put up a nice word for you."

Otto was ready to retort but stopped as the implications of Subaru's words dawned on him.

"Wait, you weren't planning to do that?!" he shouted indignantly.

What did he get in return? A snicker from Subaru before he shut the window.

If he wasn't sulking before, Otto certainly was now. Had he been tricked into being nothing
more than a coach driver? Was the whole meeting with Roswaal a lie as well?

'No, Natsuki-san is just messing with me… like he always does,' he thought gloomily.

He could already sense this would become a regular habit, and he had no clue how to put an
end to it. Rolling with the punches and waiting for the perfect moment to clap back seemed
like the best course of action.

But that would only encourage Subaru more…

There really was no hope of stopping it, was there?

And so, with his spirits in a low mood, the carriage continued on at a slow pace, the sounds
of wildlife and the carriage's movement filling the air.

After some time, Otto found himself in a different forest—one that stood apart from the rest.
The trees were larger, thicker, and denser, casting deep shadows beneath them. The whole
place was quieter than before, and he could feel the profound presence of mana lingering in
the air.

"This is it." He heard Patrasche as she observed everything around her. "This is the forest
my rider wanted to go to."

"Really? Is this it?" He mirrored the ground dragon's action as he looked around.



Despite the slight differences, it looked like a normal forest, not much different from the ones
he had traveled through before. And while the increased presence of mana could be a
worrying sign, it didn't necessarily mean anything ominous—just that there were probably
some mana deposits in the area.

"Yes. You got worked up over a normal forest, merchant," Patrasche responded.

Otto let out a nervous laugh. "Hahaha, I guess I did. I'm an idiot, aren't I?"

"Yes," Patrasche mercilessly replied without hesitation.

Crushed by how quickly the ground dragon agreed with him, Otto opened the window to
announce their arrival.

"Excuse me," he said, getting everyone's attention. "We're in the forest now."

Seeing them all looking out of the window, Otto leaned back with a sigh and continued
leading the carriage onward.

The ride had been smooth so far—no sudden ambushes, no obstacles in the path. Just a
straightforward road and an easy route to follow.

'Man, did I really get myself scared over nothing? What an idiot I am… well, at least my luck
is changing for once,' he thought with a smile.

With how peaceful the journey had been so far, Otto had started to believe that his rotten luck
had finally loosened its grip, granting him a chance to breathe. 

Everything would be just fine!

He automatically regretted that naïve thought as he heard a commotion coming from inside.

From the anxious and worried voices, Otto felt his stomach drop—only for the feeling to
worsen when Subaru's panicked shout rang out.

"Umm—can someone tell me what's going on?" he called out to the passengers, but no reply
came—only the frantic sounds of Subaru and Rem fussing over Emilia.

Turning to look outside the window, Otto saw Rem holding up a slumped Emilia while
Subaru hurried to her side. Dread welled up inside him.

He wanted to ask again, but his attention was suddenly caught by a blue glow emanating
from the necklace around the half-elf's neck. Subaru's outstretched hand was reaching for it.

And then—without warning—the glow expanded, blinding Otto completely.

The wave of fear hit him at the same time as the surge of mana flooding from the necklace.

He heard the sound of an animal howling in surprise, though his mind barely registered it as
the carriage lurched, screeched to a halt—then Otto was flung off of it, swallowed by the



light.

For a few moments, Otto was airborne, soaring through the air blind.

Then came the harsh landing.

He crashed down onto the ground, rolling violently as twigs and pebbles scraped against him.
Pained sounds escaped his lips as he tumbled, unable to stop until—finally—he collided with
a tree.

The impact let out a loud twag, and his right ribs bore the full brunt of the collision.

As everything stilled and the chaos subsided, Otto lay motionless, staring blankly at the
blurred outlines of the long branches above him.

"Owwww!" A loud pained whimper escaped his throat as aches flared across his body—his
ribs, in particular, burned like fire.

Otto attempted to rise, slowly twisting to face the ground, pressing a hand flat against the
earth as he tried to push himself up. His disoriented state made it ten times harder than it
should have been, but inch by inch, he managed to get onto one knee.

He tried to stand fully—only for a sudden, piercing pain in his side to stop him cold,
accompanied by a sharp agony in his lungs.

"Argk!" he groaned, collapsing back to the ground like a sack of potatoes, the pain in his lung
refusing to let up.

The realization dawned upon him—he had broken his ribs, and one of them had lodged itself
against his right lung.

"Ow! B-by the dragon… What happened?" he groaned in pain, his mind still fogged by the
dizziness from all the tumbling he had just endured.

As the disorientation faded, clarity returned, and Otto retraced the sequence of events in his
mind—the panicked shouting, the eerie blue light, the moment he was sent flying, and the
harsh reality of where he had landed .

That was when he grasped the gravity of his situation: injured, immobile, stranded in the
middle of the forest with no one in sight to help him.

His confusion gave way for fear to start settling in.

'D-damnit! Why! Why does this always happen to me?!' he thought, biting his lip, fists
clenched in frustration.

It had been naïve to believe his rotten luck wouldn't strike him down—it always loomed over
him like the specter of death, waiting for the perfect moment to make his life harder.



And now, here he was—near powerless. He couldn't move, couldn't run, couldn't defend
himself.

His only lifeline was earth magic. But even that was hardly reliable, with mana reserves that
barely stood above average.

"Dona!" using earth magic, Otto summoned a protective wall of earth from the ground. Three
more casts of the spell, and now four walls surrounded him, a cube of safety in the midst of
danger.

'If I can't move or do anything, then I'll just wait here until I can—or until help arrives,' he
thought, solidifying his plan.

Fear still clawed at him, but his ingrained instinct to survive pushed past the panic, forcing
him to act rationally.

Otto closed his eyes, focusing on steady, controlled breaths to calm his racing heart and ease
the pain in his lung. He carefully kept his breaths half-full—any deeper, and his ribs might
puncture his lung.

And so, he waited silently, hoping for anyone, hoping for Natsuki-san to come and save him.

Now that the adrenaline had drained away, he felt every bruise and cut littering his body, the
tattered state of his clothes barely registering in his mind. He bit his tongue and ignored it all.

'Focus, Otto, focus. Stay calm and wait. Help will come, Natsuki-san will find you, and you
will be saved. Just relax and—'

His thoughts cut off abruptly.

The sound of stomping. 

His heart sank.

It was growing closer. Closer to his hiding spot.

And it wasn't human.

The weight, the rhythm, the sheer force—it was an animal. A Mabeast.

'Oh, this is bad. This is really bad!' Otto thought, immediately going stiff. His hands flew to
his mouth to muffle his breathing.

He had thought the worst had already passed. That his cube would keep him safe.

But his luck—no, his misfortune—never allowed things to go his way.

Now, Otto didn't know how many Mabeasts were lurking outside, but he knew without a
doubt that his chaotic entrance had attracted something. His bloodied wounds likely made
him an enticing target.



But fear didn't have an iron grip on his heart. He had a backup plan.

Reaching into the side bag that miraculously was still tied to his waist, he opened it and let
out a sigh of relief upon feeling the pouch inside.

Otto had always known he might one day find himself cornered, which is why he kept a
pouch of fire stones on hand—just in case.

Opening it, he examined its contents. Multiple fire crystals of different sizes gleamed inside.
He grabbed a medium-sized one.

'Alright, Otto, just wait until it gets closer, then toss it over the wall. It should hold against the
blast and keep you safe. Hopefully, it'll scare it off. Natsuki-san will come and save you… I
hope so.'

Otto knew—without question—that he was the unluckiest man alive. Yet despite that, he still
clung to hope.

And why did he trust Subaru to be his savior in particular? Because Subaru had saved his life
before—so if it was going to be anyone, it would be him.

Or at least he hoped so.

As the Mabeast neared the wall, Otto steadied himself. All he needed to do was infuse the
crystal with some of his earth mana, destabilizing it just enough to trigger an explosion—
either on impact or after a set amount of time.

Essentially, it was a fantasy world's version of a lit stick of dynamite.

And as the Mabeast came right up against the wall, Otto braced himself, ready to inject his
mana and throw—

"Merchant? Is that you? Are you in there?"

The amount of relief Otto felt upon hearing that voice could have made him cry from
happiness.

"Patrasche?! Y-yes, it's me, Otto! Otto Suwen!" he called out to the ground dragon.

'I've been saved! Ahahaha! She's not Natsuki-san, but I'm saved nonetheless!' He was just
glad to hear a familiar voice—even if it belonged to an animal. 

Otto lifted his hand to lower the walls, only to freeze as they suddenly crumbled before him,
revealing Subaru's ground dragon staring down at him.

"Hmm… You look miserable," Patrasche observed.

Otto could only smile weakly at her "I know, tell me about it."

Patrasche took a moment to scan the area before finally locking her yellow eyes onto Otto's.



"Would I be wrong to assume that my rider isn't with you?" she questioned.

Otto shook his head. "Sadly, no. To be honest, I was hoping he would be with you…" he
trailed off.

"Figures… Well, no point in staying here. Let's get moving—the carriage isn't far off,"
Patrasche informed him.

"The carriage isn't far off ? Wait, is someone with you? Is it Rem-san or Emilia-sama? "

"The half-elf? Yes, she's fine. But she won't wake up after I licked her a little bit. Now
come on, I want to reunite with my rider before anything else."

Otto took a moment to process this.

'So, she's safe but unconscious… Thank the Od for that. What even happened anyway? I
remember everyone panicking, then a light… Were we teleported? Is that it?'

As he pondered over the events, he failed to notice that Patrasche had already started walking
away, leaving him behind.

"W-wait!" he called out after the impatient ground dragon, who stopped and glanced back at
him.

"What?" she asked, clearly impatient.

"Well… I can't stand or walk. So can you please help me?" he pleaded, offering her a
sheepish smile.

Patrasche stared at him before huffing and striding toward him. Just as he was about to speak,
she grabbed his jacket and swiftly hoisted him onto his feet, eliciting a pained yelp as he
struggled to regain his balance.

"You can walk. Now come on, we're wasting time," she said, moving ahead of the merchant
as he shakily stood up, one hand pressed against his bruised side.

As Otto steadied himself, a flash of pink flickered at the edge of his vision. He blinked and
turned toward the source—but saw nothing. Dismissing it as a trick of his mind, he quickly
hurried after Patrasche.

Before long, they arrived at the carriage, sitting in a small clearing devoid of trees.

"When that blue light came and went, I found myself here, with the carriage still attached
to me," Patrasche explained.

The carriage itself seemed intact, though dirt marred its exterior, and its wheels bore chipped
and cracked edges along the bottom.

"Wait…" when he noticed the conditions of the wheels, Otto slowly turned toward the ground
dragon beside him.



"Patrasche, did you… um, slide or something like that when that light came, or…?" he
asked hesitantly.

"Yes. I thought we were being attacked. Why do you ask?" She turned to face him, her
sharp yellow eyes narrowing slightly.

"Well, it's just—You know what? Never mind," he cowered from her eyes.

Patrasche let out a huff, clearly unimpressed by the useless question.

But for Otto, the question was anything but trivial. The memory of being sent flying before
the teleportation returned with clarity—meaning that, ironically, Patrasche had been the
source of his injuries, not the teleportation.

Pushing the thought that his savior was the one responsible for his injuries aside with a weary
sigh, Otto limped toward the back of the carriage—only to be met with utter chaos inside.

The bags of luggage they had brought were scattered everywhere, mixed with anything that
had been secured or attached to the carriage.

And among the chaos, Otto spotted Emilia, sprawled carelessly on the ground, junk scattered
around her.

"Emilia-sama," he called out, his voice drained of the urgency one might expect upon finding
someone in distress—exhaustion from his injuries now weighing heavily on him.

Yet, Emilia remained undisturbed in her sleep. Her expression showed neither pain or
discomfort, only a serene, blissful peace.

Otto approached cautiously, checking for injuries without touching her—she was a royal
candidate, after all, and the leader of the camp he was aiming to join.

Thankfully, she was unharmed. No cuts, no bruises. The only signs of her ordeal were the
wrinkles in her clothes, but otherwise, she was in pristine condition.

'At least Emilia-sama is safe… This must be the elf's physiology at work,' he thought,
recalling what he had read about elves and their exceptional durability—resilient enough to
endure blunt force without injury.

Clearing the couch of debris, the clattering sounds echoed as he pushed aside the mess. Once
he had made enough space, he turned his gaze to the slumbering beauty before him.

'This is going to suck… Why do I do this to myself?' Otto questions himself. But he already
knew the answer: because it was the right thing to do.

With a strained expression, he knelt down, biting back the pain in his lungs, took a sharp,
shallow breath, and lifted Emilia, his body groaning and muscles aching as he carried her to
the couch to ensure she could rest comfortably.



Once finished, Otto leaned against the wall, hissing as the pain in his side flared sharply, his
right lung aching even more.

But he refused to falter—now that he had reunited with Patrasche and Emilia-sama, he would
press on and find the others

Not by walking, of course—he was in no condition to do that anymore. He'll use the carriage
to search for the others.

Stumbling out, he made his way to the front seat, where Patrasche stood, scanning the area.

"Patrasche," he called to her, "We need to get moving. Emilia is safe and secure. Let's use
the carriage to find Rem-san and Natsuki-san."

He presented his idea to the ground-dragon, who, much to his surprise, shook her head.

"No. We should stay here and wait for them to come to us," she replied, fixing him with a
firm stare.

"B-but why? If we leave now, we could cover more ground and find each other faster!"
Otto argued, trying to reason with her.

Once again, she rejected his idea.

"That won't work. My rider is most definitely searching for us, and if we move, we might
be heading in the opposite direction—only putting more distance between us. It's better to
stay in one place and conserve our energy."

"And you," she added, stepping closer, examining him with sharp eyes, "Don't look like
you're in any shape to travel—even if you were to sit in the back with the half-elf. You'd
only make your injuries worse. I can see you're barely staying on your feet."

She nudged her head toward the back door.

"Go get some rest, Otto Suwen. Trust in my rider—he will find us before you know it."

Otto remained silent, floored by Patrasche's reasoning.

It wasn't that she had said anything groundbreaking—if he weren't so exhausted, he probably
would have come to the same conclusion himself.

But the fact that she was an animal—and yet capable of such logic and foresight—was
astonishing.

"You know what, Patrasche?" he finally said, shaking his head with a tired smile. "And I
don't say this lightly—but you are the smartest animal I've ever had the pleasure of talking
to."

Patrasche cast a proud glance at him—well, as proud as a ground dragon could manage.



"Of course! I'm Patrasche—a uniquely created, one-of-a-kind ground dragon—and my
rider is the most honorable and exceptional of them all. It only makes sense that someone
as remarkable as him would have a companion like me."

Otto chuckled at her words, not taking them too seriously. He chalked it up to the boastful
nature of a proud sub-species of ground dragons—especially one fortunate enough to have a
rider as extraordinary as Natsuki Subaru.

That small chuckle, brief as it was, helped release some of the built-up tension and stress
from the chaos he had endured.

Finally, Otto allowed himself to relax, heading back inside as he prepared to wait for Subaru's
arrival—

Until a tremor shook the ground beside them, kicking up dirt into a small cloud that stole
both of their attention with its sudden disturbance.

"So, th' old hag' was right—ya got some nerv' coming here, outsider!"

As the dust settled, a figure emerged.

Short, spiky golden hair. Emerald green eyes. A jagged "X" scar carved across his face,
highlighting sharp, predatory teeth. He was shirtless, his muscular frame exposed, clad only
in dark pants, a tattered purple loincloth, and worn boots.

There was a rugged, roguish air about him. The type prone to jumping to conclusions before
hearing anyone out.

But Otto paid his appearance no heed as he saw the sheer fury on the stranger's face.

His features were twisted in rage, his eyes burning with hatred as he glared at Otto and
Patrasche.

"It's bad 'nough—th' trouble ya caused back home—'n now ya think ya can show up here 'n
make it worse?" he growled, cracking his fists

"Not. Gonna. Happen."

Otto swallowed hard, the demi-human's hostility crystal clear—it wouldn't take much for him
to explode.

Otto slowly raised his hands, trying to calm him down "H-hold up! We don't want any
trouble, okay? We're just looking for our friends so we can head to the Sanctuary and—"

"Save it! Heard 'nough."

With a flash, the demi-human bolted forward—

And the only thing Otto could see was a fist, hurtling straight toward his face.



Then everything went black.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 47: Arc 4 - The Oni-maid's Wrath
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"Come on, Remmy, let’s go! I can see them all together right up ahead!"

"Okay, Rem will follow your lead, Subaru-kun!"

Within the dense forest of Kremaldy, Subaru and Rem moved through the endless sea of trees
and foliage, their surroundings offering little else to see.

For an ordinary person, navigating this labyrinth of nature would have been hopeless, but
Subaru was far from ordinary.

But how would they be able to find Emilia and the others in such a remote and dense forest,
where they could be miles upon miles apart? The answer is rather simple—because now, with
his glasses off, his six eyes scanned the terrain with precision.

It didn’t take long for him to spot their Od’s. Emilia, Patrasche, and Otto were close together
some distance away.

Farther beyond, something else caught his attention—hundreds of Od’s scattered in the
distance yet remained within a perimeter. Most were unfamiliar, while others belonged to the
Arlam refugees, Ram... and Roswaal.

His expression darkened for a moment when he caught sight of Roswaal’s Od, anger flashing
across his features. But he quickly wiped it off, refocusing solely on reuniting with his
friends.

There would be a time for that overdue conversation with the clown. He would press him for
answers, drag out the truths that had gnawed at him for far too long. But not now—not yet.

As they pressed forward, Subaru kept his otherworldly gaze locked on his friends, while Rem
remained alert, gripping her morningstar firmly. Her blue eyes darted left and right, ready to
pulverize anything that dared threaten him.

Or at least, that’s what she normally would have done.

This time, however, her vigilance was somewhat compromised. Because while she kept
watch, a good portion of her attention was focused elsewhere—stealing glances at Subaru’s
striking eyes.

His otherworldly azure-blue eyes, that seemed to shine in the darkness and carried a subtle
blue glow. They radiated power and strength, formidable yet carrying an undeniable warmth
—like a gentle mother caring for her children.



For Rem, even catching a peek at them was a victory in itself, so much so that she even
dreamed of the moment she saw them under the moonlight, the glow of the night sky
enhancing their beauty.

Among other dreams she had of Subaru-kun in various scandalous scenarios, but those were
better left unspoken, locked away and engraved deep within the maid’s mind.

As they walked further, Rem, with a faux determined expression, took a routine glance at
Subaru’s eyes. When she did, she was startled to find him already looking at her—and in that
fleeting moment, their eyes met.

Rem let out a cute "eep!" as she realized she had been caught staring. Quickly turning away,
she felt a warmth rush to her cheeks.

Subaru, in response, flashed a shit-eating grin, amused by the maid’s flustered reaction. Ever
since the Mabeast invasion, Rem had been much more receptive and friendly toward him.
Initially, he assumed it was just an attempt to build a casual friendship, to establish some
level of closeness.

But after her heartfelt confession that night in the capital, his perspective had shifted. He
finally understood the true meaning behind Rem’s recent behavior—the way she lit up when
she saw him, the way her face turned red when he accidentally brushed against her. He
wanted to punch himself for being a dense fool and not realizing it sooner.

It’s not like he had no experience with love; countless girls had confessed their “love” to him.
After all, he was a “handsome, tall, white-haired boy with sunglasses and a charming smile.”
And he himself had a crush on a certain white-haired beauty.

But this? This was different.

None of them made his heart beat faster like Rem did, nor did they make him feel genuinely
happy just by being in their presence. The same could be said about Emilia, his first friend in
this world—someone he had spent a great deal of time with.

Subaru knew with all his heart that he loved both of them. While such feelings were normally
a recipe for disaster and heartbreak, he refused to deny his heart.

After much thought back in his spare time, he had come up with a solution.

A selfish, greedy solution—but one that would make everything work out in the end.

He would implement it once he answered Rem and confessed his feelings to Emilia, once the
sanctuary situation was over, and they were all safely back home.

Right now, however, he had spotted Rem sneakily stealing glances at him—his eyes,
specifically. And with his friends safe and together, what better time was there to tease the
maid than now?

"Whatcha starin at, Rem? See something that caught your eye?" Subaru teased, his voice
carrying a playful lilt.



The maid immediately shook her head, her short blue hair swaying with the movement. "N-
nothing! Rem was just… checking her surroundings to keep Subaru-kun safe! Yes!"

"Oh really?" he said, raising an eyebrow, a smirk tugging at his lips. "I killed Whale and
Sloth, Remmy. So, while I appreciate the concern, I don’t exactly need protection. Unless
there’s something I somehow can’t see, what reason do you have for looking at me?"

"Umm—Because—Rem is…" Her face flushed a deep red as her mouth opened and closed,
struggling to form words. She had the look of a deer caught in headlights, which Subaru
found very amusing.

"So what is Rem?" he pressed, his grin widening. "Did you see something, or were you…
enamored by my eyes?" he asked, throwing in a wink for good measure.

Rem’s stammering had all but stopped, her blue eyes just kept staring at him, at his eyes,
focused solely on them—the pair of blue gems she had always dreamed of.

Her breath had turned shaky, heavy, and labored, her chest rising and falling in a rhythm that
mirrored her breathing. Her legs suddenly felt weak, unable to hold her weight. Her heart
thumped in her chest, beating faster and faster.

‘Man, this is so much fun!’ Subaru inwardly chuckled at Rem’s reaction. She and Emilia
always had the best ones out of the bunch, and he enjoyed teasing them both.

Deciding to up the ante a little, Subaru chose a bold approach.

“Remmy, if you like my eyes so much, then…”

With the grace of a snake, he slid his arms around Rem’s waist and pulled her toward him,
pressing her body against his.

She let out a squeak of surprise as she gazed up at Subaru, the height difference making her
look up at him.

“...why don’t you take a closer look? After all, you did help set me straight back then—you
deserve a little reward~” he said, leaning in closer to the maid.

It was at this proximity, at them being this near, that their hearts pounded rapidly. But despite
that, their rhythms somehow matched.

It was then that Subaru took note of Rem’s facial features. She had always been the definition
of the word “cute” in his books, but now… it was like he was seeing her for the first time.

Delicate and pretty features, soft and warm blue eyes that gazed at him with adoration and
love. A small, cute nose and rosy, soft pink lips that seemed just as inviting as they were
adorable.

And if that image alone wasn’t enchanting enough, his six eyes—blessed with great
perception—allowed him to see everything with a precision and clarity unlike anything he



had ever seen before. Just as he used them to admire the beauty of the stars, they now worked
for him to admire the beauty of the oni maid in his arms.

Subaru’s face started to mirror Rem's, as his cheeks gained a pronounced blush, their eyes
meeting and mesmerized by each other’s looks.

And, without any input from their brains, their bodies, on instinct, in unison, as if they were
cogs in a machine, moved. Their faces drew nearer and nearer, lips pursed, poised for the
inevitable contact with each other.

This… Subaru had not planned for things to go in this direction, but now that he was in the
moment—whether he wanted to or not—he was going to follow through. Because his heart
and soul told him that it was simply right for it to happen.

‘Yesyesyesyesyesyesyesyesyes—!’ Unlike Subaru, Rem was screaming in her mind, her soul
jumping up and down in sheer happiness. What had only existed in her dreams was finally
about to become reality.

And so, with great trepidation and barely concealed excitement—so much that she could drill
a hole into the earth—Rem closed her eyes and leaned forward to finally experience the
heavenly sensation that was about to come.

She waited for the warmth of Subaru’s lips to meet hers…

And waited…

And waited…

But Subaru's delicious-looking lips never came.

Confused, Rem pried open one of her eyes, expecting Subaru—but instead of leaning in to
kiss her, instead of even looking in her general direction, he was staring off into the distance,
his eyes narrowed into slits, unreadable emotions reflected within them.

“S-Subaru-kun? W-what’s the matter?” Rem voiced shakily, her arousal making her words
unsteady.

Subaru didn’t answer her. He just kept staring, focused so solely on a certain direction into
the forest.

If Rem’s mind had been clearer, she would have realized that he was staring toward the
direction where the others were.

“Shit,” he cursed, his voice so low that Rem barely caught it. Then, without warning,
Subaru’s hands withdrew from her waist, pushing her out of his embrace—a movement that
sent her body protesting, longing to return to the warmth it had just lost.

Rem opened her mouth to ask, but was beaten out by him.



"Rem! Otto’s under attack, I have to go!” He rattled off, and without warning, he took off
running into the forest, disappearing out of sight in a matter of moments.

Rem could only blink at what had just happened—confused and bewildered beyond
comprehension—her body still on edge. A storm of thoughts flooded her mind, trying to
process everything, but the sheer confusion only made her brain hurt.

But one thing was certain: whatever had just happened had ruined her first-ever kiss with her
hero.

‘Whoever you are, it doesn’t matter. Rem will make you pay for ruining her first kiss!’ 
She thought, the dark look on her face promising untold pain for whatever poor soul would
have the misfortune of facing her wrath.

 

---------------------------------

 

As the fist crashed into Otto's face, his head snapped to the side with a loud, sickening
crunch. The force of the blow sent him propelling backward until he slammed into the
carriage behind him. The impact made the vehicle tilt dangerously before it wobbled back
into position. The merchant slid down the carriage wall and collapsed into a crumpled heap,
unmoving except for a few weak twitches.

Otto has been Knocked out in one hit.

The assailant, a golden-haired demi-human, snorted in amusement at the pathetic sight before
him.

"Tha't it’? Yer knocked’ dow’ wi’h jus’ on’ punch?" he sneered, his sharp teeth glinting in the
sunlight. The merchant didn’t even put up a fight—just crumpled like wet parchment.
Absolutely pathetic.

“Kyaaa!” The demi-human turned sharply, locking eyes with the ground dragon that glared
back at him. Its beady yellow eyes narrowed into slits—a clear sign of intelligence beyond
simple instinct.

That made him laugh. "Th’ merchan’ don’t got’ guts, but at leas’  his ride got some, eh?"

Patrasche gave no reply, just kicked her hind legs back, tearing up the dirt in preparation to
charge.

Seeing that, the man’s grin stretched wider. "Yar a good groun’ dragon’, aren’tcha? Alrigh’,
imma waitin’ for ya! Com’ on!"

He threw his arms wide, standing firm in the dirt, ready to meet the charge head-on. His grin
stretched wide, flashing sharp teeth as he steadied himself, every muscle bracing for the
impact.



Patrasche surged forward, kicking up a storm of dust behind her, the ground trembling
beneath her powerful strides.

He prepared for the inevitable clash with the charging beast, but the encounter ended
differently than he had imagined. 

In a display of intelligence and agility, Patrasche halted just a few paces away, pivoting
sharply and sending a cloud of dirt into the man’s eyes, forcing him to raise his arms
defensively.

Seizing the opportunity, she harnessed the momentum of her run, using her tail like a whip to
strike him on the side of the head, catching him off guard.

The sharp crack of the impact echoed as he staggered back, his feet digging into the earth and
creating deep grooves until he finally came to a halt several paces away.

Lowering his arms, he revealed a small but noticeable bruise forming on his cheek, and the
golden glint in his eyes, coupled with a scowl, indicated his displeasure.

"You lil' rascal—tha' actually hurt!" he exclaimed, glaring at the audacious creature, his teeth
bared in a mix of irritation and surprise.

Patrasche, undeterred, met his gaze with a defiant glare of her own, her tail swaying playfully
and her head held high, exuding an air of mockery.

Though he wasn’t the most perceptive, the demi-human quickly grasped the message she was
sending: she was mocking him.

His brows twitched at the realization, stoking the fire of his annoyance.

"Tch. Oh, so ya think tha's funny, huh? Jus' a lil' joke to ya?" His face contorting into a
sharpened grin, mirroring the dangerous edge in his voice.

Cracking sounds filled the air as he twisted his neck and clenched his fist, a dangerous smile
creeping onto his face—one that promised wrath and pain, magnified by his sharp teeth.

“Howabout ah just clobber ya around, eh? See how funny it i’ when I hav’ ya brains
splattered al’ ova the ground, hmm?” he threatened, but the ground dragon wasn’t fazed by
his words.

Instead, it casually lifted its miniature front legs—ones resembling a dinosaur’s—and
scratched its long neck, completely disregarding the threat and ignoring the man entirely.

The man’s eyes darkened at the insult. He had wasted enough time trying to scare it—it was
high time he killed that thing for the insult.

“Donta dare t’ ignore me, ya bastard!” he roared as loud as he could, and just as she had done
to him, he charged directly at the ground dragon.



His speed was so great it surpassed anything in the forest. To anyone watching, he would
only appear as a blur, gone in the tiniest of moments. If one were to blink, they would have
missed him entirely.

Patrasche couldn’t track him with her eyes, even if she wanted to. To her, he had just
disappeared—the only sign of his existence being the trail of dirt following behind him as he
lunged towards her.

Any animal in her position would be whimpering in fear, and any human or demi-human
would have their face contorted in dread, knowing their time was coming to an end.

Anyone but Patrasche herself, who remained uncaring toward her seemingly impending
doom.

That man might have been the fastest and strongest person around, but he failed to account
for another person—her rider—one that dwarfed him in every physical category.

And he had just arrived to save her.

The man had his hands outstretched, his demi-human heritage granting him sharp claws,
ready to dig into the ground dragon. A nasty smirk formed on his face as he imagined what
he would do to it.

That smirk was wiped away in an instant as a foot lodged itself firmly against his cheek, the
force behind it stronger than anything he had ever felt. The effect was immediate—he was
veered off course, flung sideways at a speed resembling a bullet fired from a gun.

He flew through the air, crashing into trees and shattering them upon impact, splinters and
branches falling as he continued his uncontrollable flight into the distance.

Landing softly on the ground, Subaru stared toward the direction the assailant had been sent
flying, a neutral expression resting on his face.

‘Who the hell was that guy?’ he thought, not getting a clear image of him as he intervened
just right as he was about to harm his ground-dragon.

Speaking of which, Subaru turned toward his companion. "Patrasche! Are you okay? Did he
hurt you?"

Patrasche shook her head and ran forward to him. When she reached him, she nuzzled her
head into his neck, a soft rumble escaping her throat.

"I guess I’ll take that as a no, then. I’m glad you’re okay," he smiled gently, slowly rubbing
her neck—an act she greatly appreciated, leaning further into him.

Then, turning to the side, his smile vanished, replaced by a wince and a look of pity as he
took in the merchant's poor condition.

“Otto…” he said, leaving Patrasche and kneeling down in front of the merchant. He placed
two fingers on his neck and let out a relieved breath upon feeling a faint but noticeable pulse.



Otto was in bad shape. His six eyes gave him great details of his body covered in bruises and
cuts, his strained breathing hinting at possible rib injuries, and his hung-open mouth—likely
due to a dislocated jaw alongside several loose teeth.

But at the end of the day, the merchant was still alive.

Subaru hadn’t known him for more than two days, yet he had already taken a liking to him.
His teasing was proof enough of that—not that he’d ever admit it.

He turned toward Patrasche, who was approaching him. “Patrasche, can you do me a favor
and look after him?”

“Kyaaa!” she responded in the affirmative and walked over to Otto, standing protectively
over him. Subaru approved of her stance, offering a small pat on her head.

Now, it was time to confront the man who had hurt him—the same one who came flying out
of the treeline, landing a short distance away from Subaru, golden eyes burning with rage.

“You! Who th’ hell d’ya thin’ ya are, sneak' attckin’ my amazin’ self like that!” he growled,
looking dangerous—or at least, he would have, if not for the large bruise swelling on his right
cheek.

“…”

Subaru didn’t respond. Instead, behind his sunglasses, he scanned the man, taking in his
features and hair color, and a realization flickered behind his lenses.

‘Ah, no wonder I thought his Od felt familiar. That must be him, isn’t it?’

Even without his six eyes, it didn’t take a genius to know who this person was. His
appearance alone was telling—and thanks to Frederica’s warning, Subaru knew the name of
who he was dealing with.

Seeing that he was ignored again made him scowl even harder, his face twisting in fury as he
was purposely disregarded yet again within less than a minute.

As was evident before, he didn’t take kindly to being ignored. Normally, he would have
lashed out at anyone who dared dismiss him, and the urge to do so was overwhelming. But
his rational mind and instinct restrained him from lunging forward recklessly.

He had been hurt—badly. And Garfiel had rarely suffered injuries from anyone outside a
select few people. But he knew those people, and Subaru was not one of them.

So he had to stay wary and careful around him, while outwardly projecting an intimidating
presence to discourage any attempts to attack him.

As his killing glare and low growls filled the air, Subaru finished his quiet analysis and
finally decided to break the silence, hoping to cool him off.

“Hey, Frederica told me about you. Is your name—“



“Garfiel!”

A feminine voice interrupted Subaru mid-sentence, completing his words for him. Both men
turned toward the source and saw Rem standing at the foot of the treeline.

Subaru opened his mouth to speak, but Garfiel beat him to it. “R-Rem! Is that you?! Tha’ hell
ar’ ya doin’ here?!” Garfiel exclaimed, his tone filled with surprise.

Subaru blinked in shock upon hearing Rem’s name leave Garfiel’s mouth.

‘Rem?! He just said her name… Does he know her?’ he thought, shifting his gaze between
the two.

But Rem didn’t respond. Instead, she simply stared blankly at Garfiel, her eyes hidden behind
her hair. Then, her gaze flickered to Subaru and Patrasche, moved briefly to the unconscious
Otto, before settling back on Garfiel.

Subaru didn’t need his six eyes to know that Rem was angry—he had been unfortunate
enough to experience her wrath firsthand when she attacked him. But this time, that rage was
directed at someone else.

And despite what Garfiel had done to Otto, Subaru silently prayed for his well-being.

For Garfiel would not like what was about to happen next.

Wordlessly, Rem slowly walked toward the demi-human, who stared at her in confusion at
her mysterious silence. Shouldn’t she at least greet him?

“Rem? What’ tha’ matter? Why are yer so quiet?” he asked, but then his expression darkened
as he turned to Subaru.

“Did ya hurt her? Did ya hurt Rem? I swear if ya did somethin’ to her then ah’m gonna—!”

He was cut off by a loud thwack, a foot slamming into his chest and knocking him to the
ground.

“Ow! What th—!” He stopped mid-sentence as his eyes locked onto the look of utter fury on
Rem’s face—her fists clenched tightly, her mouth trembling as she pressed her lips together.

“Don’t presume Rem’s hero would ever hurt her, Garfiel!” she shouted, making him clamp
his mouth shut in surprise.

“Rem was about to have the happiest and most joyful moment of her life… And you ruined it
for Rem!”

A pink horn appeared on her forehead, accompanied by radiant power flooding through her
body with ambient mana. She knelt down, hovering over him, her knee firmly rooting his
torso in place.

“She will make you pay for what you’ve done!”



The beatdown that followed—delivered by Rem with not an ounce of mercy—made Subaru
and Patrasche wince and look away from how brutal and bone-crushing it was.

Chapter End Notes

Garfiel just cockblocked Rem, Biggest mistake in his entire life.



Chapter 48: Arc 4 - A Stand-Off With A Stubborn Cat
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The sound of the carriage’s backdoor creaking broke the quiet stillness, followed by the soft
groan of a foot pressing against the hardwood floor.

As Subaru stepped inside, his gaze swept over the scene, and his expression turned blank at
the sheer disorder before him.

‘Holy hell! It’s like a tornado tore through the carriage,’ he thought, momentarily stunned by
the mess.

But he quickly dismissed the thought. The state of the carriage was irrelevant compared to
the real concern—the well-being of the person he was most worried about.

Moving closer, he reached out, his fingers brushing against her cheek in a gentle, reassuring
caress as he studied her features.

‘Emilia…’ he murmured, his eyes softening while his six eyes carefully scanned her
condition.

Her Od was steady, her gate was fully functional, and her reserves were intact. No signs of
drain. No injuries, not even the faintest bruise or scratch.

Subaru released a deep, shuddering breath of relief, realizing she was completely unharmed
—not just physically, but magically and spiritually as well.

"Emilia… I’m so glad you’re safe. I don’t know what I would have done if you were hurt. If
my… negligence had put you in danger," he whispered, though the last words were especially
difficult to force out.

There were wounds, caused by bad memories within Subaru that he could never bring
himself to share—not even with Rem.

The memories were just that painful.

Shaking off the thoughts threatening to pull him deeper, he refocused his attention on the
cause of Emilia’s unconsciousness—the source of the chaos they had endured in the past
hour.

The necklace.

The gift Frederica had given her lay on the ground, its string burned away, leaving only
fragile, crumbling remnants. Without hesitation, Subaru bent down and retrieved it, gripping
it tightly in his palm.



Subaru analyzed the mana crystal, sensing it even before his eyes landed on it. The residual
mana signature pulsing from it wasn’t the usual energy a blue crystal held—it was different.

A faint layer of black mana—yin magic—coated the crystal, but it was already fading,
disappearing as quickly as it had appeared. Whatever spell had been cast to teleport was long
gone, leaving only this fleeting trace as evidence of its existence.

‘Damn, I would’ve loved to know what that spell was… Wouldn’t mind adding it to my
arsenal,’ he thought, irritation flickering in his mind.

Sure, he could teleport on his own, but learning this spell would’ve allowed him to enchant
items, giving his friends an escape route when trouble came knocking. He wouldn’t pass up
on the opportunity to add something like that to his arsenal.

‘No, don’t get distracted, Subaru. Focus.’ He pushed the thought aside and turned his
attention to the obvious question—who was behind this?

And really, there was only one likely suspect.

The loli spirit only cared about anything happening inside the mansion, which left only one
other yin magic user who had the knowledge and audacity to pull this off.

‘Roswaal… Yet another question to add to the ever-growing list. I don’t know what your
game is, clown, but you better have a damn good excuse for every single one of them.’

With a sigh, Subaru shoved the necklace into his pocket and turned his full focus to Emilia.

She lay there, her breathing slow and peaceful, her expression serene—almost untouched by
the chaos surrounding her. She looked like a princess, frozen in time, undisturbed by decay or
danger.

A small smile tugged at his lips as he reached out, gently pinching her cheek.

“You’ve been making me worried sick lately, Emi,” he murmured.

His gaze shifted, sweeping over the carriage—the mess, the wreckage, the signs of
disturbance. Yet, the space around Emilia was untouched, clean, as if someone had gone out
of their way to make sure she remained undisturbed.

‘I don’t know why the carriage ended up like this. Maybe it was the teleportation, maybe
something else. But one thing’s for sure—you sleeping comfortably must be because of
Otto…’

Subaru offered a small, grateful smile, directed toward the merchant. He barely knew them,
yet they had ensured Emilia's comfort.

As he recalled the merchant’s condition, he let out a deep sigh, the exhaustion in his breath
unmistakable. In less than half a day, he’d been through much—separation, an encounter with
a greedy, evil witch, and Otto getting beaten up. It was nothing short of chaos.



‘Good grief, I knew things would get hectic after my stunt in the capital, but I didn’t expect it
to be this bad… I’m starting to get tired of it all.’

From knights aiming to take his life to a whale and sloth attacking his home, a man his age
shouldn’t be caught up in all of this. But here he was.

“I hope the Sanctuary doesn’t turn out too badly… And I hope you wake up soon,” he
murmured, absentmindedly twirling a strand of Emilia’s hair between his fingers, his worried
eyes now directed at her.

Since their reconciliation, Emilia had been acting differently. Not withdrawn, exactly—but
there was a clear shift in her behavior.

She had become more focused, throwing herself into work, determined to contribute in any
way she could. During their temporary stay at Crusch’s estate, she had taken every
opportunity to assist wherever possible, always pushing herself to do more.

And whenever she made a mistake, she was quick to reprimand herself then correct it,
working even harder to ensure she wouldn’t slip up again.

While her determination was admirable, there was an underlying issue—whenever he, or
anyone else, offered to help, she would quickly and politely refuse, insisting she could handle
things on her own. And any worries she carried? She simply reassured that everything was
fine, even when it clearly wasn’t. Even resorting to lying.

As evident during the carriage ride to the Sanctuary, something weighed on her mind,
something that made her uneasy—yet she wouldn’t open up. Not to him. Not to Rem.

Subaru gazed at the sleeping beauty, his smile turning bittersweet as he gently squeezed her
hand.

“I don’t know what’s going on with you, Emi. I know I’ve said this a million times, but I’ll
always be by your side—when you laugh, when you cry, when you succeed, when you fail.
And I’ll always be here to help you.”

His grip tightened ever so slightly, his eyes locked on her sleeping face.

“Because, I…”

The words caught in his throat, lingering there before he slowly shook his head.

“No. The first time I say these words, you should be awake to hear them.”

Standing up from his seat next to Emilia, Subaru headed to the door leading outside, casting
one last glance at her before stepping through.

He rounded the corner and spotted his destination.

“Hey, Remmy, how’s Otto doing?”



“Otto-san is stable, Subaru-kun. Rem cannot heal him to full health, but she will do what she
can.”

There, on the same side where Otto had impacted the carriage, he lay motionless on the
ground. His cloak and shirt had been set aside, exposing his slightly toned upper body.

Kneeling on the ground, Rem sat in front of the merchant, her white-stocking-covered knees
pressing into the dirt. Her hands were outstretched, surrounded by a small glowing blue balls.

Subaru watched as mana flowed from Rem’s gate to her hands and then into Otto. The energy
sank into his flesh, filling it with power, accelerating the healing process, and closing up the
numerous wounds and bruises on his body.

Healing magic, regardless of its origin, would always be a marvel to him, and Rem was
skilled at it.

Not as skilled as Shoko Ieiri, though. That girl was a beast when it came to Reverse Cursed
Technique. She was even the one who “taught” him—if you call the random “fyo” and “hyi”
sounds she made.

“That’s a relief. Try and heal him as much as you can, Rem. He deserves it, but don’t push
yourself too hard, okay?”

“Of course, Subaru-kun!” she replied brightly, refocusing on the injured merchant. Her hands
hovered over the badly bruised and discolored right side of Otto

Seeing that Rem had everything under control, Subaru moved to the front of the carriage,
some distance away, Patrasche stood—alert, ready, and carrying out her guard duty with the
utmost diligence.

"Patrasche," Subaru called out, catching the ground-dragon's attention. "How's our resident
troublemaker doing? I hope he's behaving well."

"Kyaaa!" Patrasche responded in the affirmative, her gaze shifting to the figure sitting against
the tree, watching his every move.

Subaru followed her gaze. "So, your name is Garfiel, right?"

The man who had attacked Otto was none other than Garfiel—the one Frederica had warned
them about. He looked like he had seen better days, his bitter scowl reflecting his physical
condition.

He was in a rough shape—bruises covered his body, swelling distorted his features, and his
blackened eye looked especially nasty.

All of that damage came from Rem, who had made sure he paid for ruining her first ever kiss.
Had Subaru hadn’t stepped in, she might’ve left him in far worse shape.

Garfiel shifted slightly, glaring up at Subaru with a mix of pain and defiance. "Yea? Who th’
hell’s askin’? An’ how d’ya know my amazin’ self’s name anyway?"



Subaru blinked at the question. So did Patrasche. The two exchanged glances before looking
back at Garfiel, their movements oddly synchronized—almost as if rehearsed.

Garfiel didn’t like the way that bastard was staring at him. It Didn’t matter to him who that
man was, the way he looked at him, like he was some kinda clueless idiot, got under his skin.

"What’s with th’ damn look, huh?! Got somethin’ ta say?" he growled.

‘This guy seriously didn’t hear Rem yell his name?’ Subaru was used to stupidity, but this
was a new level of dumb.

Not wanting Garfiel’s short fuse to ignite again, Subaru cleared his throat and gave him the
simplest answer possible.

"Natsuki Subaru. Frederica told us about you before we got here."

Garfiel stiffened like he'd heard something impossible, his posture shifting as he got to his
feet. His glare sharpened, his lips pulling into a dangerous sneer, the sort that made it clear he
wasn’t above throwing fists first and asking questions later.

“Why th’ hell did I hear dat name off of ya nasty mouth? How th’ hell do ya know ma big
sister?”

'Great, now he's on guard. Just what I needed,' Subaru suppressed a sigh. Now, getting the
information he wants would be more difficult than before.

Seeing the open hostility, Patrasche stepped forward, a low rumble vibrating from her throat
as she glared at the demi-human, her protective instincts compelling her to shield her driver.

Subaru reached out, resting a hand on Patrasche’s head. Sensing his intent, she obeyed and
stood down, though her muscles remained tense with readiness. Satisfied, Subaru turned back
to Garfiel.

"Like I said, Frederica warned us about you—told us to ‘beware of Garfiel’—and now I
guess I know why," he said, watching the tension build between them.

"So..." He stepped closer, and Garfiel immediately stiffened, his body language turning
defensive.

"You’re going to answer every question I ask, starting with this: why the hell was Otto in the
state I found him in? And why were you about to attack Patrasche?"

Garfiel scoffed, unbothered. "I ain’t answering shi’. Ah don’t care who ya think ya are, but ah
ain’t scared o’ ya, ya hear me? Ya got a cheap shot at me—could snap ya like a twig if I
wanted!"

Subaru didn’t flinch. He simply took another step forward. "Good for you, then. I don’t care
if you’re afraid of me or not. I just want answers—answers only you can give—so you are
going to answer me."



"Or what?" Garfiel shot back, narrowing his eyes. "What if ah don’t? What’re ya gonna do
‘bout it?"

Subaru kept walking, closing the gap between them as Patrasche growled from behind.

Now face-to-face—or close to it. Garfiel had to crane his neck up slightly, a fact that visibly
irritated him as another low growl slipped out.

"Nothing," Subaru finally said. "In fact, I’d rather we have a civil conversation where I get
what I want, and you go on your way. But if you’re going to make this difficult..."

He let the words linger, leaning in slightly.

"...Then I’ll have to take drastic measures."

Garfiel glared at him, despite his beaten up condition he refused to back down, nor to be
talked down or disrespected like this. Rem was one thing, but this upstart? Absolutely not.

"Is that a threat?" Garfiel asked, his tone grave, hostility burning in his eyes. A faint red glow
flickered around him—his body itching for the fight to begin.

"A warning," Subaru replied flatly, uncaring. Still, his concealed eyes carefully tracked
Garfiel’s sudden surge of power.

In response, Subaru gathered just a bit of cursed mana, letting his right hand glow a dark
blue.

Why only his hand? Because that was all he needed to end this fight before it even started.
Even though Garfiel didn’t fully understand what the glow meant, he picked up on the
implication, his teeth baring in fury.

Now, they stood off—Garfiel, a cornered beast unwilling to back down, and Subaru, simply
looking for answers. Behind him, Patrasche stood ready, prepared to intervene at a moment's
notice.

They stared each other down, neither side yielding… until the sound of coughing drew their
attention.

Rem stood off to the side, regarding the standoff with a neutral look. "Subaru-kun, Rem has
finished healing Otto-san."

"He is? Good. You did a great job, Remmy," Subaru said, flashing her a bright smile.

Mirroring his expression, Rem did so with the same energy as his.

"...T’ hell?" Garfiel muttered, catching sight of the way Rem smiled at Subaru—genuine,
warm, unlike anything he'd seen before.

Hearing him, Rem turned her gaze toward the demi-human, her smile fading, replaced with a
flat look—one that reminded Subaru distinctly of Ram.



"Garfiel, it's been a while since we last met, but you're just as troublesome as Rem
remembers," she stated matter-of-factly.

"Eh? Wha—?" Garfiel grunted, taken aback.

Rem let out a sigh. "Garfiel, there’s no need for your stubbornness or your hostility. You
attacked Otto and put him in bad shape. Rem already taught you a lesson, so Subaru-kun
won’t hurt you. He just wants to ask a few questions."

She then turned to Subaru. "Subaru-kun, Garfiel can answer your questions on the way to the
sanctuary. Rem knows the direction, so she will drive the carriage, okay?"

Subaru paused for a moment before nodding. "Yeah, that would work… assuming he actually
cooperates, that is."

Faced with pressure from Rem and her vouching for Subaru, Garfiel begrudgingly stood
down. The reddish glow surrounding him flickered before disappearing entirely as he folded
his arms.

"Fine, fine! Just ‘cause ya asked me nicely, Rem," he grumbled, shooting a pointed glare at
Subaru. "Ya can go now. I’ll answer any questions ya got—but only the ones I wanna, deal?"

Subaru suppressed a sigh as he took a step back. "I guess that’s the best I can get out of
you… Fine, you have a deal."

As they prepared the carriage for travel and he and Rem worked to clean the interior, Subaru
couldn’t shake the nagging feeling in his gut. That Garfiel was going to be a real pain in the
ass to deal with in the future…

Why? Because of his first impression of Garfiel: hot-headed, stubborn—the type to punch
first and talk things out later.

He sincerely hoped he was wrong.

Chapter End Notes
