Chapter 49: Arc 4 - On-Road Interrogation &amp; Awakening
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

After some cleaning was done, the carriage’s interior now resembled what it looked like
before the unfortunate teleportation, all thanks to Subaru and Rem’s hard work.

Rem had gotten to the front seat, taking up the role of the driver who would guide them with
Patrasche, who was surprisingly eager to pull the carriage to its destination.

One thing Rem had told Subaru was that ground dragons thrive on physical labor and
especially love pulling carriages—it’s like a natural calling to them, the perfect activity to
showcase their prowess and magnificence. Patrasche confirmed this fact wholeheartedly.

Subaru felt his love for his ground dragon deepen. What more could he ask for in a
companion? Loyalty? Hard work? Intelligence? Patrasche had it all—an all-in-one package!

Otto was still unconscious as he was carried inside the carriage, laid down on one of the
couches. It wasn’t as spacious as the one Emilia rested on, but it was enough for him to feel
comfortable.

All of this happened in just a few minutes.

The carriage now moved along, having found the dirt road it had veered away from and was
back on track to reaching the Sanctuary.

Inside, Subaru and Garfiel sat. Otto and Emilia were close to each other but on separate seats.
Subaru took the smallest one—only big enough for a single person—and settled into it. To
his left was the sleeping Emilia, and below the window that opened to the driver sat Otto,
positioned to Emilia’s right.

The seating arrangement wasn’t random. Not only did they lay where they were most
comfortable, but they were also positioned behind Subaru, ready to be protected at a
moment’s notice should danger arise.

Subaru observed the arrangement and decided to position himself by the back door for the
rest of the trip, his typical grumpy expression settling in as he leaned against the wall.

They remained quiet for a few moments, with the only sounds being the wheels rolling over
the dirt road and the occasional bump from driving over a rock.

It wasn't a comfortable silence, as there was still tension lingering in the air between them,
which was understandable considering what had just happened—almost coming to blows
until Rem stepped in to ease the situation.

A smile crept onto Subaru's face as he recalled how Rem had intervened and made the
impulsive man agree to a compromise that left both parties satisfied.



‘Now that’s Remmy for ya,’ he chuckled to himself. ‘Cooking? Cleaning? Protecting?
Passionate? Understanding'? That’s all Remmy, the multi-talented maid!’ He gave Rem the
praise she truly deserves.

Indeed, Subaru holds Rem close to his heart, seeing her as someone who would stand by him
through thick and thin. They even almost kissed for goodness' sake! They would have gone
through with it if not for a certain someone…

“So what are you looking at?” Subaru asked, noticing how Garfiel’s gaze would sneakily
drift over to Emilia before quickly looking away, trying not to draw attention, which didn’t
work on him.

Garfiel let out a grunt as he stopped his sneaky glances and stared directly at Emilia, which
triggered Subaru’s protective instincts.

“Emilia, tha’ her? Th’ candidate for tha throne?” he inquired of the butler.

Subaru nodded, “Yeah, that’s Emilia alright. Why? Have you heard of her?” He raised an
eyebrow.

The sanctuary struck him as an isolated place, if the barrier and the forest were any
indication. So for someone to live there, he must not know about the royal selection or even
the royal family’s downfall. Therefore, he seriously doubts that Garfiel has heard of Emilia or
her candidacy for the throne.

Unless Roswaal or Ram had informed him.

Garfiel snorted as he narrowed his eyes at the sleeping beauty. “Oh yeah, hear’ all ‘bout her
plenty ‘lright. That clown wouldn’t shut up ‘bout the half-devil an’ the role she plays—”

A loud thud cut him off. He blinked, eyes flicking up to see Subaru standing over him, his
hand pressed against the metal above the door, fingers digging in slightly. His face was
twisted into a deep scowl.

“Half-elf, not half-devil. You don’t fucking get to insult her when she did nothing to you, got
that?” Subaru snapped, his voice sharp.

Garfiel might hate him—sure, he could hurl insults all day, no skin off his back. The opinions
of strangers? Worth about as much as wet tissue paper as a weapon against a special-grade
cursed spirit.

But insulting his friends? The people dear to him? Unjustly? That was a hard line no one
should cross.

Even still, Garfiel wasn’t intimidated. Even with the bruises from Rem’s lesson still aching,
even with Subaru standing over him like he’s got something to prove—he sneered, unphased,
clearly displeased by this attempt at intimidation.

“Really? She did nothin’ wrong, ya say? Oh no, she did plenty, alright! That devil’s the
reason we’re so deep in this shit! She’s th’ reason for all the problems in the world!” He



proclaimed, his voice cutting through the heavy air thick with tension.

Subaru gritted his teeth at Garfiel’s accusations.

Leaning in further, their foreheads nearly touching, the tension between them built up—so
thick it could be sliced clean with a blade.

“Listen here,” Subaru hissed, his tone sharp as a dagger. “I don’t know what your damn
problem is, and quite frankly, I don’t care. So I’ll tell you this just once—apologize, or you’ll
fucking regret it.”

Garfiel didn’t budge. The threat only fueled his frustration further.

“Oh yeah? I ain’t apologizin’ for shit! Do yer worst, asshole!”

The moment was a second away from igniting into a full-blown fight—until the sharp sound
of a window sliding open put an abrupt stop to it.

"Garfiel," Rem's voice cut through sharply, "You have gone too far now. Stand down and
apologize."

Garfiel didn’t back down like last time; instead, he protested, "No way! I ain’t gonna
apologize—"

"Garfiel," Rem said again, this time more stern and sharper than before, "Emilia-sama is the
lady that both Rem and Nee-sama serve loyally. To insult her would be to insult both of us.
What would Ram think when Rem tells her about your behavior?"

Garfiel felt like he gulped down an entire lemon, judging by the face he was making’ when
Ram was mentioned—something Subaru noticed.

"Grr… Fine! Fine! Ya win! My amazin’ self apologizes for callin’ that half-elf—"

"Emilia,"

Garfiel scowled but continued on, "Emilia a half-devil. Ther’, ya happy now?"

Subaru pursed his lips, stiffly noddin’ as he went back to his seat, shooting Rem a grateful
look, which she acknowledged with a slight smile before returning’ her focus to drivin’.

He could tell Garfiel wasn’t being sincere, but his unfair opinion seemed set in stone, so this
was the best he was gonna get outta him.

Subaru didn’t know what was truly wrong with him, for him to be this hostile toward them—
towards Emilia— when they did nothing wrong or endanger anybody.

But, he agreed to answer some questions Subaru had, and now was the time to ask ‘em.

"Why did you attack Otto?" Subaru started his question without wasting’ a moment’s notice.



Garfiel just clicked his tongue, knowing’ he had to answer now. "Tsk, ‘cause he’s an outsider,
what else?"

"So you just beat him up because he came from the outside? That’s enough justification for
him to end up in this state?" Subaru said, pointing’ to the unconscious Otto.

Garfiel scrunched his nose, "My amazin’ self just punched ‘im square in da jaw, ‘nocked ‘im
clean out. He was already roughed up by a Mabeast or somethin’ when I found ‘im."

Subaru scrutinized him for a moment before drifting back to Otto, recalling the injuries he
witnessed on that poor merchant. Then his gaze shifted back to Garfiel—more specifically
his fingernails. They were clean, absent of any blood.

Subaru had no reason to disbelieve him, and similarly, Garfiel was in a bad spot, so he had no
reason to lie.

"If you say so..." he hesitated before continuing, "What’s your role in the sanctuary? I take it
you’re some sort of guard or something?"

Garfiel just chuckled—a loud, rough one, the first time he’d done so since they met.

"My amazin’ self ain’t no guard, Ah’m way better than that! Name’s Garfiel Tinsel, shield of
da sanctuary! Ah protect it from outsiders or troublemakers like ya!" he proclaimed, pride
clear in his voice.

‘A proud hothead… What a lovely combination,’ Subaru could already foresee him being a
headache to deal with, as if their interaction less than five minutes ago was any indication.

But then, when he heard Garfiel’s full name, something struck him.

"Garfiel Tinsel? Isn’t your sister’s last name 'Baumann' or something?" he asked. He
surmised they were half-siblings, Their Od were similar, but not similar in the degree of Ram
and Rem, which was an indication that they were half-siblings but it didn’t hurt to confirm.

At the mention of his sister’s name, the proudness in Garfiel’s tone disappeared, replaced by
the gruff annoyance that had dominated their encounter.

"Yeah, an’? She’s my hal’ sister, so what ‘f we got different names? Does it even mattah t’
ya?" he snarled.

Subaru shook his head. "No, it doesn’t… I take it you guys are on bad terms?"

"Aggh! Ah ain’t answerin’ shit ‘bout my family, knock it off!"

"Alright, alright. No need to get angsty with me," Subaru raised his arm to soothe Garfiel and
backed off from that line of questioning, knowing it carried family drama—lest they end up
back at square one with him.

"Frederica mentioned that Roswaal is in the sanctuary, is that right? And how long has he
been there?" he inquired.



Garfiel scrunched his face for a moment before responding, "‘Bout three days, give or take. I
wasn’t really countin’ how long that bastard’s been there."

Subaru nodded as he absorbed the information and began to analyze it.

'Three days ago… Today’s the fourth day since Sloth attacked the domain. That means he
went to the sanctuary on the same day we evacuated…'

Subaru blinked at the implication he had just realized.

'Emilia mentioned that Roswaal was on business when I was in the capital. He hadn’t
returned when we were evacuating And Frederica told us he was already in the sanctuary
when we got back.'

'Did… Roswaal went to the sanctuary on the same day we evacuated? And if he did, then
how the hell did Roswaal know to go there? Is there some kind of contingency if an
evacuation was to happen? Did Ram leave a letter?'

Then an idea struck him, and just thinking about it made him furious, 'Was it all just a lie?
This whole "I’m on business" story? Did Roswaal… did that clown know about an attack
from an Archbishop and do nothing to prevent it? Did he leave on purpose, knowing what
was about to happen?’

‘Is Roswaal part collaborating with Witch Cult?! Is he a part of it?!'

If that were true… then forget about him being his feudal master; he would genuinely kill
him, without hesitation, regardless of the future problems that might arise.

But if he did that, then Emilia’s candidacy would be at risk, as he was her only sponsor…

'Calm down, Subaru. There has to be a reasonable explanation for all of this. There must be
one. Maybe Ram wrote him a letter; I sent Rem to inform the mansion before the force
arrived… Maybe Roswaal found the letter, read it, and went to the sanctuary afterward… but
that still doesn’t explain everything.'

It wasn’t a complete explanation, but Subaru hoped that the latter was the truth. That this was
all just a massive misunderstanding and that despite how shady the clown could be at times,
he was innocent of it all.

Because if the former turned out to be true…

He didn’t want to believe that he had been playing all of them for whatever purpose that
clown might have.

Through his inner musings and mounting anger, Subaru maintained a stoic expression as he
pressed on with the interrogation.

"‘That bastard?’ I assume you’re not fond of Roswaal?" Subaru sensed that Garfiel held a
negative view of the clown and decided to pursue that line of questioning.



"Absolutely not! That bastard’s the reason for all da mess happenin’ in th’ Sanctuary! He’s
made our lives miserable! Ah’d break ‘im in two if Ah could!" he shouted, his tone having an
angry tone to it.

Subaru was taken aback by such a passionate response. "Wow, you really don’t like him that
much? Did he do something to the Sanctuary?"

Garfiel hesitated for a moment, then shook his head gently, reverting to his usual grumpy
demeanor. "Neva mind. Ah ain’t gonna answer ya."

Subaru blinked "Why not? Did Roswaal do something?" He pressed on, eager to uncover
more details about Roswaal or the sudden reason for Garfiel’s reluctance to continue.

"Ah said Ah ain't gonna answer, Ah refuse to respond to any more questions, clear?" he
huffed.

Subaru frowned slightly, ‘Why not? Why won’t you keep going, Garfiel? We were making
progress, but the mention of Roswaal doing something to the Sanctuary made you stop?
Why?’

Subaru understood that he and Garfiel had an agreement, that Garfiel could cease answering
whatever questions he wanted, and Subaru was the kind of person who respected deals with
others.

However, Subaru couldn’t respect this one; he needed to extract more information, even if it
meant risking a confrontation with him.

Subaru opened his mouth to speak, but the soft, low sound of groaning captured his full
attention.

He turned to his left, and what he saw brought him relief. The sound was emanating from the
unconscious half-elven beauty, her lips slightly parted as the sound escaped from them.

Subaru shook her shoulders gently, trying to wake her up. His voice was gentle as he called to
her “Emilia, Emilia. It’s me, Subaru, wake up!”

Slowly, Emilia’s eyes fluttered before opening, her amethyst gaze unfocused as she stared at
the blurred silhouette of Subaru’s face.

Gradually, her eyes regained its focus, and his smiling face finally came into view. Her mind
stirred from its slumber, recognizing the ever-cheerful butler.

"S… S—Subaru...?" she murmured, her voice soft like silver bells. To Subaru, it sounded
almost like a siren's call.

"Yes, Emilia, it’s me! Natsuki Subaru, the greatest butler in the world! Here, let me help you
sit up," he said, carefully helping her into a seated position.

"What… What happened?" Emilia asked, her voice laced with dizziness as she struggled to
regain her bearings. Her movements were sluggish, her body still recovering.



"What happened?" he echoed, concern flickering across his face. "You don’t remember
anything, Emilia?" Did she hit her head When she was on the floor? 

"N-no, I—I do remember… The necklace—it was shining reeeeally brightly. I remember
feeling scared and confused… Then, everything just went black." She frowned, frustration
settling in as she tried to recall anything beyond that.

Subaru let out a relieved sigh—no memory loss. For a brief moment, he had feared the worst,
but with everyone now together and in good condition—or stable in Otto’s case—he could
finally put his heart to rest.

Now, the only thing left to deal with was Roswaal and getting the villagers back where they
belonged.

"That necklace knocked you out and teleported all of us away. It took some time, but we
finally reunited. We’re now on our way to the sanctuary," he explained.

"Knocked me out...?" she repeated, a deepening frown forming. Her hands instinctively went
to search for the troublesome necklace, but it was nowhere to be found.

"Eh? Where did it go? It was right here…"

"I took it away, Emilia. That thing was nothing but trouble," he said, hoping to ease her
concerns.

She looked at him, and he returned her gaze with a reassuring smile. Emilia offered him a
small smile in return, but then she noticed they weren’t alone in the carriage.

Her amethyst eyes shifted to the back, where she spotted a half-naked blonde demi-human
with messy, spiky golden hair, sharp teeth, and striking emerald eyes. His appearance vaguely
reminded her of someone, but her half-awakened mind couldn’t quite place who. They locked
eyes for a brief moment before he clicked his teeth and turned away with a huff.

Emilia felt a pang of disappointment at being disregarded like that. It reminded her of the
way people so often looked at her—like something to be feared, to be avoided. Her half-elf
heritage had always drawn prejudice, no matter how much she tried to prove herself.

Still, despite the dismissive attitude, Emilia was a kind-hearted person. And with Subaru’s
and Puck’s tutelage on making a good first impression, she set out to introduce herself
properly and get into the good graces of the boy in front of her.

“Hello there. I don’t think we’ve met before. My name is Emilia, just Emilia—no last name.
Can I have yours?” she asked, her tone soft and inviting.

“Shaddub, don’t talk to me,” Garfiel responded gruffly, refusing to meet her gaze.

Emilia’s expression faltered at the rejection, her eyes dropping slightly as an old, familiar
sting settled in her heart. No matter how many times it happened, it still hurt just the same.



Subaru pressed his lips into a thin line, irritation flashing across his face. As much as he
wanted to smack some manners into Garfiel, he restrained himself for Emilia’s sake.

With a sigh, he took it upon himself to introduce them. “Emilia, this is Garfiel, Shield of the
Sanctuary. Garfiel, this is Emilia—the candidate for the throne of the Kingdom of Lugunica.”

Garfiel didn’t respond, continuing to ignore the half-elf, but Emilia chose not to dwell on it.

No, her mind was replaying the events that had happened earlier that day—her meeting with
Frederica after she returned, their conversation before she left, and, most importantly, the
warning she had given.

"Beware of Garfiel,"  

Which meant that this Garfiel person was dangerous enough for Frederica to warn her about
him.

And now, here he was—sitting in the same carriage… the very same one that Subaru was in.

Whether it was because she wasn’t fully awake or because her instincts urged her to protect
Subaru from harm, the outcome remained the same—Emilia shot up from her seat and
positioned herself between the boy and Subaru, her arms spread wide in defense.

"Stay back! Don’t get close!" she shouted, determination hardening her features as she
addressed the boy, startling both Subaru and Garfiel.

"What the fuck?! I ain’t done nothin’ to ya!" Garfiel shot back.

"I don’t care! You’re dangerous! Veeeery dangerous! I can’t let you get close, or else I’ll have
to—"

"Emilia!"

Subaru’s sharp voice cut through her panic, stopping her mid-sentence. She turned, meeting
his slightly stern gaze—a gaze that made her heart sting for the second time that day.

“Stop it, Emilia. Just stop. Garfiel won’t hurt anyone.”

"B-but Subaru! That’s Garfiel! The one Frederica warned us about! He must be dangerous!"

"No, Emilia, he isn’t. Not anymore. Just take a good look at him, okay? Does he look like in
any condition to pose a threat to us?" he said, gesturing toward Garfiel.

She did—and her eyes widened slightly.

Bruises littered his body, some small, others far nastier, particularly one that stood out on his
cheek. Yet despite it all, he remained standing, still scowling at her.

“Oh, y—you're injured. But I thought you were—what happened to you…?” she asked,
concern creeping into her voice.



“Garfiel will be fine, Rem merely taught him a valuable lesson, Emilia-sama,” came Rem’s
response, answering the half-elf’s inquiry before Garfiel could.

“Rem?” Emilia’s silver-bell voice rang as she turned toward the window, where Rem’s face
appeared.

Rem smiled warmly at her. “It’s good to talk to you again, Emilia-sama. It truly puts Rem’s
heart at ease, knowing that you are finally awake.”

“Rem…” Emilia whispered, touched by the girl’s concern. But the tender moment was
abruptly cut short as her gaze drifted below the window—where she saw Otto, looking worse
for wear.

“Otto?! What happened to him?! Is he okay?” she exclaimed, rushing to his side. She nudged
him gently, trying to rouse him—but he remained still.

Her amethyst eyes scanned his body for injuries, worry tightening in her chest as she took in
his condition. A deep bruise darkened his ribs, and his jaw hung slack, making her wince at
the sight.

“Don’t worry, Emilia-sama,” Rem reassured her. “Rem healed Otto-san to the best of her
ability. There is still more work to be done, but he will recover soon.”

But then, Rem’s eyes narrowed at the culprit—who refused to meet her gaze.

“But someone caused all of that damage to Otto-san… Someone that Rem personally
‘educated’ and ensured would never do it again.”

Emilia followed Rem’s gaze and turned toward the perpetrator.

“Garfiel-san?”

“Yeah, him,” Subaru answered. “That necklace teleported all of us away, separating us. Me
and Rem reunited quickly before tracking you guys.. By the time we found you, Garfiel and
Otto were…” he paused for a moment, choosing his words carefully.

“In the middle of a scuffle. But like she said, Rem made sure he learned his lesson,” Subaru
said, casting Garfiel a look—the blonde simply clicked his tongue in response.

Then, Subaru gently placed a hand on Emilia’s shoulder and guided her back to her seat.

“You can relax, Emilia. Everything has been taken care of, so you don’t have to worry.”

“…”

Emilia didn’t reply to Subaru—she simply nodded stiffly, her expression passive despite the
storm raging inside her.

She had made a quiet promise to never be a burden, to put forth her utmost effort, to prove
her worth—not just to Subaru, but to herself.



She was tired. That much was undeniable. She was afraid. That was only natural. But making
others worry about her? That was something she refused to do. Those fears, those struggles—
they were hers alone to bear.

Yet, when disaster struck their group—when she should have stepped up and led—what did
she do?

Nothing.

Just like always, Subaru had undoubtedly been the one to fix everything. He had a knack for
it, after all.

And she?

She was knocked out and rendered defenseless. Like some helpless princess waiting to be
rescued, contributing nothing.

She had barely even started and had already failed to be of any real use.

Her gaze drifted toward Subaru, catching the soft smile on his lips as he told her to relax.

Was he… pitying her? Was he acknowledging her effort while simultaneously reassuring her
that, even if she had been awake, she wouldn’t have been able to do anything anyway?

The thought made her chest tighten painfully. The urge to curl up and cry threatened to
overwhelm her—but she shoved those feelings down.

Because they only reinforced what Subaru already thought of her.

“…I have some contracts with minor water spirits. I… I could heal Otto-san a little before we
arrive.”

“You do?” he asked, his eyebrows lifting slightly. Was he actually surprised that she had such
a skill?

“Well, if you think you can help him, then be my guest. All the better for him.”

‘If? Think?’ Did he doubt her? Was this how Subaru saw her? A useless doll incapable of
doing anything on her own?

Emilia nodded, moving to Otto’s unconscious form. She held out her hands as small blue
orbs emerged around her, responding to her call. She beckoned them to channel healing
mana, doing whatever she could to mend his wounds.

But while she was working on healing him, her mind was onto something else entirely.

‘This—This won’t stop me! I promised not to be a burden, and I won’t break that promise!
No matter how hard it gets, no matter how painful—it doesn’t matter. Subaru never showed
any weakness, and I won’t either! I’ll prove to him that I can stand beside him through
everything and show that I’m his equal!’



With renewed conviction, Emilia pushed forward, refusing to back down in her fight for
recognition. For Subaru’s recognition. To not be his inferior and to stand beside him as his
equal.

But unbeknownst to her, when the fall came, it would be utterly devastating.

Chapter End Notes

Emilia's on her self-destruction road, hopefully she doesn't crash and burn



Chapter 50: Arc 4 - A (Not So) Warm Welcoming
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"Emilia-sama, Subaru-kun, Garfiel, we’ve arrived," Rem announced from the driver’s seat,
popping her head out of the window to inform the carriage’s occupants.

Hearing the announcement, Subaru stretched out widely in his seat, letting out an
exaggerated sigh.

"Finally! We’re at that stupid place! Honestly, with all the crap we went through, you’d think
we were chasing after an ancient treasure and not some backwater village no one’s heard of!"
he said loudly.

"Subaru! Language, please—" Emilia tried to reprimand him, but her words overlapped with
a louder voice.

Garfiel let out a low growl, clearly offended by Subaru’s remark. "Oi! Watch yer mouth!
That’s my home, ya hear me?! I don’ wanna hear ya slanderin’ it with that filthy tongue o’
yers!" he shouted at him.

Subaru didn’t acknowledge Garfiel, simply standing up and opening the side window,
pointing outside while deliberately ignoring the angry demi-human who was less than three
steps away.

Garfiel was volatile and stubborn, and whenever he was pissed, things tended to spiral into
threats or even an all-out brawl. Engaging with him now would only make things worse, so
Subaru pointedly ignored him, keeping his focus on the outside.

Being disregarded like that sent Garfiel’s anger boiling over. His fists clenched tighter, his
sharp teeth gritted, and his eyes sharpened, fixing on Subaru’s figure with heated frustration.

Never.

Never in his life had he been ignored and disrespected like this. Not once had it ever
happened to him, and the fact that it was coming from an outsider—someone from the same
type of people that had ruined his life—only made it worse.

And this was the third time. Two times had come from Subaru.

Seeing how angry Garfiel was getting, Emilia decided to be the camp leader she was
supposed to be and stepped in to smooth things over with the boy before something bad
happened.

"Umm, Garfiel-san. I understand you might be angry, Subaru can sometimes be impolite—"



The moment her soft, light voice reached his ears, Garfiel’s emerald eyes snapped toward
Emilia’s amethyst ones, causing her to flinch slightly at how fast he turned to her.

"Ughhh! Yer so annoyin’! Shut yer mouth! Yer th’ last person whose voice ah wanna hear,
‘sides that asshole!" he shouted at her.

Emilia was taken aback that his anger was directed at her—she had only been trying to calm
things down, yet she was met with hostility. 

She still didn’t understand why he was so rude to her when she had done nothing to wrong
him. She was just trying to get them both to get along, so what is it that she did wrong—

…It’s because of her heritage, isn’t it?

Right. It’s always that. Why was she even questioning it? The answer was clear as day. He
hadn’t even met her eyes when he first saw her—for goodness’ sake!

She really is stupid, isn’t she?

Emilia would have felt sad or dismayed, but she swallowed hard and crushed that feeling,
refusing to let it take hold of her or dictate her actions. 

‘Subaru never showed any weaknesses, so neither should I’ Emilia reasoned to herself.

She had just renewed her promise, had just reaffirmed her conviction—she would not back
down from it.

"Garfiel," she said, forgoing the "san" honorific, her tone carrying a slight firmness.

"That is a rude and unfair thing to say. I have been reeeeeally nice and courteous with you so
far, so I ask that you treat me with the same respect I have shown you."

Garfiel stared at her before snorting loudly. "What’s this? Ya finally grew a backbone? Good
for ya. But guess what, ‘Princess’? Ya can shove yer ‘respect’—I’ll treat ya however I like!"

Emilia’s lips thinned as she absorbed his response. It stung—It always does, but despite that,
she refused to back down and roll over. Circumstances have changed and she’s now going to
prove herself.

"Emilia," she heard Subaru call her, cutting her off mid-sentence. She turned and saw him
looking at her, then at Garfiel.

For a moment, the air felt heavy, pressing against her shoulders. She let out an involuntary
shudder. But when she looked at Garfiel, she noticed something different.

The hair on his body seemed to be standing on end, his arms crossed but trembling slightly.
His scowl, once full of raw anger, now had something else—his breaths were shallow, his
entire body shaking just slightly.



She turned again, seeing Subaru staring right at Garfiel, and Garfiel staring right back. But
unlike before, his glare lacked its usual fire—there was hesitation, caution.

Then, just as suddenly, the weight in the air lifted, the suffocating pressure evaporating.
Garfiel let out a quiet breath, one he probably wasn’t even aware of, though his expression
remained unchanged.

Subaru turned back to her.

"Just ignore him, Emilia. Talking to this guy is like talking to a brick wall; you just won’t get
anywhere with him," he told her, then gestured to the window.

"Come here, I can see the sanctuary now. You should take a look."

Emilia turned back to Garfiel, expecting him to explode, to fire back, to insult Subaru like he
always did. But nothing came.

No rage. No shouting. Just a small, scornful scowl on his bruised face. Nothing more.

Subaru had subdued Garfiel with just one look—no, not even a look. He just turned his head
in Garfiel’s general direction, and that was enough for the stubborn boy.

‘How? How did Subaru do that? Did it have something to do with that weird feeling in the
air? Is that it? His trick?’ she wondered.

Regardless of what it was, it only proved how amazing Subaru truly was—able to control and
assert his authority in any situation with just a slight movement of the head. And he’d had his
sunglasses on the whole time, not even unleashing his beautiful eyes on anybody.

This simply meant she had to work twice as hard to reach his level.

Complying with Subaru’s request, Emilia stepped beside him, her gaze following him toward
the open window.

Outside, she beheld the so-called "Sanctuary"—a village hidden deep within the Lost Forest
of Kremaldy, primarily inhabited by demi-humans.

Her breath hitched as she took in the sight, eyes widening slightly with every new detail that
became clearer as the carriage rolled forward.

The village was in a rough state. The houses and buildings, worn and crumbling, looked as
though they had been abandoned only recently. Dirt-streaked windows—some shattered—
stood as silent witnesses to the decay, yet people still lived within these structures.

Plant life flourished despite the poor conditions, vines creeping over wood and stone
unchecked, weaving a blanket of greenery across the neglected surfaces. But its growth was
less a sign of thriving nature and more of slow, unchallenged encroachment.

The land itself bore signs of neglect—rough, uneven, unplowed. No cobblestone roads lined
the village pathways, only bare dirt stretched beneath them, a stark contrast to the standard



seen in most villages.

As the carriage entered what seemed to be the central plaza, the scene remained unchanged.
The buildings matched the state of the ones before them—worn, brittle, and fading with time.
Market stalls stood abandoned, remnants of livelihoods now left to decay.

And then, there were the villagers.

Rem had told them earlier that the Sanctuary was one of the rare settlements where demi-
humans lived in significant numbers. Such communities were uncommon in this world, with
most attempts at establishing larger, independent settlements meeting varying degrees of
failure—the most infamous being the demi-human civil war decades ago.

These people should have been considered the fortunate few, able to live alongside their own
kind.

But their expressions told a different story.


They gazed at the carriage as it rolled past, its opulence undeniable—grand, polished, and
unmistakably expensive. As expected, given that a royal candidate rode within.

Yet, instead of awe or curiosity, the eyes fixed upon it reflected something far darker.

Hatred. Fear.

The adults, dressed in worn, inexpensive clothing, their appearances slightly disheveled, did
not look upon the carriage with admiration. Their gazes were heavy with disdain, eyes
burning with anger and contempt.

These were the same glares that abused peasants cast toward oppressive lords—resentful,
bitter stares aimed at those who paraded their wealth and superiority so shamelessly.

Then there was the other reaction. Fear.

A minority of the villagers, mostly children, shrank away as the carriage passed. Some fled
entirely, while others clung tightly to their parents’ legs.

But their fear wasn’t directed at nobles. They were too young to grasp such notions.

No, the source of their terror was the half-elf peeking out from the window. The reason
behind their trembling was so obvious, it didn’t require explanation.

“I gotta say, this place... Whoever came up with the name ‘Sanctuary’ must’ve had a real
sense of humor,” Subaru said from beside Emilia, surveying the scene with a deepening
frown.

“It’s just like the slums back in the capital. Remember how that place looked last time we
went there, Emilia?”

“…"



Silence.

Subaru’s question hung in the air, unanswered.

He turned his head, eyes landing on Emilia. She stared out at the scenery, unmoving,
expression blank. Her face revealed nothing. Her eyes echoed that emptiness.

She was elsewhere—lost in thought.

“Emilia?” Subaru murmured, nudging the half-elf beside him. The gentle push seemed to do
the trick as she blinked, snapping out of her trance and turning her attention toward him.

“Uh, Subaru? Is something wrong? Did you say something?” she asked, her voice carrying
faint traces of confusion.

Subaru shook his head. “No, I was talking to you, but you were spaced out. Everything
alright?”

Emilia registered his question and gave a quick shake of her head. “Yes, I’m fine, Subaru.
Nothing is wrong. Why do you ask?”

“Well…” Subaru glanced out the window for a moment before looking back at her. “This
place doesn’t exactly… feel welcoming.”

Subaru had sharp perception—his instincts honed by experience, strengthened by his
hereditary trait from the Gojo clan—the six eyes. And he could tell, without a doubt, that the
demi-human villagers did not welcome them, especially Emilia. The glares sent her way were
pointed and harsh, making it painfully clear she wasn’t wanted here.

He understood their resentment. He knew why they reacted this way. But that didn’t make it
any less infuriating.

Judging someone for something they had no control over—condemning Emilia simply
because she resembled that infamous witch without bothering to see how truly kind, gentle,
and incredible she was—was an injustice Subaru could never abide.

Unfairness sat alongside cruelty in the list of things Subaru despised, especially when it was
his friends who suffered because of it.

And Emilia… had faced this treatment for her entire life. Not even her royal candidacy status
shielded her from it. That much had been evident during the royal selection commendation
ceremony. Even among nobles, prejudice showed no respect for rank.

That’s why he asked.

Because he knew Emilia too well. Knew that she was easily disheartened by such scorn. And
that, no matter how much she tried to stay strong, such rejection—again and again—would
always weigh heavy on her heart and—

“Subaru, you don’t have to keep worrying about me over everything. I’ll be fine.”



Her voice pulled Subaru from his thoughts, snapping him back to reality.

“Emilia…” he said, looking over at her. Her amethyst eyes held a rare determination—one he
had only seen on rare occasions, like when she commanded him during Milie’s attack on
Alarm Village.

“I know that, Emilia. But I just can’t help but feel worried about you, especially after
everything that happened recently,” he admitted.

Emilia sucked in a breath and exhaled, her eyes still determined but softened. “I know,
Subaru. I know. Lots of really scaaaary stuff happened recently, and it made you worried
about everyone. But you don’t have to keep worrying or fretting over me.”

She looked outside the window, noticing how some people stared at her.

“I know how these people view me. Arlam Village used to treat me the same way when they
thought I was just an evil witch.”

She then turned toward Subaru, her eyes filled with conviction and determination. “They’re
scared of me, probably even hate me. But I know I can change their view, just like I did
before.”

She locked her gaze onto his sunglasses, knowing that behind them, he was meeting her eyes
directly.

“I’m asking you to stop worrying about me and to give me the chance to prove myself—to
prove to everyone that I’m Emilia. Just Emilia. Not the evil witch of envy, but a candidate
who will win the royal selection and achieve her dreams.”

Emilia boldly delivered her declaration, her amethyst eyes seeming to burn with
determination and conviction. She wanted to show everyone that she was not a fragile doll,
but a capable leader who could overcome obstacles and fix everything without showing
weakness.

And to prove that she was worthy of standing beside Subaru as his equal.

Subaru remained silent as he stared at her, taking in the conviction burning in her eyes and
the seriousness and determination in her voice.

“…Emilia, please explain to me how you're so adorable at times. I swear, I just wanna pinch
your cheeks so bad!” Subaru cooed at the half-elf.

If Garfiel hadn’t been standing here near them, he would’ve definitely gone for it.

“Subaruuuu!” Emilia’s determined expression immediately vanished, replaced by the
adorable pout he loved so much. Her cheeks flushed slightly.

“Hehe, sorry~” he said, with absolutely no sincerity in his tone.



“But,” he added, his voice shifting ever so slightly into something more serious, prompting
Emilia to drop her childlike demeanor.

“Emilia, if this is really what you want, then I have no choice but to respect your wishes,” he
told her.

“I know you said I shouldn’t worry, but sometimes I just can’t help it. I care about you—a
lot, you know?… I’ll do as you say, but please, if something’s wrong, something you can’t
handle, tell me, okay? I’ll do whatever I can to help.”

Emilia paused. Normally, she would be overjoyed to have Subaru’s unwavering support. He
was a dear friend—someone close to her.

But right now… she didn’t feel happy about it.

After all, how could she prove herself if she told him her struggles, only for him to step in
and fix everything like he always did?

No. Emilia would do this on her own. Without showing weakness. Without asking for help.

“…Of course. You’re my friend, after all.”

With great hesitation, she pushed out those words, ensuring Subaru would trust her.

She… lied to his face.

Watching this exchange from the sidelines, Garfiel couldn’t help but have the most sour,
scrunched-up expression on his bruised face. The same type of face one would make if they
ate the world’s most sour lemon ever.

‘So that half-devil thinks she can jus’ waltz righ’ in an’ change everyboda’s mind ‘bout her?
Hah! Fat chance ‘n hell sh’ would do that! That clown an’ this bitch is the cause of all our
trouble!’

Garfiel was about as blunt as his personality and would’ve loved to tear into the half-witch
right then and there, to tell her what he truly thought of her and her stupid “conviction.”

But he, with great reluctance, bit his tongue and held himself back, all because of the man
standing beside Emilia, the one Garfiel was side-eyeing with disdain.

He didn’t know what it was, but back then, he felt great pressure washing over him,
suffocating him, making him unable to say a word or move, lest he felt like he would die on
the spot. He could only watch weakly as Subaru just gave him a look hidden underneath
those black things he wears on his eyes.

Garfiel felt his anger and hatred toward Subaru increase because of that.

He really wanted to tear into that man bit by bit, but Rem was in the way, and he’d have to
deal with that clown, which was even worse than him. So he would have to tolerate him for
now.



The carriage then slowly came to a stop, the world outside the window now coming to a still.
The sound of the sliding window came, and Rem was peeking through.

“We’re finally here. We can leave now,” Rem announced from the driver’s seat.

Emilia and Subaru looked at each other.

“Guess we’re here then. Let’s go.”

Subaru opened the sliding door, stepping onto the dirt. He turned and helped Emilia step out
of the carriage, then looked at his surroundings.

They were standing in front of a house, one that looked bigger and better maintained than any
other building in the Sanctuary. If he had to guess, this building would be the town hall or the
house where the head of the village resided.

But what drew his attention were two figures standing in front of it.

A woman with pink-colored hair and red eyes, wearing a maid outfit that matched the attire
of a certain blue-haired maid. This was none other than Ram—Rem’s older sister.

Standing beside her was another individual, shorter than Ram, her height reaching just past
Ram’s shoulder. Her hair was pink like Ram’s, but much longer, cascading down her back.
Her blue eyes were visible beneath the large black robe that covered nearly everything—even
her lower face. In her hand, she gripped a massive staff, comically oversized compared to her
frame.

What stood out most to him were her ears—pointed, much like a certain silver-haired
individual standing right beside Subaru.

‘Is this loli an elf? Or a half-elf?… Her pointy ears look similar in length to Emilia’s, so she’s
probably the latter,’ he thought.

It was quite the surprise for him. Elves were among the most discriminated groups in the
world, thanks to a certain witch. Many were forced into hiding or isolated communities just
to survive.

Still, it made sense—if an elf sought peaceful refuge, then a demi-human settlement was the
logical place to be.

By now, it was practically a habit for him whenever he encountered someone new—
analyzing them with his six eyes to gain a proper assessment of their strength and potential
threat.

She had… well, normal mana reserves, and her gate’s strength was average at best. Really,
she posed no threat should she become a foe later down the road. But that wasn’t what
mattered most. His gaze lingered on the state of her Od.

It wasn’t natural. It didn’t have a predetermined shape, just morphing and moving like an
amoeba. There was barely any spiritual energy inside of it, and whatever remained seemed



desperate to flee—yet it was contained, trapped within a layer of mana that kept it locked
inside.

A containment spell was suppressing the energy, but it appeared nearly depleted. And the
energy itself… didn’t belong to her body. That was why it was trying to escape.

‘An artificial Od… I swear, This is getting weirder and weirder by the day.’ he noted.

The spirit of a perverted witch persevered in a pseudo-domain, a demi-human village with a
hypocritical name, isolated deep within a forest infamous for being dangerous, and now an
artificial half-elf.

Seriously, what the hell is this place? And who the hell came up with it?

All of this registered in mere moments as Subaru stepped forward, flashing a smile so bright
that his pearly white teeth reflected the sunlight, momentarily blinding those who looked
directly at him. He raised a hand in greeting.

“Rammy! It’s good to see you again! I can't believe this is the fourth day since we’ve seen
each other. Such a long time apart made my heart hurt in agony! How have you been?!” he
called out enthusiastically.

Ram simply stared at him with her signature stoic, flat expression—the one she always wore,
especially when dealing with him.

“Barusu,” she began, tone as dry as the desert, “You were supposed to get here sooner. Did it
seriously take you this long? Just how useless can you be? As your senior maid, Ram has
decided your punishment is that you’re banned from eating her famous steamed tatos from
now on.”

“Harsh!” Subaru yelped in exaggerated despair.

Hopping down from the driver’s seat, Rem rushed toward her pink-haired twin, her face
lighting up with joy.

“Nee-sama!” she called out excitedly.

Hearing her sister's excited shout, Ram’s stony façade softened. She allowed herself a small
smile—not nearly as bright as Rem’s, but carrying a deep warmth.

“Rem. Ram can finally be happy now that she has her sissy back,” she said as they embraced.

Subaru watched the exchange with a childish pout.

“Rammy, would it really kill you to greet me like that too? Your cold shoulder is tearing my
delicate heart to shreds!”

Hearing Subaru’s pathetic whining, Ram pulled away from Rem just long enough to give him
a flat stare



“So Barusu admits that Ram is the loveliest being in the world? That he desperately craves
her hug just to bask in her divine magnificence? Tsk. What a deplorable, degenerate pervert."

“H-huh?! How the hell did you even reach that conclusion?! I really don’t understand how
your head works sometimes…”

“Nee-sama, nee-sama! You shouldn’t be too hard on Subaru-kun—he’s just so happy to see
you!” Rem chimed in, always ready to defend him.

Ram, without even looking, replied, “Rem, Rem… Ram couldn’t help but notice that you’ve
been sticking up for Barusu quite a lot lately.” She turned, narrowing her visible eye at her
younger twin. “He hasn’t done anything inappropriate to Ram’s little sister, has he? He
hasn’t... charmed you?”

As Ram uttered her words, Rem’s mind flashed back to her moment with Subaru in the forest
—where she had nearly locked lips with his delectable ones. Her face flushed deep red.

“N-no! Subaru-kun has done nothing to Rem! He’s still the hands—uh, the respectful
gentleman he’s always been! Yes!” she blurted out, scrambling.

Ram eyed her suspiciously, making Rem shrink back.

“So you’re absolutely sure that this lecherous Barusu didn’t do something scandalous?
Absolutely sure?” she pressed.

Ram bombarded her with more questions, forcing Rem into a desperate flurry of denials—
both eager to ease her sister’s suspicions and terrified to let slip her true feelings as Rem
hadn't yet tell her sister about her love for Subaru. Meanwhile, Subaru and Emilia stood off to
the side, quietly watching.

Subaru grinned to himself, thoroughly enjoying Rem’s flustered and panicked reactions,
while Emilia looked on in amused confusion.

“I don’t understand? Did something happen that I don’t know about?”

“Don’t worry your pretty little head—I’ll tell you when you’re older.”

“Hey! I’m a hundred years older than you! Tell me!”

Subaru smirked at her demand—her adorable side coming to life once again—but just then,
the mysterious girl standing beside Ram stepped forward to greet them.

“Greetings. Welcome to the Sanctuary,” the girl said, her tone flat as she gave a slight bow.
“My name is Ryuzu Alma, I am the caretaker of the sanctuary. It’s a pleasure to finally meet
you, Emilia-sama and Natsuki-sama.”

Emilia blinked, “You already know our names?”

“Indeed,” Ryuzu replied. “Roswaal-sama informed us of your arrival ahead of time.”



“Oh really? He did?” Subaru tilted his head. “How many people knew we were coming?”

“He told me directly, and at his request, I announced it to the entire village. So everyone in
the Sanctuary should already be aware of you two,” she explained.

Subaru nodded absently, his thoughts spinning. ‘If they knew about us, then why were they
so cold and hostile? Did Roswaal do something to antagonize them? Is that why they don’t
like us?'

His mind flicked back to Garfiel’s words about Roswaal—the way he supposedly made their
lives miserable. The pieces of the puzzle were lining up, and none of them painted a pretty
picture.

“Regardless, do you happen to know where young Gar is? He was out on patrol in the
forest…”

“Ah’m right here, hag,” a gruff voice rang out as Garfiel stepped forward, scowling.

Ryuzu’s eyes widened slightly as she took in his injuries and rough appearance. “Young Gar,
what happened to you?” she asked, concern seeping into her tone..

Subaru and Emilia exchanged glances—this was going to be awkward to explain to her,
especially since she seemed close to Garfiel, judging by that nickname.

Fortunately, the cutest maid in the world stepped in to save the moment.

“Rem is responsible for his injuries,” she announced, regaining her composure and drawing
everyone’s attention.

“Garfiel attacked and badly injured Otto-san without justification, so Responsible Rem had to
teach him a lesson to make sure he doesn’t repeat that mistake.”

Ram tilted her head at the unfamiliar name. “Who’s that?”

Emilia answered, “Otto Suwen—that’s his name. He’s a merchant looking to join our camp,
and he’s here with us to discuss it with Roswaal.”

“Is that so?” Ram mused, then turned to Garfiel. “And Garf is the one who gave him a
beating?”

“Ah had to! He was an outsider, an’ my amazin’ self didn’t know his motives, so ah dealt
with ‘im!” Garfiel protested. Then, his expression twisted into a pout. “Yer little sister hurt
me bad, Ram. Don’t ya got somethin’ ta say to ‘er?”

Ram simply huffed. “If sissy thought it was necessary to beat you up, then there’s nothing
Ram needs to say to her.”

“C’mon! That ain’t no way t’ treat me. Can’t ya be a bit nicer?”



“Ram is being nice by allowing you to bask in her presence, Garf. Now stop whining, or Ram
will have to impart her own lesson on you,” she warned flatly.

Ryuzu stepped forward. “Come this way, young Garf. I’ll help you get back to health.”

With a grunt, Garfiel followed Ryuzu, and the two disappeared into the house beside them.

Once things settled, Ram turned to Emilia, finally straightening into her proper greeting
stance—just as a maid should. “Welcome, Emilia-sama. It’s good to see you again in good
health.”

Emilia smiled. “Me too, Ram. I missed you as well.”

Ram then rose from her bow. “Come, Roswaal-sama is waiting inside for you, Emilia-sama.”

Subaru glanced at the house, then back at Emilia. “Well, you heard her Emilia, the clown is
—“

“It’s Roswaal-sama,” Ram interrupted sharply, her gaze narrowing as her tone darkened.

“Roswaal-sama is our lord, and you are his attendant. You will address him with the full
respect his position demands and not any insulting nicknames. Ram will only say this once,
Understood?”

“Ah, right, sorry, my bad, it won’t happen again,” Subaru replied quickly, trying to appease
the strict pink-haired maid.

With a huff, Ram gestured for Rem to follow as she entered the house, with Emilia and
Subaru trailing behind.

‘Finally, we’ll have our meeting, clown. I have so many questions for you, and you better
have good answers for them,’ 

After days of impatient waiting, Subaru would finally get his chance to confront Roswaal L.
Mathers.

 

Chapter End Notes

Emilia's being a naughty naughty, Puck would be so dissapointed in her.



Chapter 51: Arc 4 - Reunion With A Clown
Chapter Notes

This chapter was a bitch to write; it took me three days just to finish it. Hope you guys
enjoy it.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

“The hell happened to you, Roswaal? You look like you got vandalized by a bunch of kids
with toilet paper. Is this your attempt at a Halloween costume? I think your clown get-up was
way better, no offense.”

“Barasu! Ram has already given you a warning. Now she will have to—”

“Now, now, Raaaaam. Subaru-kun was merely jesting, I’m sure he is just as shocked and
worried about my health as you all are.”

How did such an unexpected and amusing exchange occur? Well…

Following behind Ram, Rem, Subaru, and Emilia all entered the house that Roswaal was
lodging in, and from one look, one could see that it was a modest house.

The sturdy, uneven stone walls complemented the exterior, adorned with paintings and
murals that added a touch of character. A wooden table sat surrounded by chairs, dishes
clattering atop it, while carpets draped both the windows and the floor. A few sacks hung
from the ceiling, various items were scattered atop a small table, and an unlit fireplace stood
at one side of the room, its brick chimney stretching upward with an empty pot resting on the
grill above charred wood. At the far end, a corridor branched off, leading to several rooms

All in all, this looked like what you would expect from a regular, albeit larger and slightly
lavish village home.

He followed closely behind Ram as she walked right through it. As he walked, he could feel
the shift in the air and the sound of someone talking; it was Garfiel, grumbling about
something he couldn’t pick up as they walked past his open door.

Blue mana was swirling and gathering in the room, the culprit behind the phenomenon being
Ryuzu as she applied healing spells to fix Garfiel’s many wounds.

At last, Subaru would get the chance to interrogate the clown, and he better have satisfactory
answers—lest he end up getting the White Whale treatment.

Subaru, Emilia, and Rem entered the room, a slightly cramped bedroom with a double bed, a
few decorations, a desk, a chair, and a wardrobe tucked away in the corner.



But those details barely mattered. What Subaru focused on was the man who had been the
source of his headaches for days.

Roswaal was perched on the bed, pillows stacked behind him, but what caught Subaru's
attention was his condition.

His face was bare for once—without the usual layer of clown makeup—exposing his ghastly
pale skin in full. His indigo hair was a bit unkempt, and his extravagant clown costume was
gone, replaced by something entirely different.

Bandages.

Wrapped around his head, his hands—his whole body—though "wrapped" was an
exaggeration. They were haphazardly applied, barely clinging to him, and in some places,
they had started slipping off entirely.

At the sound of the door opening, Roswaal turned, his heterochromatic eyes gleaming as he
took in the sight of Rem, Subaru, and Emilia entering. His gaze lingered on Subaru for a
moment longer—something unreadable flickering in his mismatched eyes—before he finally
spoke.

“Ahhhh, Emilia-sama, Suuuuubaru-kun, Rem, it’s good to have all three of you grace this
place with your presence. I feel happy now that the camp is all united in one place,” he said
in that sing-song tone of his.

And that’s how Subaru ended up earning Ram’s immediate ire, her pink eyes narrowing in
warning as she prepared to deliver a punishment severe enough to make the Sword Demon
weep.

Fortunately, Roswaal intervened before she could act, saving Subaru from a fate worse than
death—cleaning the chimney for a week.

Now, as for Roswaal’s comment about Subaru being worried… that was mostly wrong. He
did hold some concern for the man, sure—but not for his overall condition or well-being.

He was worried that Roswaal might be too injured to hold their conversation—unable to
speak at all.

But judging by his usual jovial mood, he seemed more than fit for their one-on-one meeting.

Emilia’s expression shifted to one of surprise and concern as she took in Roswaal’s battered
condition. "Roswaal..." she murmured, trailing off as the worry seeped into her tone.

Rem stepped forward slightly, her blue eyes reflecting her unease. "Roswaal-sama, what
happened to you? What could have caused such wounds?"

Roswaal’s mismatched eyes shifted to Rem. "I feeeeel happy knowing how much you care
about my health, Reeeeem. But no need to worry—no one’s done anything to meeeee. After
all, I’m the strongest mage in this world!" he assured her in his signature drawl, throwing in a
quick boast about his capabilities.



Rem let out a quiet sigh of relief at his words. Roswaal was not just her employer—he was
the one who had taken her and Ram in after their village was destroyed, giving them a home,
employment and a purpose when they had nowhere else to turn.

Just like her sister, Rem deeply cared for Roswaal, but in a different way, so it was only
natural that seeing him injured filled her with concern.

"Rem is relieved to hear that, but is there anything she can do? She dislikes seeing her lord in
this state..."

Roswaal smiled at the maid’s worry. "There iiiis. As you know, I’m still injuuuured, and
healing magic isn’t exactly my specialty. So, if you could lend me your talents, that would be
muuuch appreciated."

Rem nodded quickly. "Of course! Rem will do everything she can to help her lord!"

Ram, now standing beside Roswaal, cast Subaru a smug look.

"See this, Barasu? Sissy’s first instinct is to help Roswaal-sama, not to joke at his expense.
You get zero out of ten," she declared with absolute certainty.

Subaru rolled his eyes. "When have I ever scored higher than a zero, Rammy? And hey—
aren’t you the one who wrapped these bandages? His wounds aren’t even covered properly!"

"What nonsense. Ram was simply using an ancient healing technique passed down by the
Oni village. Barasu’s pig-like brain cannot comprehend the wisdom behind it."

"You can just admit that you don’t know how to wrap wounds, Rammy. No shame in
acknowledging shortcomings."

"Shortcomings? Ram is the most lovable, perfect being to ever grace this world. To claim she
has shortcomings would be blasphemy against all logic!"

"Oh really?" Subaru said, "I think the word ‘delusional’ fits you more perfectly. No offense,
Rammy."

Subaru and Ram then descended into their usual petty argument, which, as always, would
drag on endlessly since neither the prideful Ram nor the cocky Subaru ever backed down.

After all, giving in meant admitting defeat to the other side—and they’d sooner face death
than allow that humiliation.

By now, Rem had moved to the other side of Roswaal's bed, extending her hands as small
blue spheres formed around them. She quietly cast healing spells, doing her best to mend her
lord’s wounds.

Emilia, who had remained silent until now, finally spoke up. "Roswaal… Ever since the royal
selection started, you’ve been gone. Where have you been all this time?"



Roswaal turned his attention to Emilia, his mismatched eyes locking onto hers. "Ahh, Emilia-
sama. Yes, I’ve been gone for quite some time. Hasn’t Ram explained where I’ve been?"

"Yes—she did. But you barely returned to the mansion before leaving again immediately…
Was what sent you away really that urgent?" she asked.

Roswaal simply nodded. "Veeery urgent. As I am the sole sponsor for your candidacy, I
haaad to reach out and arrange meetings with nobles toooo ensure their support… with
limited results, I’m afraid. Is there something you wish to tell meeeee?"

Emilia nodded, Since he’s her sponsor she figured it’s his right to know what went down
recently, aka, the Witch Cult assault.

“Ram has informed me of all that has traaaaanspired recently, but I would like to hear it from
the start directly from the first-hand source, Emilia-sama,” Roswaal said, casting a glance
toward the maid, who was currently locked in a debate about the superiority of Tatos as a
food item.

Emilia drew in a deep breath. “The Witch Cult attacked us four days ago—specifically the
Sloth Archbishop. I haven’t met him, but I think he goes by the name ‘Petelgeuse’ or
something.”

At the mention of that name, Roswaal’s smile faltered ever so slightly, his mismatched eyes
dimming for just a brief moment. A flicker of melancholy passed over his expression before
he swiftly masked it.

“I see… That’s quite terrible. I presume Natsuki-kun is the one who slayed the Sloth
Archbishop. Correct?” He asked, shifting slightly toward Emilia, his focus entirely on her
upcoming words.

She nodded. “Yeah, Subaru-kun arrived and drove the Witch Cult away. He also brought
another candidate to help—Crusch Karsten. She helped a lot in evacuating the village and
proposed an alliance between us. I agreed to it, but I’m waiting for your response before
anything is set in ink and paper.”

“…”

“…”

A brief pause settled between them—an unspoken moment where Emilia and Roswaal
remained locked in each other’s gaze, each expecting something different from the other.

“…Roswaal-sama? Is something wrong?” Rem asked from the side as she continued healing
him, noticing his lack of response. Emilia mirrored her concern.

“…”

“Roswaal? Is everything okay?” Emilia asked him as he kept staring at her.



Roswaal didn’t reply. His smile wavered, then faded entirely, his brows knitting together in
thought. His usual clownish demeanor had disappeared, replaced by something unfamiliar—
confusion.

By now, even Ram and Subaru had paused their petty argument, drawn in by Roswaal’s eerie
silence.

Slowly, Roswaal turned to Subaru. The mischievous glint that normally danced in his eyes
was absent. Instead, there was an uncharacteristic sharpness—a seriousness that made Subaru
blink in surprise behind his shades.

“Subaru-kun,” Roswaal drawled, his tone matching the sharpness in his eyes. “Can you
kindly explain the circumstances under which you met and recruited Crusch-sama to your
aid? And your stay in the capital as a whole?”

‘Hmm? Why? What does that have to do with anything?’ Subaru thought, caught off guard
by suddenly becoming the center of attention.

Still, Subaru was used to being put in that position, so he quickly recovered and responded.
“Well, after you and Emilia left, not much really happened in the capital. Rem and I just
spent the week exploring the place, and that’s about it.”

“Not much else?” Roswaal’s tone had shifted, as serious as an elder reprimanding a
grandchild. “Are you certain that nothing significant happened during your stay? No matter
how trivial or troublesome it may seem, you can just tell me, Subaru-kun.”

‘Weird… His “accent” is gone. No more drawn-out words like he usually does…’ Subaru
narrowed his eyes at Roswaal, careful to keep the suspicion hidden from everyone else.

‘No, this is how Roswaal actually speaks. That clownish accent he has is just for show. But
why the sudden change? Did I do something wrong? Or was he expecting something to
happen?’

The more Subaru considered it, the more certain he became—the exaggerated way Roswaal
spoke was just a mask. Had he been putting up a front every time they conversed?

Subaru recalled the last time Roswaal spoke in such a serious tone—when he was requesting
Emilia’s help with Meili. Back then, he hadn’t thought much of it; he had an entire village to
handle, and their conversation had been brief.

“…No, Roswaal. Nothing happened in the capital. Like I said, Rem and I just explored the
place, that’s all,” Subaru answered.

As he finished speaking, Rem glanced at him briefly—just for a moment—before returning
to healing Roswaal. Subaru caught the movement from the corner of his eyes.

It was obvious. He had just lied to Roswaal. They had been ambushed by knights—for what
he had done to the “finest” one among them.



He had promised Rem that he would share everything with everyone, but that part would
come later—once he figured out Roswaal and they finally left this “Sanctuary.”

"And what about the Karsten matriarch? How did you recruit her to assist you?" Roswaal
asked, smoothly shifting the conversation to the other topic—one that seemed even more
important to him.

"Right. When we were heading back to the mansion, we came across Crusch and her army
struggling against the Whale. They were losing pretty badly, so I decided to step in, help take
it down, and… well, I did. That earned me her gratitude and favor," Subaru explained.

Roswaal paused, carefully absorbing his words before questioning further. "Crusch does
possess the strength to face a Great Mabeast like the Whale on her own, especially with the
Sword Demon by her side. Was there anyone else aiding them in the battle, Subaru-kun?"

‘Why does this feel like an interrogation? Wait—I am being interrogated!’ Subaru realized,
more bewildered than miffed as the script completely flipped on him.

He was supposed to be the one doing the interrogation, not the opposite.

Still, he had been engrossed with Ram to take the lead, so he might as well play along. After
all, if things ever got out of hand, Subaru could take down the clown without breaking a
sweat.

He was the strongest, after all.

"I don’t know the specifics, and I never asked, but Crusch had the mercenary group Iron Fang
assisting her. Looked like she and Anastasia made some kind of deal," Subaru replied.

"And what became of the mercenaries? Were they all killed, or…?"

"No, they made it through. After the Whale was defeated, they packed up and left early in the
morning."

"..."

Roswaal didn’t reply. Instead, his expression shifted into something deeply troubled—his
wide, unblinking eyes fixed on a thought that seemed to weigh heavily on him.

Whatever had just crossed his mind, Subaru had no way of knowing. He wasn’t psychic, after
all.

Emilia, Ram, and Rem exchanged glances, with Ram and Rem looking particularly troubled.
They had known Roswaal for nearly a decade, and never—not even once—had they seen him
like this. Their lord was always flamboyant, theatrical, effortlessly composed. This was
completely out of character.

Emilia didn’t have the same long history with Roswaal as the maids did, but even she could
tell his expression was anything but ordinary.



And then—just as suddenly as the tension had built—

Roswaal smiled.

The stiffness in his face evaporated, replaced with the usual carefree, calm demeanor he
always carried.

"Weeeell now, that was quite the story, Subaru-kuuuun. To fight the White Whale and the
Witch Cult in the span of a daaaaay. I am glad that my favorite butler is safe and sound in the
ennnnnd," he drawled.

Subaru… was not surprised by Roswaal’s abrupt shift in attitude. He had already deduced
that Roswaal put his “mask” back on. Metaphorically speaking.

"Roswall, what’s with all the sudden questions? And Ram already told you everything, right?
Why did you need to hear it from Subaru again?" Emilia spoke up, her curiosity piqued.

Roswaal turned to her, his mismatched eyes twinkling with amusement. "Ahhhh, I merely
wanted to confirm the information. While I dooooo not doubt Ram’s validity, a second source
never hurts. I simply waaaaaanted to fill in any gaps she might have missed," he replied
smoothly.

"Cool, cool. So you got what you needed, yeah? Okay good." Subaru quipped sarcastically
from the side, not even expecting an answer before continuing.

"So now that you're done with ‘Ask Ten Questions Featuring Natsuki Subaru,’ it’s my turn to
ask you some," he said.

Roswaal simply kept smiling, unfazed. "Whyyyy of course! Ask away, and I shall answer
whatever it is that you wish to know."

Subaru nodded—it was time to get things moving. "First of all, can you explain to me why

Roswaal tilted his head slightly. "Because It’s a smaaaaall, modest village and a safe haven

The name landed like a shockwave. Ram and Subaru remained unreactive—Subaru had

But Emilia? She looked taken aback. Her expression froze as she seemed to be absorbing his

Those three had what could be considered a “Tame” reaction, but Rem?

The poor maid looked as though she’d been smacked in the face by a sledgehammer,

"W-wait, did R-roswaal-sama just say W-w-witch’s Graveyard? L-like the W-witch of

Rem met her lord’s gaze, still shaken. "B-but Roswaal-sama—! Th-the Sanctuary is within

Subaru nearly laughed at Roswaal’s remark—the witch herself had openly declared that she

"The answer is quite obvioussss, Subaru-kun," Roswaal replied. "The House Mathers makes

‘…My gratitude? Not our gratitude?’ Subaru noted but let Roswaal continue.

"Due to the… unique circumstances of this plaaaaace and our hiiiistory, this remains a family

about this place under tiiiight lips," Roswaal concluded.



"But why take the risk?" Subaru asked. "I mean, if word got out that you’re managing a place
connected to a witch, your house would be done for . So why?"

"For the same reason you are standing riiiiiight here," Roswaal answered instantly, as if he
anticipated such question. He closed his mismatched eyes briefly before fixing them back

"Emilia lost her insignia to a thief, but you helped heeeeer get it back. Now, if I were just any
other noble, what do you think I wouuuld have done upon hearing about it? More
specifically, once I know about your involvement?"

Subaru paused for a moment, genuinely considering it. His interactions with nobles had been

"I’d probably be bribed to keep quiet about it—or worse, killed off."

"I guess so, yeah," Subaru admitted.

"Which is whyyyyy I am more than willing to take this risk. Becaaaause, without her—
without Echidna’s generosity—our family wouldn’t be in the prosperous position it holds
todaaaay," Roswaal continued, his words carrying both sincerity and unwavering conviction.

Subaru opened his mouth to ask another question—

"Ahh! My amazon’ self sees that Yer all still runnin’ yer ugly mouths," a gruff, unmistakable

There stood Garfiel, looking much better than before—most of the bruises had faded, and the

"Hah?" Garfiel scoffed. "Yer stayin’ under my roof outta the kindness of my heart. I can

Subaru suppressed the urge to sigh loudly. Seriously—he had no patience for this guy and his

’’’’Huh?!’’’’

Subaru, Emilia, and Rem were all caught off guard by his words. House arrest? How? He is
the lord of the domain, so how was he placed in one? 

"I knooooow, it’s shocking, isn’t it?" Roswaal mused, completely unfazed. "Me, Raaaaam,
and the people of Arlam… Oh, and you three now that you’re here," he added.

"Yeah, that’s right," Garfiel chimed in, flashing a grin. "All of ya are trapped here with us!
And ya can’t leave—even ‘f ya wanted t’!"

Subaru simply stared at him, before allowing a small smile to creep onto his face. One that

Really now?" he remarked, his voice tinged with amusement and an undercurrent of menace.

lot worse than that footprint on your cheek…"

Garfiel snarled, baring his teeth and clenching his fists. "That was just a cheap shot! If ya had

Another confrontation flared between them. Garfiel and Subaru were at odds yet again—it

"Why not?"

"Because the barrier's last-line defense mechanism has been triggered, I’m afraid."

"And what does that mean?"

"It’s a mechanism implanted into the barrier at its creation. When activated, it completely

passing through," Roswaal explained.

"So, we’re stuck here together!" he cheerfully declared to everyone—though no one shared

"Roswaal-sama, nee-sama…" Rem murmured to both, her expression clouded with concern
and unease, same as Emilia, while Ram was just as passive as always.

Subaru’s brow just twitched at the implication. ‘What kind of bullshit is this?! Who the hell
makes a barrier with that setting?!’ Subaru thought in frustration, his expression turning into
a deep scowl.

"…Can’t we just break it?" Subaru asked. "Aren’t you, like, the best mage in this kingdom,
Roswaal? There has to be something you can do about it?"

Roswaal shook his head. "Nooooo can do. This barrier is an ancient fooooorm of magic
application—it is simply impervious to anything I do."

"You must be joking, right? Who the hell would create something like this?" Subaru asked,
and Roswaal's knowing smile gave him the answer.

'Damn it, Echidna. What the hell were you thinking? Were there secrets here you didn’t want
anyone getting their hands on?' Subaru thought in frustration.

All of this nonsense—from meeting Echidna up until this point, all within just a single hour
—was starting to give him a serious headache.

"So, how do we even break it? Or are we stuck here forever?" he asked, though Subaru had a
few tricks he could pull.

Namely—cursed energy.

Through careful experimentation and application of cursed mana, Subaru had come to
understand the true nature of the relationship between mana and cursed energy.

At first, he believed that cursed energy and mana would mix and intertwine to create cursed
mana. But the truth was entirely different. Simply put, cursed energy would cannibalize
mana, absorbing its power to fuel itself.



Like a mathematical formula—multiplying a negative number by a positive one—you end up
with a greater negative value.

And since spells couldn't be powered by cursed mana, he could release cursed energy into the
mana flow sustaining the barrier, disrupting it and shutting it down.

Or, he could brute-force his way out with a Hollow Purple. Even a large-scale teleportation
might work—though he had never used it before, so he wasn’t sure if he could pull it off.

"To break the barrier, one must complete all the trials of the Sanctuary. It is the only way, I'm
afraid," Ryuzu finally answered him.

"And that’s where the half-elf comes in!" Garfiel said, turning to a startled Emilia.

"H-huh?! Me?" she stammered.

"Like Granny said, th’ only way t’ break through the barrier is through the Graveyard Trial.
And yer th’ only one who can do it!"

"Why Emilia? Can't you do it instead?" Subaru shot back.

"Nah, not just anybody can do it. Only those who ar’ qualified can undergo th’ trials. And if
ya tried t’ take ‘em when ya ain’t..." He pointed toward the clown, who simply smiled in
response.

"We want Th’ half-elf will t’ do th’ trials and break th’ barrier, That’s our ultimatum! If th’
half-elf can’t do it, then we’re all stuck ‘ere together! Even those damn annoyin’ villagers o’
yers ain’t going nowhere!" Garfiel said with a grin, clearly enjoying the displeased scowl on
Subaru’s face.

"…"

Silence fell over the room, filled with a mix of emotions.

Garfiel looked ecstatic, sporting a broad smile as he finally gained the upper hand over
someone he found endlessly irritating.

Ram and Ryuzu remained passive, their expressions unreadable. They didn’t seem
particularly troubled, as if being trapped in what was essentially a prison didn’t faze them in
the slightest.

Subaru, on the other hand, was thoroughly annoyed. He just wanted to knock that smug grin
off Garfiel’s face.

Roswaal, unsurprisingly, maintained his signature smile, lounging comfortably as he
observed the silence with unreadable eyes.

Rem was confused and slightly frightened. She couldn’t understand how a simple trip to the
Sanctuary had spiraled into this mess. The only consolation was that she had her hero beside
her.



And who knows? Maybe this would lead to something straight out of a story—where two
people trapped in a dangerous place slowly come to rely on each other, until one thing leads
to another, and then they have se—

As for Emilia…

"I’ll do it."

Her voice sliced through the silence that had gripped the room, immediately drawing
everyone’s attention.

"Emilia…?" Subaru trailed off, his expression unreadable, but the sound of her name made
Emilia turn toward him.

"I said I’ll do it, Subaru," she repeated before shifting her gaze to everyone in the room. "I’ll
do the Sanctuary’s trials and free everyone."

"Emilia, are you sure? I can find another way—"

"No!"

She cut him off, her voice sharper now—firm enough to make Subaru stop in his tracks. Her
amethyst eyes locked onto his, unwavering.

"I said no, Subaru, just no. Did you forget what I told you before we got here? That I wanted
to prove myself? Well, this is it. This is my chance, and I’m going to take it."

She then turned to Garfiel and Ryuzu. "I don’t understand why you would do this—why you
would trap everyone here. But if taking the trials is the only way to free everyone, then I’ll do
everything I can to succeed."

Subaru remained silent. He wanted to argue—that he has another way to fix this without
playing into their hands, without risking whatever unknowns the “trials” had in store.

But he had agreed to give Emilia the spotlight, and he wasn’t going back on his word.
Reluctantly, Subaru had to let her take the lead on this one.

"Is thaaaat so? You will undergo the trials to freeeeee everyone? Is this truly what you wish
to do? Those trials will not be easy at alllll, Emilia-sama. Lots of people have undergone
them before you and have all but failed. Are you ready to take the responsibility for everyone
here?" Roswaal asked.

Emilia turned to face him, her amethyst eyes burning with conviction, her posture one of
confidence and determination.

"Absolutely," she said resolutely, her tone firm and unwavering.

Roswaal’s smile widened at this. "I seeee. Splendid, Emilia-sama. We are all counting on you
now, so do not dissssappoint us."



Emilia nodded. She had no intention of failing—not this time. She was certain she could get
through the trials with relative ease.

This was her golden opportunity to prove herself to everyone, handed to her on a silver
platter. And she couldn’t be happier.

Roswaal’s smile, however, was not one of encouragement. No—his grin carried something
deeper, something selfish, something wicked.

‘A few minor hiccups, but everything is moving perfectly according to the writ. I will finally
fulfill my long-held goal, sensei…’

Chapter 52: Arc 4 - Arlam’s Welfare Check
Chapter Notes
