Gone was the eventful reunion with Roswaal, along with the bombshell that everyone was
essentially trapped inside the Sanctuary. Garfiel and Ryuzu led the group to familiarize
themselves with their new lodgings.

The house was spacious enough for everyone to have their own space. Roswaal and Emilia
had separate rooms, while Ram and Rem shared one since they were twins. Subaru,
unsurprisingly, got the smallest room—a cramped space that he likened to a tiny college
dorm or even a walk-in closet.

And of course, it was Garfiel who assigned the rooms—this was the troublemaker’s house,
after all—and he had a giddy, smug grin as he gave Subaru into the smallest room, tossing a
verbal jab in the process. But Subaru didn't take the bait and accepted it without fuss.

Rem tried offering Subaru a spot in her bed, but one sharp glare from Ram had the younger
twin backing down sheepishly.

Ryuzu Alma had a bedroom for herself, but she willingly gave it to Otto when he was
brought in for resting. The merchant was still unconscious, worn out from the stamina-
draining effects of Rem’s healing.

Naturally, Garfiel was quick to protest. “Why!, jus’ leave that weaklin’ in th’ damn carriage,”
was what he complained, but Ryuzu stood her ground and refused to budge.

Patrasche was meant to be taken to the village stable, but the stubborn ground dragon outright
refused to leave the carriage—or the house, for that matter. This frustrated Garfiel but
thoroughly amused Subaru. In the end, she was allowed to stay near the house.

And so, this new prison of theirs now had a “home” for them. Everyone unpacked whatever
meager belongings they had brought from the carriage.



A few hours passed, and as the sun was in the process of dipping below the horizon, Emilia
and Subaru walked through the Sanctuary proper.

They could take in the sights up close and personal, and the picture was just as grim as they
drove through it. The whole village looked to be in pretty rough shape, like it had been
ransacked by bandits—except the villagers had been left behind.

And if that wasn’t enough to hammer the point home, the locals reacted the same as before:
mistrust, disdain, and hatred, with even a hint of fear mixed in.

Subaru glanced at Emilia from the corner of his vision. He could see how her amethyst eyes
darted from side to side, taking in the people's reactions. Her expression, however, remained
unchanged, as if she were unbothered.

But he noticed the slight tremble in her shoulders, the hastened steps—she clearly wanted to
escape those stares, but she held herself back.

Subaru frowned slightly. ‘Emilia’s affected by this... What did we even do to deserve this
treatment?’ The thought crossed his mind, but he held himself back from comforting her. He
had given her his word, and he wasn’t going to break it.

They walked in silence for a while, but it wasn’t just to take in the scenery—they were
headed toward the reason they came here in the first place.

Following Garfiel, they soon arrived at a tall brick cathedral, its red-and-white exterior giving
off the appearance of a Christian church. The biggest difference? A dragon emblem stood
atop the gates instead of a cross.

Two demi-human guards flanked the wooden gates—one a cat, the other a dog. The cat held
a pitchfork, the dog a short but aged sword. Both gripped their weapons tightly upon seeing
the approaching group, eyes filled with wariness.

Yet the moment Garfiel stepped forward, they straightened up and puffed out their chests.

""Garfiel-san,"" both men said in unison as the aforementioned demi-human stood before
them.

"Bran, Mark, good, yer bot’ are actually in yer spots, unlike last time..." he said, trailing off
while narrowing his eyes at the two, who avoided eye contact with their boss, looking
sheepish.

"Of course, boss... But in my defense, Bran was the one who took off first," Mark suddenly
accused. "I ran after him to drag him back to his post and—"

"Wha—Hey?!" The dog demi-human shouted at his cat partner. "Yer the one who slipped
away tryin’ ta steal some food! I told ya to—"

"Aghh! Ye lot are so annoyin’! How ‘bout I jus’ castrate ya both ‘n be done with ya?!"
Garfiel snapped at the arguing demi-humans, shutting them down instantly.



Garfiel dragged his hand down his face, letting out a groan of irritation at the two. Of all the
guards—who were really just regular villagers with weapons—these two were the most
headache-inducing to him.

But they were among the few willing to do the work, so he’d make do with what he got.

"Listen, my amazin’ self ain’t got time for chit-chattin’. How ‘re the people inside? They
cause any trouble?" he asked.

"No, sir! Everything is in order!" Bran answered.

"Good, don’ wanna waste anymore time," he nodded to himself, then turned to Emilia and
Subaru, who quietly lingered behind him.

"Ahright, ya heard it yerselves, yer vill’gers are all safe ‘n sound, satisfied yet, hmm?"
Garfiel called out to the two.

After all, the reason he was leading them here was because Subaru had requested him to
check on the villagers to make sure they were safe and sound. Emilia had also tagged along
when she caught wind of this.

Garfiel begrudgingly agreed, of course, just so he could rest and prepare for what was about
to happen in the evening.

"..."

Subaru didn’t answer Garfiel as he looked inside the church with his six eyes. He could see
the Od of the Arlam villagers inside; a little more than a hundred were present, which
matched the number that had been sent off to the Sanctuary.

‘Everyone is accounted for, but that’s only their numbers, not their living conditions.’

You see, the healthier a person was, the shinier and brighter their Od appeared, while the
older or frailer someone was, the dimmer their Od would be. Other factors played a role too
—whether someone used their own Od to fuel magical spells—like the White Whale—or for
Metias.

Wilhelm’s Od, for example, was dimmer than that of younger people, because of his
advanced age.

Everyone inside had a variety of shines, making it difficult for him to discern their living
conditions.

Luckily for him, Emilia took the words he wanted to say right out of his mouth.

“We’d like to check up on everyone ourselves, Garfiel-san,” Emilia asked.

“Tsk, fin’, jus’ don’ take too long, my amazin’ self doesn’t want t’ spend more time ‘n dis,”
he grumbled, then turned to the guard duo, who were eyeing Subaru—and especially Emilia
—warily.



“Ya heard ’em, open th’ gates,” he ordered, and the two complied, each pulling a door open.

Subaru and Emilia stepped inside behind Garfiel and took stock of their surroundings. The
church was large, built of stone, with a high ceiling. Chandeliers with lit candles illuminated
the interior, alongside the large windows dotted along the walls.

There were no pews in sight, nor an altar. The place was barren, save for the villagers, who
all resided in the nave. They clustered together in small groups—likely families and friends
huddling close. Lining the walls on all sides were more guards, watching over the people
inside with stern, unwavering expressions.

The people were in... acceptable condition. They weren’t sitting around with the happiest
expressions or with their stomachs filled to the brim, but they weren’t in pain or fear either—
just solemn or anxious. None of them seemed to be starving or hungry, yet the longing to
return home lingered in every one of them.

'None of them seem to be hurt or sick. That’s good.' Because if they were, then things would
have turned ugly real quick.

All heads inside turned toward the door at the sound of movement. When Emilia and Subaru
were spotted, the guards grew slightly more tense yet remained reassured by Garfiel’s
presence. As for the villagers…

"Subaru-sama!"

Garfiel stepped to the side as a voice rang out from the group, and like a switch being flipped,
everyone—whether old or young—scrambled forward toward the duo... or, more specifically,
toward Subaru.

"Thank the Dragon you're here! We were starting to get so worried!"

"We’re truly relieved you’re okay!"

"Is everyone safe? Are they back?!"

"My children! Are they okay?"

"We heard the Lord was hurt—is he okay?"

"Did you beat them? The Witch Cult? Did you do it?!"

"Will you finally get us out of here?!"

"How are—"

"Can you—"

"Is Petra—"



Questions upon questions were hurled at Subaru, quickly overwhelming him as the eager
villagers surrounded him in a chaotic storm of inquiries. He raised his hands in a calming
gesture, trying to get them to ease up.

"Okay—okay, settle down a bit! I can’t answer a thing if you guys keep bombarding me with
questions!" He raised his voice slightly, just enough to regain control over the eager crowd.

Emilia stood next to him, but she might as well have been invisible, as everyone focused
solely on Subaru, completely ignoring her.

‘Subaru is really trusted and adored by them…’ she thought, feeling a slight tightness in her
chest at the attention and admiration he was receiving.

Emilia may now enjoy a favorable reputation among the villagers, a far cry from the negative
and hostile sentiments that once surrounded her whenever she approached them.

But was it truly because of her own efforts and hard work? Did she actually deserve the
higher standing she held with them?

The answer was simple: no.

The only reason they appreciated her was because of her association with Subaru. He was the
one who brought her to the village, personally rescued the kidnapped children, and single-
handedly defeated a horde of Mabeasts—all while she merely watched.

And when it came to removing the curses from them, it was Puck who did the work, not her.

Arlam hailed both of them as heroes, protectors of their children and the village—but Subaru
was the one who truly did everything. He was the one who deserved all the praise and faith
they placed in them.

That sentiment was only reinforced when they arrived, and everyone rushed straight to him
without giving her a second glance.

So she stood silently as Subaru calmed the loud and boisterous villagers, eventually bringing
them all to quiet.

"Alright, you guys finally settled down. I swear, I almost went deaf from how loud you guys
were,” he joked. “First off, I’d like to start with this," he began, cracking a smile at the
anticipating villagers.

"I’m happy to announce that the Witch Cult has been defeated and driven back! Your village
and others are all safe and sound!" he declared.

Instantly, there was an upbeat reaction to the news. Some of the rowdy folks cheered loudly
—typically the younger ones—while others simply sighed in relief and expressed their
gratitude.

The guards, and even Garfiel, all had looks of surprise on their faces at the news.



Once they settled down, he resumed, "The others have all gone back to their homes. They
were well taken care of and are completely healthy, so there’s no need for you to worry about
them."

"But what about the children? What about my Petra!" one of the villagers asked, drawing
Subaru's attention.

She was a middle-aged woman with brown hair and blue eyes, dressed in simple attire.
Beside her stood a man of similar age with reddish hair and green eyes. Subaru recognized
them as Marian and Elias Lyte, the parents of the most adorable girl in the village, Petra Lyte.

Subaru nodded toward the couple. "The children are all being looked after by your neighbors
and friends. They’re in good hands, and I personally made sure of that, so you don’t need to
worry about her."

During the evacuation, some of the children had been separated from their families, and
Subaru had arranged for them to be cared for until their parents returned from the sanctuary.

Marian and Elias both sighed in relief. "Oh, thank you so much, Subaru-sama. We were so
anxious about her, but you’ve always done your best to ensure she and the other children
were safe."

"Don’t mention it! Just doing what’s right!" he replied, giving them a thumbs-up, which made
them and everyone else smile.

"Hohoho, always taking care of our young ones, aren’t you? Are you sure you're not a child-
at-heart, Subaru-sama?" a voice called out from the crowd. It was rough, belonging to an
elderly person who was calmly making their way to the front.

"Milde! I thought you might’ve dropped dead from all the stress! I guess after all these
decades dealing with your husband, you’ve gotten used to it, right?" he joked.

"As if! These old bones of mine have stood strong against the tests of time! And my foolish
husband doesn’t even hold a candle to that!" she proclaimed, and they both shared a light
laugh.

Milde Arlam was the chief of the village, which had been named after her family name. She
was also a notorious pervert, often trying to "accidentally" grab his butt multiple occasions.

Fortunately, his infinity thwarted her and many other attempts, protecting his chastity from
the perilous clutches of these ravenous creatures they call women.

"Now, as much as I’d love to sit and chat about boring matters over tea, I believe there are
more pressing concerns that should be addressed," she began, getting straight into the heart of
the matter and instantly dimming the lively atmosphere.

"We heard that the lord was recently injured. How bad is it? Will he be alright?" she asked,
showing genuine concern for the lord who had his popularity amongst the villagers rise due
to recent events.



Subaru was quick to reassure her, "Roswaal’s fine. He got hurt trying to do the trials, but he’s
safe and recovering quickly. Give it a day or two, and he’ll be back to full health."

"That’s a relief. And what do you mean by the ‘trials’? Also, when can we expect to return
home?" she asked.

The question made Subaru’s smile falter. It seemed the villagers hadn’t been fully updated,
and he was going to have to deliver some bad news.

"Errr, right. About that…" he began. "You guys know about the barrier surrounding the
Sanctuary, yeah?"

"Yes, we do. The pink-haired maid—err Ram was it? told us about it before we arrived,"
Milde answered.

"Good, then I won’t need to start from scratch. Let’s just say that, due to some…" he cast a
subtle glance at Garfiel, "…unforeseen circumstances surrounding the barrier, we are all
officially stuck here."

The cheerful atmosphere that had once filled the room was officially dampened by the
announcement, leaving the villagers murmuring in hushed whispers, their expressions
darkened with unease.

"W-we’re stuck here? But I want to go home!"

"How long do we have to stay here? I’m sick of this place."

"If I don’t tend to my crops soon, I won’t be able to feed my family…"

"I miss my children…"

"That’s quite a grim situation, Subaru-sama…" Milde said slowly, uncertain of how to
respond to the news.

Noticing the anxious and fearful atmosphere settling over the crowd, Subaru put on a
comforting smile and spoke in a light, reassuring tone.

"Everyone, please, I know it sounds bad…" he called out, ensuring all eyes were on him.
"But all hope isn’t lost—there is a way to break the barrier so that we can all return home."

The villagers immediately perked up at his words.

"Really? Please tell us, Subaru-sama," Milde urged.

"The Sanctuary’s trials. By completing them, the barrier will deactivate, and we’ll all be able
to go back home," he explained.

A wave of relief swept through the crowd as the tension and fear visibly lifted from their
faces.



Milde beamed, her remaining teeth now fully visible. "That’s wonderful news, Subaru-sama!
When will you do it? You saved our children and protected us from the Witch Cult—for you,
I bet it’ll be as easy as a walk through the garden!"

Others nodded eagerly, fully agreeing with Milde’s sentiment. They had seen firsthand just
how reliable Subaru was.

"That’s right, you got rid of thos cultists, you can do anything!"

"My daughter was saved all thanks to you!"

"You helped me carry my bags all the way home!"

Voices rang out, recalling the many ways Subaru had assisted them. Praise poured in for his
kindness and selflessness.

In his free time, whenever Emilia was busy to hangout, Subaru would often visit the Arlam
villagers to play with the local children and lend a hand wherever he could, always doing so
with a bright smile.

The villagers, both young and old, cherished and adored him for it.

Standing on the sidelines, overlooked, no one seemed to notice Emilia—but had they, they
would have seen the expression of someone who had just taken a gut punch.

The words spoken didn’t bring a smile of happiness for Subaru’s well-earned admiration.
Instead, they only reinforced her earlier realization about her standing among the villagers.

Subaru normally would’ve basked in the praise, letting it inflate his ego to dizzying heights—
high enough that Ram would need to step in just to bring it back down to bearable levels. But
instead, he merely shook his head slightly at their compliments.

"You know, I appreciate your kind words guys," he said, "But I’m sorry to disappoint you all
—I won’t be the one doing the trials."

His statement caused the room to fall silent, confusion now spreading across everyone’s
faces. Why wouldn’t Subaru be the one to take them on? He could probably clear them faster
than they could blink!

Before anyone could ask, Subaru continued, "The one who will be taking them on instead is
the world’s most adorable elf, Emilia-sama!"

He proclaimed, motioning to the half-elf who had been all but forgotten—until now.
Suddenly, with the attention of around a hundred people fixed solely on her, and with Subaru
openly calling her adorable, a furious blush exploded across Emilia’s face.

"Umm—T-th-that’s right! S-Subaru doesn’t meet the requirements for the trials, b-but I do.
So I w-will be the one to complete them and free us all!" she declared.



‘Idiot, idiot! When everyone finally focuses on you, you stammer like a foolish girl! Why?!’
she berated herself internally for stumbling over her words.

A deep breath later, Emilia finally reeled in her composure. "You all have been separated
from your families for days now, and I’ve heard your worries—your stress, your longing to
be reunited. I understand those feelings more than you know."

As she spoke, her fingers gently brushed over her necklace—the one housing the Great Spirit,
Puck, whom she regarded as her father.

Unbeknownst to her, her words and actions caught Subaru’s attention, making him raise an
eyebrow in slight confusion—yet he chose to remain silent.

"But I refuse to let this separation last any longer," she continued, her voice firm with
determination. "I promise you all that I will break the barrier and free everyone by midnight!"

Her voice carried unwavering conviction, fueled by her earlier resolve and the promise she
had just made to the villagers.

A brief silence followed Emilia’s unexpected declaration, until Milde finally spoke up,
addressing the half-elf.

"Emilia-sama," she said, "I know we may have said this before, but we sincerely apologize
for how we used to treat you."

Milde lowered her head in a small bow, and one by one, the rest of the villagers followed suit,
leaving Emilia staring at them in shock.

"T-there’s no need for this! I’ve already forgiven all of you!" she exclaimed, seeing history
repeat itself before her eyes.

She recalled the moment when Puck was lifting the children’s curses. Back then, Milde, the
parents, and another individual had all humbly apologized to her, overwhelmed with guilt.
Emilia, equally overwhelmed, had meekly accepted their heartfelt words.

"We know," Milde said, straightening up, "But I still feel the need to repeat it. I don’t know
much about these ‘trials,’ but these old bones of mine tell me they may be difficult for you.
And yet, you’re willing to go through them just to help us."

Then, she offered Emilia a warm, grandmotherly smile. "We are deeply grateful for your
help, Emilia-sama. I, and everyone here, pray for your success. May the dragon watch over
you in your hardships."

""""We wish you the best of luck, Emilia-sama!""""

Hearing those rare words of kindness, Emilia couldn’t help but break into a genuine smile—
one that made her face seem to glow under the sun’s soft orange light.

‘Oh man, Emilia has to be arrested for how ridiculously adorable she looks when she smiles;
my heart might just stop at this rate!’



Beside her, Subaru stole a glance at Emilia, cheeks slightly flushed at the sight. His Six Eyes
enhanced the moment, making it even more vivid—an image permanently engraved in his
mind.

He still harbored his doubts about her taking on the trials, knowing there were better
alternatives than playing along with Garfiel and Ryuzu’s game.

He still didn’t understand why they had activated the barrier’s “last-line defense mechanism”
when they did, nor why they were keeping the villagers trapped—essentially holding them
hostage. But if going along with it led to moments where Emilia could shine like this, he was
willing to follow the flow, as long as no one was harmed.

With the electric charge still lingering in the air, Subaru and Emilia left the villagers behind.
The sun was now sunk beyond the horizon as they made their way back to their lodgings.

Soon, Emilia would face the trials, and with the faith placed in her and the support she had
been given, she felt more ready than ever to prove herself.

Emilia knew she would overcome the trials and free everyone; the fierce determination in her
amethyst eyes made it abundantly clear to all.

She will not fail.

Chapter End Notes

Emilia will do it guys, trust me



Chapter 53: Arc 4 - Despair
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The time to undergo the trials had finally arrived.

The moon hung high and mighty, ruling over the heavens and casting its ethereal glow upon
the earth. Beneath the moon’s light stood a dark and decrepit structure, looming under the sky
with an air of ancient majesty. Chipped stone, crumbling rock, and creeping vines threatened
to reclaim it, a silent testament to its age. A stone path, flanked by torches flickering on both
sides, led to the grand staircase that ascended into the ruin.

Its sheer presence carried enough weight to strike fear into even the bravest of hearts. The
suffocating mana emanating from within made it even more foreboding, and its infamous
name alone would have been enough to dissuade most from stepping inside.

But not Emilia.

Her amethyst eyes gleamed—not with fear, but with determination and confidence.

And she was not alone.

Ram, Rem, Garfiel, Ryuzu, and Subaru stood beside her, their gazes locked on the looming
structure ahead.

Ryuzu stepped forward, her oversized staff—comically large for her small frame—thudding
against the ground. “Emilia-sama,” she began, “this is the Witch’s Graveyard. The very place
where the Witch of Greed, Echidna, met her end centuries ago.”

Emilia nodded, casting another glance at the ruin, seeing it with fresh eyes. The name suited
it well, in her opinion.

“Umm, Rem has a question she wants to ask,” the blue-haired maid spoke up, drawing
everyone’s attention.

“Roswaal-sama said this place was where the witc—umm, Echidna-san lost her life. Is that
true?” she asked Ryuzu.

The half-elf nodded. “That’s correct, young Rem. This tomb houses Echidna’s body.”

Rem frowned slightly, her expression tinged with thoughtfulness and concern. “If that’s the
case… then how did she die? Was it because of… her?”

Rem didn’t mention a name—not that she needed to. Anyone with half a working brain could
understand the implication behind her words.

Satella.



The Witch of Envy, the monster who rampaged across the world, consuming half of it in her
wake four centuries ago. Just speaking her name—or even uttering her title as a witch—was a
deep taboo, one few dared to break.

To even say it aloud risked ostracization, hatred, or at worst, accusations of being a Witch
Cultist. After all, they were the only ones who spoke of her favorably, worshipping her as
their deity.

Or so the rumors claimed.

Rem hadn’t mentioned her name out of idle curiosity. She had done so for a reason—out of
consideration. Especially since the victim of Satella’s notorious reputation stood right beside
her.

Emilia didn’t answer Rem’s question. To the untrained eye, her silence might have been
mistaken for hesitation, weakness, or hurt. After all, Satella was at the core of many of the
hardships she had endured.

But no.

The words simply washed over her, like raindrops falling—uncaring, indifferent to any
obstacles in their path as they sought to reach the earth.

Instead of dwelling on them, she used them as fuel.

Emilia knew the sanctuary’s residents associated her with the Witch of Envy. It was the root
of every suspicious glare, every disgusted look thrown her way.

She needed to pass the trials. She needed to break the barrier. If she succeeded, maybe then
they would look at her differently. Maybe their hostility would fade.

Subaru had earned Arlam’s warm welcome through his own efforts. If she wanted true
acceptance, she had to do the same. She had to prove herself—not just to them, but to herself.

To show them all that she could achieve something on her own.

Without anyone’s help.

“I’m sorry to tell you this, Rem-san, but if you're looking for a different story, then I don’t
have any. All I know is what the legends say—that the Witch of Envy consumed the rest of
the witches before going on a rampage across the world, until she was finally stopped,”

Ryuzu answered the oni, to which she nodded. But if anyone paid close attention, they would
have noticed Subaru scoffing.

“How long will they take?” he asked.

“I don’t know. No one has been able to pass the first trial to begin with, so I’m unable to give
you an answer,” Ryuzu said, an apologetic tone creeping into her voice.



“So, Emilia-sama, before you begin, I have to ask—are you absolutely ready to undergo
them? No matter how long they take?”

Emilia didn’t answer right away. Instead, she took a few moments to ponder Ryuzu’s
question before coming to a realization.

“Actually, there’s something I have to do first,” she said.

Normally, Puck would be here to support her whenever she was about to face something
major. But since her father had stopped responding to her—no matter how much she called
for him, which hurt her deeply—she opted for the second option.

Emilia closed her eyes and clasped her hands, focusing intently. A gentle flow of mana
seeped from her gate, enriching the air around her.

Then, as if answering a call, they came.

Dozens of tiny orbs of light appeared, flickering softly in various colors—green, black,
white, blue, red, and more. Though most were blue, their collective glow surrounded her like
a radiant halo.

The soft luminescence from the minor spirits illuminated Emilia like a Christmas tree,
accentuating her features and making her presence impossible to ignore.

She remained unaware of the reactions around her. Otherwise, she would have noticed Ram
stomping on Subaru’s foot for “lusciously” staring too long at her, or Rem sending a deep,
jealous pout in the Jujutsu sorcerer’s direction.

Instead, Emilia stayed focused on the spirits encircling her. They hovered, some drifting
closer to examine her directly, while others lingered at a distance, simply watching.

But they weren’t just floating aimlessly. For she and the spirits were communicating.

Minor spirits were much like newborns—unable to form words, express themselves audibly,
or engage in structured conversations. Instead, they relied on mana.

Through this medium, they transmitted their thoughts and emotions, sending messages that
carried their intent to the receiver. Emilia was doing the same, responding through mana
rather than words.

However, these spirits were still in the early stages of life, incapable of processing complex
thoughts or intricate information. Their messages were limited—restricted to raw feelings
and general ideas.

Emilia, an experienced spirit user, understood this well. So rather than attempting to relay
anything overly complex, she simplified her message.

She conveyed feelings of determination—the challenge she was about to face—and her
desire for their support.



The minor spirits answered in kind.

Each responded with encouragement and faith. Some sent their messages repeatedly, filled
with excitement, while others offered quiet, steady reassurance.

Emilia smiled at the encouragement she received from the spirits. It wasn’t from Puck, but
their support was enough to embolden her further—to strengthen her resolve in what she had
set out to do.

“Got the support from the minor spirits?” Subaru asked from behind, grinning at her.

She turned and nodded. “Mhm, they were really encouraging,” she replied.

“Even more than Puck?” His grin widened before he gasped dramatically, hands flying to his
face.

“Oh my god, Emilia, don’t tell me you think some random spirits are more dear to you than
your own father?! Ahh, the betrayal! What would Puck say about this?!”

“Puck wouldn’t think anything of it! I will not acquiesce  with your words, Subaru!” She
blew a raspberry at him, a playful habit she had picked up from Puck.

‘Who even still says acquiesce in this day and age?’ This was the mutual thought shared
between Rem and Subaru.

A loud groan broke through their exchange—none other than Garfiel, looking as though he
wanted to be anywhere but here.

“Can ya just go ‘head and do th’ trials? My amazin’ self don’t wanna waste more time
listenin’ to this nonsense,” he complained.

Surprisingly, Garfiel found unexpected support.

“As uncouth as Garf is, he has a point. Useless chatter won’t break the barrier any faster, and
Ram does not want to shower with cold water any longer, lest she resorts to unnecessary
violence.”

“So cold water does bother you! I thought nothing could affect the proud, strong, confident,
annoying—”

“Ram sees that Barasu has been afflicted with delusions. Very well. Ram will prepare her
signature tea to remedy this issue promptly.”

“I’d rather eat dirt and mud than drink your tea, Ram!”

With Ram and Subaru now trading jabs, Ryuzu turned her attention to the half-elf.

“To break the barrier, you must complete the three trials you will encounter inside. Once you
finish all three, you will gain access to the mana crystal powering the barrier. Disable it, and
the barrier should drop—you’ll be able to return home,”



Emilia nodded to Ryuzu’s instructions. They were simple, and she was confident she could
complete them quickly.

Her confidence was unwavering, after all.

She took a few steps forward but was surprised to see the ruin suddenly bathed in a soft blue
light.

Turning around, she caught Subaru, Rem, and Ram staring at the glowing structure, their
expressions shifting to awe and surprise.

Seeing their reaction, Ryuzu explained, “The light means Emilia-sama has been approved as
a qualified challenger in the trials. She may now enter and begin them.”

Everyone turned their attention to Emilia. Before she could even open her mouth,
encouragement was thrown her way, each in their own distinct manner.

“Rem wishes you the best of luck, Emilia-sama!”

“No one has completed a single trial before. If you manage to do so, you’ll accomplish
something great—even if only a handful of people know about it.”

“Tsk, whatever.”

“Ram wishes you the best of luck—only because she does not want to be stuck here.”

“Good luck, Emi! You promised everyone you’d free them by midnight! They’d be very
disappointed if you failed now!”

Despite Subaru’s playful, light-hearted tone, his words had the opposite effect of what he had
intended.

They made Emilia painfully aware of the stakes—the promise she had made in the heat of the
moment to those waiting for her.

But as quickly as it became clear, she shoved those thoughts aside. She was going to succeed,
so why waste time worrying about something that wouldn’t come to pass?

She had resolved to pass the trials, and she would.

“Thank you, everyone.” With a firm nod, acknowledging their support, she stepped forward
—closer and closer to the ruin.

She walked up the stairs and stopped in front of the corridor leading inside. This time,
intricate blue patterns illuminated the walls and ceiling, casting an ethereal glow over
everything.

On the floor, a thin trail of light glowed, guiding her toward a specific direction. Recognizing
it as the ruin leading her to the first trial, Emilia opted to follow it until it brought her before a
closed door.



As she approached, she noted the door’s ancient and worn state—the wood forming its frame
was splintered, brittle with age, and the hinges looked rusty and caked in dust.

She wrapped her fingers around the door handle, the metal cold and grimy beneath her grip,
and pushed it open.

Inside, she found a small, empty room, with an identical door standing at the opposite end.
Like the corridor before, the chamber was bathed in a soft blue light.

She had barely taken two steps forward when a voice whispered directly into her mind.

“The first hardship one faces is their very own past.”

Then, as if a puppet had its strings severed, Emilia collapsed.

Paralyzed. Unable to move. Unable to speak.

Her eyelids grew heavy, darkness slowly creeping in.

The only thought that lingered before she lost consciousness was that the voice sounded
exactly like hers—only younger…






---------------------------------

 

It was late morning. The sun hung high in the sky, bright and shining, bathing the forest in
warm light. The plants and leaves swayed gently with the cool breeze, birds chirped, and
animals wandered through the trees.

Deep in the forest, a figure moved between the trees, her steps leaving behind the soft crunch
of leaves and twigs beneath her feet. She hopped over foliage, weaving her way toward a
bush.

Her porcelain-white skin glowed under the sun, her silver hair shimmered in its light, and her
amethyst eyes sparkled as her face lit up with the brightest of smiles.

Dressed in a simple purple dress, white shoes, and a white coat, she was none other than
Emilia—a younger, child version of the royal candidate for the throne.

In her hands, she carried a small wooden basket filled with edible berries of various shapes
and sizes.

Stopping in front of the bush, she began picking berries one by one, carefully placing them
into her basket. Her fingers moved slowly, methodically, as she counted each one aloud.



“Ninety-eight, ninety-nine… umm, what comes after that?” She paused, momentarily stuck,
unable to remember what came next.

She pressed a finger beneath her chin, scrunching her face in thought. She remained still for a
moment before sighing loudly.

“Uwah, I don’t know! It must be a reeeeally big number for me not to know it!” she
complained, a small pout forming on her adorable face.

But the pout disappeared as she took another look at her basket. It was filled to the brim with
berries—far too many for her to count.

Emilia’s tiny, excited brain connected the dots. When she reached her conclusion, she
squealed with pure happiness and joy.

“If I can’t count the number of berries, that means I must’ve gathered a lot ! I’ve never done
that before! Yipeeee!” She jumped in excitement.

Picking up her basket, she skipped forward, her beaming smile visible to all. She hummed a
simple tune as she walked.

“I finally did it! I got a new score at collecting berries! I can’t wait to get back home and
show it to… Umm…”

Emilia paused in her tracks, her face scrunching up in confusion, her earlier joyous mood
slowly fading away.

‘I wanted to show the berries to someone, but who was it?’

She scratched her head as she tried to remember.

She wanted to show her achievement to someone, but she just couldn’t recall who. She knew
it was a person, but whenever she tried to remember any details beyond that, her mind went
blank.

Emilia took another look at her berry-filled basket, and the feeling of confusion deepened.

Why was she gathering berries to begin with? She used to do this a lot before, but she
couldn’t recall a specific reason for doing it today.

Today…

What was she doing today? Before she went berry picking? At what time did she wake up?
What did she eat for breakfast? What had she even done today aside from berry picking?

Or yesterday. What had she done yesterday?

Or before that? Or even before that? Or—

‘Wh—why? Why can’t I remember anything?’ She whined, pressing her hands to her head.



The more she tried to remember, the more the blank space in her mind expanded. When she
pushed even deeper, a headache started to form.

It grew in intensity and spread. What started in her forehead now stretched across her entire
brain, the pain growing unbearable.

‘Ow, ow! Stop, stop, stop! Make it stop! Please!’

She dropped her basket and crouched down, her headache morphing into a migraine, then
into something far worse.

It felt as if someone had pierced her skull with a needle-tipped stick and was now dragging it
across her brain, causing unbearable agony.

“Please, please! I don’t want this! I’m sorry! Please don’t hurt me! Please! Make it stop!
MAKE IT STOP, PLEASE!”

Emilia was now screaming, her childlike pleas for help echoing through the empty forest,
tears steadily streaming down her face as she squeezed her eyes shut.

The pain had reached a threshold where she could do nothing but scream—even if those
screams didn’t register in her mind, even if she couldn’t hear them through the sheer intensity
of the agony.

Her tiny hands dug into her head, fingernails scratching and clawing at her skin in a desperate
attempt to make the pain go away.

She didn’t know how long she had been here. Didn’t know how long she had been scratching
at herself. Didn’t know the full extent of the damage she had inflicted.

All she knew was pain.

But then, just as quickly as it had come, it suddenly vanished.

And in the aftermath, Emilia became acutely aware of how loud her screams had been—of
how raw and aching her throat felt. She clamped her mouth shut, her cries replaced by soft
whimpers and quiet sobs.

Next came the awareness of the marks on her face, the stinging pain that accompanied them.
Slowly, she opened her eyes, though the blur of tears and unfocused vision made everything
hazy.

Bits of skin clung to her fingernails. Strands of silver hair lay scattered.

Heaving, Emilia remained on the ground for some time, trying to gather herself, trying to
bring her sobs under control—trying desperately to suppress the terror clawing at her heart.

The fear that the pain would return.

That it would put her back in that same helpless, hopeless state.



Just the thought of it made her shudder, made her whimper.

Eventually, Emilia forced herself to stand, her crying now reduced to tired sniffles. Her
clothes were dirtied, stained from the ground, and her berry basket lay tipped over on the
earth.

A rabbit had found her discarded berries, nibbling away, its soft white fur now tinted with
berry juice.

On any other day, she might have found the sight cute. But right now, she couldn’t bring
herself to feel anything at all.

Her young, frightened mind latched onto only one thought—only one priority.

‘Home… I want to go back home. I don’t want to feel the pain again.’

With that, she bolted. Her tiny legs and muscles carried her as fast as they possibly could. Her
sole purpose was to find her home—to ask for help or at least hide beneath her bed.

At least under her bed, the pain wouldn’t be able to reach her there.

But as she ran, she stumbled into a small clearing. Emilia had been running with her eyes
barely open, so she let out a scared yelp as she crashed into something and fell onto her
behind.

“N-No, no, no! P-Please don’t h-hurt me! I—I d-did nothing to you! P-Please!” she begged,
fresh tears now spilling down her cheeks as she wrapped her arms around herself in a
desperate attempt to protect herself.

Minutes passed, and when nothing happened, Emilia hesitantly opened her eyes—only to
find herself staring at the back of something.

No… someone.

He was clad in a dark black cloak, and she could just make out dark green hair peeking out
from beneath a flat hat clinging to his head.

Emilia’s eyes lit up.

This stranger hadn’t attacked her. That meant he wasn’t the person who had caused the pain
in her head.

M-Maybe he was an elf—someone she could ask for help?

For the first time since the ordeal began, Emilia felt relief rise within her chest, hope stirring
now that she had finally found someone who could help.

“E-E-excuse me, m-mister,” she stammered, her voice shy and low, tinged with a lingering
trace of fear. “I—I n-need help… C-Can you h-help me?”



“…”

“I-I w-was in the f-forest p-picking berries when s-suddenly… m-my head started to h-hurt
reeeeally badly f-for no reason,” she shuddered slightly at the memory.

“…”

“I—I d-don’t know w-where it c-came from. Or h-how it happened. B-but it h-hurt me r-
really badly… I—I c-couldn’t handle it at all…”

“…”

“C-C-can y-you t-take me b-back home? M-my home is in the v-village… s-somewhere in
the f-forest. P-Please…”

Throughout her pleading, she hadn’t noticed that the person remained motionless, not
reacting to her words or even shifting in the slightest. It was only after she stopped speaking
that the realization struck her—he had yet to respond or acknowledge her presence in any
way.

“M-Mister… A-Are you t-there?” she called out hesitantly, concerned creeping into her voice
as she studied him.

Maybe he was suffering just like she had. If that was the case, she had to help him. The pain
had terrified her, but she couldn’t just stand by while someone else endured it alone.

“M-Mister, a-are you o-okay? A-Are you f-feeling a-alright?” she asked, inching closer, her
tiny hand tentatively reaching toward him, trembling slightly.

“If—If y-you’re f-feeling pain, p-please t-tell me… I-I think I can h-help—”

Her words cut off the moment her fingers brushed against his shoulder, her breath hitching as
ice rapidly spread across the fabric beneath her touch. The deep black of his cloak was
consumed by a jagged sheet of blue frost, sealing itself in place as if her very presence had
triggered it.

“Eh?” she squeaked, glancing between her trembling hand and the frozen patch, confusion
swirling through her mind. What had just happened?

Before she could process it, the man abruptly stood up, the sudden movement shaking off her
grip as he pulled away. His actions were slow yet deliberate, a strange heaviness in the way
he turned to face her.

And the moment she saw him fully, Emilia gasped loudly, her eyes widening in shock.

His face was indistinct, blurred like trying to peer through tear-filled eyes. No matter how
much she focused, she couldn’t make out any features, nothing solid or recognizable—just a
vague, hazy outline of a person.

She couldn’t even be certain if he was a man or a woman.



But the uncertainty surrounding his identity paled in comparison to what he was holding.

Cradled in his arms was another figure, just as featureless and distorted, yet undeniably
lifeless. Though their identity remained obscured, one thing was unmistakably clear.

A slow, steady trickle of crimson liquid dripped from the body, staining the dirt below.

Blood.

The body was drenched in blood, brutal wounds and scars marring its lifeless form. The deep
crimson soaked through the fabric, dripping steadily onto the ground below.

The sight made Emilia’s breath hitch, her small, delicate feet frozen in pure shock, trembling
uncontrollably. Her amethyst eyes shrank to pinpricks as she stared, horrified, at the
gruesome scene before her.

She only managed to move when the corpse’s hand lifted—reaching for her face.

“No, no, no, no! S-Stay back!” she shrieked, turning sharply before bolting in absolute terror.

Tears streamed down her face in waterfalls, her breath coming in sharp, ragged gasps despite
the fact that she was not physically exhausted. Her heart hammered violently in her chest,
like a blacksmith striking molten iron.

She was shouting, screaming—fear had fully taken hold of her, shoving all reason aside. The
only thought racing through her mind was escape.

She didn’t know how long she had been running or how long she had been screaming. But by
the time she spotted the rooftops of her home village, her clothes and body were filthy with
mud and dirt, her throat was raw and aching, and her voice had turned hoarse and strained.

“H-h-home! Finally home!” she cried out, her voice breaking with relief, desperate for the
safety she longed for.

Without hesitation, she dashed forward, weaving through houses, leaping over fences and
wheelbarrows as she rushed toward the village center.

“Help… Help! Please help me!” she called, sprinting toward the first person she laid eyes on.
Ignoring all sense of decorum, she crashed into them, nearly knocking them to the ground.

“Help! Y-You gotta help me! S-Some meanie tried to h-hurt me, and—there was this d-dead
body, and—and—”

But Emilia stopped abruptly, her voice cutting off completely as the figure turned to her.

She froze. Staring in pure, unfiltered horror.

She couldn’t make out a face.

All she could see—just like the others—was a blur.



“No—no, no, no, no! Y-You c-can’t—”

The chilling sound of frost crackled through the air as the fabric beneath her fingers stiffened,
rapidly turning to ice. In the blink of an eye, the frost consumed everything, encasing them in
a crystalline prison, fully transforming them into an unmoving statue of ice.

Emilia stared at what she had done, horror striking deep into her bones as she stumbled
backward, her legs weak beneath her. Falling onto the ground, she scrambled away, retreating
until her back met the cold, solid wall behind her.

Only then did she realize the commotion she had caused.

Figures surrounded her—faceless and blurred. Some stared at the frozen person while others
focused entirely on her. Their words were lost to her ears, indecipherable murmurs filling the
space around her, but she knew.

They were talking about her.

They were speaking in hushed voices, whispering unkind things she couldn’t make out yet
could feel deep within her heart.

“N-No...” she whimpered, her voice barely audible, trembling as she clutched her arms
around herself. “P-Please stop... I—I didn’t mean to... It was an accident, I swear!”

But nothing changed.

Their murmurs continued.

The gathering grew larger, their unseen eyes locked onto her, their whispers pressing down
harder and harder, suffocating her, drowning her in a sea of condemnation and hatred. Every
second that passed weighed on her shoulders, a burden far too heavy for her small frame to
bear.

Then, something inside her broke.

“Aaaaahhhhhhh!”

With a desperate scream, a wave of ice burst from her, surging outward in uncontrollable
force. It did not stop; it only grew, expanding in strength and intensity, freezing everything in
its path.

And then—

“AAAAHHHHHH!”

One final, explosive cry sent a massive surge of ice unlike anything before cascading across
the village. Snowflakes fell upon her clothes, white and blue covering the world around her,
the biting cold pressing against her skin.

But as her eyes darted across the scene, her breath caught in her throat.



Statues—dozens of them—stood frozen in place. Their movements were captured in
unnerving stillness, ensnared in her icy storm, frozen in time as though the very moment had
been sealed forever.

Emilia could only stare in horror, unable to process the overwhelming weight of what had
happened. As if in response to the devastation around her, she felt her own body turning cold
—life draining from her as numbing frost spread across her skin. Each breath left behind a
delicate mist, the only proof that she was still there, still breathing, still existing for one final
moment.

Then, she felt herself freeze entirely.

Everything faded to darkness.






---------------------------------

 

Darkness.

That was what surrounded her. That was all she could see. That was everything she could
feel.

Nothing but an empty, lifeless, lightless void.

Yet she paid it no mind, lost in the torment of her own thoughts.

She sat on the ground, motionless, tears pouring down her face, her expression frozen in
absolute horror, fear, despair, and sadness. Each sob was broken, uneven, raw—a sound of
pure grief that filled the emptiness around her.

“I—I… It was me—I—I did it.” Her voice barely escaped her lips, fractured into painful
gasps as she cried uncontrollably.

This wasn’t the child Emilia, but the older, more mature version of herself—or at least who
she was supposed to be. But in this moment, there was nothing poised or composed about
her. Her disheveled form, her tear-streaked face, her trembling hands—all of it spoke to the
absolute ruin within her heart.

Not that it mattered.

Nothing mattered.

The only thing occupying her mind was what she had seen—what she had lived—what she
had done .

She was the cause of it all.



She was the one who had trapped the elves in eternal winter.

She was the one who had frozen the Elior Forest and turned it into a wasteland of unending
frost.

She was the one who had condemned her own people to an everlasting prison.

And now, the weight of that truth pressed against her chest, suffocating her, crushing her
under its unbearable force.

The realization sliced through her, the pain so deep that she could feel her heart threatening to
shatter into countless fragments. The tightening in her chest was relentless, her breath
hitching, unable to steady itself against the overwhelming burden.

“A m—monster… T-that’s who I am—just a monster… I—I—”

“You’re right.”

Emilia flinched violently, a startled shriek tearing from her lips as she whipped around to see
a frozen elf standing before her.

“You are a monster.”

The voice crawled through the void, warped and distorted, echoing from the depths with an
unnatural reverberation. She could only stare, trembling, as more voices followed.

“You froze us.”

She turned sharply, her breathing ragged, her entire body stiffening as another statue
appeared.

“You did this…”

“You killed us all…”

Two more figures emerged, their frozen forms inching closer, their lifeless voices bearing
down on her.

And then—more.

More and more statues manifested, surrounding her in a suffocating circle of ice and
condemnation.

“You did this...”

“You froze us...” 

“You killed us...” 

“You murderer...” 

“You monster...”



The accusations rose together, hundreds of voices crashing against her all at once, filling the
void with an overwhelming cacophony of judgment. The distortion in their tones twisted and
warped, making every word unbearable, every sound razor-sharp as it slashed through her
mind.

Emilia had stopped moving altogether, her breath locked in her throat, her wide, unblinking
eyes reflecting the horror before her. Every whisper—every damning word—dug into her
spirit, burying her in an unrelenting flood of condemnation.

Then, just as suddenly as they had appeared, the figures vanished, leaving her alone in
suffocating silence.

But the silence did not last long.

Before her stood the corpse—the one she had seen before. Only now, it stood on its own, its
blurry, indistinct face turning directly toward her, locking onto her with an unwavering gaze.

“You killed me...”

The words were cold, devoid of emotion, unkind and indifferent to the torment threatening to
rip her apart.

“I protected you. I took care of you. I fed you. I dressed you. I raised you...”

Each word crashed into her like a tidal wave, cutting deeper and deeper, stabbing at her heart,
hammering against her mind. There was no escape, no pause, no mercy in the voice’s
relentless accusations.

“But you betrayed me...”

Emilia’s breath hitched, her heart frozen in her chest, the pulse of fear pushing against her
ribcage like ice spreading through her veins.

“You are—”

The words echoed, stretching into the darkness, twisting like a jagged blade sinking deeper
into her fragile mind. Her thoughts splintered, fracturing into incomprehensible fragments,
too sharp, too cruel to piece together again.

“Nothing but—”

Her body seized, stiff and paralyzed, her limbs locked in place as though frozen in time,
mirroring the statues that had condemned her moments before.

The weight of the few uttered words crushed against her ears, pressing down on her like an
unbearable force, suffocating, inescapable.

“A disgusting witch.”



The word dripped with venom, its meaning clawing at her skin, latching onto her very
existence like an unrelenting curse.

The empty void around her seemed to crack, the darkness shifting, warping, dragging her
deeper into its endless abyss.

Her confidence, her conviction, her psyche had been shattered—Thrown into the depths of
despair.

Emilia had failed the first trial.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 54: Arc 4 - Words She Longed To Hear
Chapter Notes

I'm sorry for the delay; I had some documents that required renewal, and it took quite a
while to get everything sorted out. Hope you guys enjoy this one.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Emilia sat at the head of a long, elegant table, draped in an intricately patterned cloth and
adorned with silver and gold-plated silverware. The soft crackling of the nearby fireplace was
nearly drowned out by the lively chatter bouncing around the dining room’s high walls.

She glanced to her sides—Roswaal sat to her left, Ryuzu to her right. Next to them were Otto
and Garfiel, chatting animatedly. Down at the far end of the table was Puck, lazily curled up
in Beatrice’s hand.

All across the table, conversations buzzed with energy. Roswaal and Otto were deep in a
discussion about politics and merchant matters, while Ryuzu and Garfiel exchanged words
about the lavish decoration of the mansion. Beatrice, meanwhile, seemed content simply
petting the fluffy spirit cat nestled against her palm.

The atmosphere was light and warm, steeped in comfort and good spirits. Emilia mirrored
that mood, her smile radiant and relaxed—as was everyone else’s.

Of course, this wasn’t just any ordinary dinner—far from it. This was a celebration, marking
an achievement worth gathering for.

And really, what kind of celebration would it be without food?

The aroma came first: sweet pastries, sizzling meat, and countless other savory delights
wafted into the room, tickling Emilia’s sharp elven senses even before the doors opened. A
few seconds later, the lavish dining room doors swung wide—and every head turned.

“Behold, everyone! The food has arrived!” came a loud, cheerful shout.

It was Subaru, beaming as he dragged in an elegant cart piled high with plates of mouth-
watering dishes. Just behind him came Rem, pushing a second cart nearly identical to the
first, and trailing them gracefully were Frederica and Ram.

They set the carts beside the table and began placing down the plates of food. Pastries, soups,
meats, sweets, and many others were spread out. Rem moved quietly around the table,
placing dishes methodically in front of everyone, while Ram focused mostly on Roswaal and
his meal.



Subaru made his way toward Emilia, a warm smile on his face—the kind that made her
stomach flip in that odd, fluttery way again. It was something she only ever felt because of
him, and she welcomed it completely.

“Here you go, Emi! I made these ones especially for you!” he said cheerfully, setting down
plates right in front of her.

The food looked unfamiliar—long strands of dough floating in broth, eggs and beef mixed in,
rice with slices of red meat on top, and a whole assortment of dishes she didn’t recognize at
all.

“Ramen and sushi. Staples from my home country,” he explained with a grin. “You’re gonna
love ’em, I’m sure.”

“Hmmmm, these look like traditional Kararagi cuisineeeee,” Roswaal said with interest as he
examined the food. “Are you from Kararagi, Suuubaaru-kun?”

“Kararagi, huh?” Subaru tilted his head, thinking for a moment. “Nope. My home’s got a
similar culture to theirs, but that’s about it.”

“Then where is your home?” Roswaal leaned in, eyes gleaming. “Youuuuu haven’t told us
much about it, if anything at allll?”

“Does it really matter?” Subaru replied casually, his tone light. “It’s pretty isolated and far
away. I doubt you’ve even heard of it.”

“Regardlesssss of whether I’ve heard of it or noooot,” Roswaal drawled with a curious smile,
“your place of origin is of greeeeat interest to me. So try me—whooooo knows, I might end
up knowing about it after alllll.”

Subaru and Roswaal stared at each other, and even though both wore pleasant smiles, there
was a tension crackling beneath the surface. Emilia could sense it clearly—maybe because
she was the only one truly watching the two… or maybe because Subaru was standing so
close beside her.

Even though Roswaal was pressing about Subaru’s background, Emilia couldn’t help but feel
just as curious. She wondered how he’d respond. After all, she herself had always wanted to
know more.

He had told her once—way back when they first met—that he was from a place called
“Japan,” and that he couldn’t go back, even if he wanted to. She had tried to ask him about it
a few times since, but he always danced around the subject with vague answers before swiftly
changing the topic.

Both Roswaal and Subaru were locked in their stare when—

A loud rumble echoed from one side of the room.

Every bit of noise vanished. Every conversation stopped as heads turned in perfect unison
toward the source of the sound.



Of course, it was none other than Garfiel.

And judging by the different shades of red overtaking his face, he wasn’t exactly thrilled
about the sudden attention.

“Oi oi! Th’ ‘ell r’ ya starin’ at?!” he barked, throwing a glare around the room—trying to
look fierce, though it mostly came off awkward.

“By the dragon, is that how you announce your hunger to everyone, Garf?” Ram asked dryly,
her voice flat as a blank page.

She let out a loud, dramatic sigh, then gave him a look that said she was staring at something
utterly tragic.

“I suppose it’s fitting. You and manners are two mutually exclusive things, after all…”

“Sh-shud up! Ah don’ ‘now what yer talkin’ about! That ain’t me!” Garfiel snapped, glaring
daggers at her—but it didn’t last long.

His expression crumpled into a wince as a firm hand yanked at his ear.

Frederica stood behind him, her sharp emerald-green eyes narrowed in disapproval.

“Garfiel,” she said sternly, “what did I tell you about lying?”

“N-nothin’! It ain’t me! I tell ya—Ow!”

Similarly, Ryuzu had Garfiel’s other ear clutched firmly, though she had to awkwardly reach
up due to the height difference between them.

“Young Gar,” she said plainly, no more words needed. Her expression matched Frederica’s
perfectly—stern and unforgiving.

Caught between two formidable women—literally and metaphorically—Garfiel realized this
was a battle he couldn't win. Surrender was the only way to save his poor ears.

“Aight aight, ah’m sorry, O’kay! I swear I won’ lie eva’ again!” he yelped, and with that,
both pairs of fingers released his ears from torment.

“That’s better,” Frederica said sharply. “And quit drooling over the food, Garfiel. You’re
staining the tablecloth—even if you’re trying to hide it.”

“My amazin’ self can’t help it! Tis smells too damn good!” he whined with a dramatic groan.

“So Garfiel finally admits to being nothing but a flea-ridden dog who can’t hold back his
primal urges. Hmph, typical,” Ram deadpanned, her eyes gleaming with smug superiority.

“But I suppose it’s only natural,” she added, flipping her hair. “After all, Ram’s food is
irresistible to all. Bow your head and give thanks to your Ram for what she hath prepared.”



Of course, her words were all bark and no substance. The truth was, the dishes were Subaru’s
concept, with Frederica and Rem handling the cooking. Ram spent more time sipping tea
than touching a ladle.

“Well, as uncouth as Garfiel is, his stomach’s got a point,” Subaru finally said, cutting
through the banter. “The food’s right in front of us, and this dinner’s for Emilia’s big win,
yeah? So what the hell are we waiting for? Let’s dig in!”

Right on cue, Garfiel’s stomach let out another loud growl, like it was cheering Subaru on.
The demi-human shrank a little in his seat, red-faced and defeated once more.

“Ahhhh, I suppose Subaru-kun said it well,” Roswaal drawled, lifting his glass. “I see noooo
point in stretching it any further. I, Roswaal L. Mathers, announce that the feast made in
honor of Emiliiiiia… has officially beguuun!”

It was a formal way of announcing the start of a feast—one usually reserved for when nobles
or important figures were invited. But since this was a special celebration for Emilia, it
actually felt rather fitting to do it in such a grand way.

And with that announcement made, the feast had officially begun in earnest.

Looking down, Emilia reached for the pair of small sticks in her hands. Chopsticks. She
remembered Subaru calling them that. Utensils from his homeland—“Japan,” he’d said.

She’d also heard they were common in Kararagi, too. Whatever Subaru’s mysterious country
was, it certainly had a lot in common with the city-states.

Carefully, Emilia picked up the chopsticks—holding the first one like a pencil, resting the
second along her ring finger. She made sure they were both pointing the same way, just as
Subaru had shown her before.

Then, slowly and with great focus, she reached toward the “ramen” and twirled the long
strands of dough around the tips of her chopsticks before guiding them to her mouth—

Only to taste nothing.

The noodles had slipped free and fallen to the table.

Embarrassed, Emilia hurried to swipe the escapee away before anyone could notice.

In her defense, she had only used chopsticks once before. Even though Subaru had tried
teaching her, she still fumbled with them most of the time. But she was determined—and
getting better, little by little.

This time, being extra careful, Emilia finally managed to catch a bite of ramen—noodles and
all—with just a bit of the broth still clinging to it.

After a bit of chewing and swallowing, only one word came to her mind:

‘Delicious’ she thought, her eyes sparkling.



Rem’s cooking always tasted good—warm and comforting. Subaru’s dishes, though strange
and unfamiliar, had flavors and textures she’d never imagined. When you combined the two?

You got food fit for royalty.

Encouraged, Emilia moved on to the next dish: the “sushi.” She gently picked up the bundle
of rice with its slice of meat laid across the top and took a bite.

And just like the ramen—it was delicious. Different, too. The temperature surprised her: cool
and refreshing in contrast to the warmth of the ramen, but just as wonderful in its own way.

She also recognized the meat as fish—something she only ate on rare occasions, but whose
distinct taste she still remembered clearly. Fish was a rare commodity in Lugunica… and a
pricey one at that.

As Emilia continued eating—sampling the delicious sushi, ramen, and all the other strange-
yet-wonderful things Subaru had made—she looked up from her plate to glance around the
table.

Roswaal was still deep in conversation with Otto, eating with the grace expected of a noble.
Otto was trying to mimic the same elegance… with mixed results.

Garfiel, on the other hand, looked moments away from flinging his utensils aside and just
tearing into the food with his bare hands—if not for the two women seated at his sides who
were clearly holding him in check.

Beatrice and Puck were sharing a small bowl of soup together. Her father was sipping it from
a comically tiny spoon made just for him, looking perfectly content.

Ram sat quietly, eating in silence. But her gaze kept drifting toward Roswaal’s end of the
table… where Ryuzu was seated. Did she want to sit there instead? Was her current spot not
comfortable? Weird.

Then there was Subaru and Rem—talking animatedly as always. Emilia actually had to blink
and rub her eyes when she caught Subaru spoon-feeding Rem, and the maid gleefully
accepting it.

She puffed out her cheeks a little.

This was her celebration, wasn’t it? Subaru should be feeding her, not Rem!

Still, the feast carried on joyfully. Drinks were rolled out and everyone was given a cup.
While most went for wine or some other type of alcohol, Emilia politely asked for a nice
glass of fruit juice instead.

After Puck froze the mansion, Emilia had tried alcohol for the first time—and quickly
discovered that she had a low tolerance for it. And because she didn’t want to experience a
hangover, she decided to avoid it on this occasion.



She had just lifted her glass to her lips when the clear clink of metal against glass rang
through the room. She looked up to find Subaru standing, tapping a spoon gently against his
wine glass.

“Everyone! A moment of your time, please!” he called out, catching everyone’s attention as
all conversation halted and heads turned toward him.

He cleared his throat with a small cough before continuing. “As most of you probably know,
the Witch Cult attacked a few weeks ago. We managed to drive them off, but we had to
evacuate the villagers for their safety. Some were taken to the Sanctuary, but due to…
interference—”

His eyes flicked briefly toward Garfiel and Ryuzu, who both looked away sheepishly.

“The Sanctuary was locked down tight, and the villagers were trapped inside. But this is
where Emilia comes in,” he said, turning to the half-elf with a proud smile.

“Thanks to her, she completed the Sanctuary trials and freed everyone. They’re all home now
—safe and sound.”

“Of course she did,” came Puck’s voice, floating in the air with his little arms crossed and his
nose pointed up, wearing a very smug and proud expression.

“This is my daughter we’re talking about. Her passing the trials was only natural. I raised her,
after all.”

“Well, my little ball of sass and fluff, you’re absolutely right!” Subaru added, beaming.

“And because of what she’s accomplished—freeing the Sanctuary—this feast isn’t enough.
So I think the least we can do is offer a toast in her name. What do you say, Emilia?”

“M-me?!” she stammered, a little red in the cheeks now that every pair of eyes was suddenly
on her.

“Well—I guess—if you guys really want to—but you don’t have to!”

“Hmph. This is going to get annoying very quickly, I suppose,” Beatrice spoke up for the first
time, crossing her arms. “Just gracefully accept it and say yes, I suppose. You passed the
trials—a feat worthy of recognition, I suppose. And in return, this troublesome man threw
you a feast. A toast is hardly asking for too much, in fact.”

Despite Beatrice’s blank and slightly exasperated tone, she was actually praising the half-elf
—something practically unheard of from the Great Spirit of Yin.

It also made clear the reason why the feast was being held: to celebrate Emilia’s
accomplishments in passing the trials and breaking the barrier. And just like Beatrice said, it
really was a feat worthy of praise—especially considering no one had succeeded before her.

“Rem agrees,” the oni maid suddenly added, her voice soft but firm. “Emilia-sama
accomplished something wonderful. A feast and a toast are the least we can do for her!”



And just like that, the dam broke.

One by one, voices began echoing around the table in support of the half-elf.

“You’ve achieved what many before you failed. Be proud of that, young Emilia.”

“I suppose my sister is right. It’s thanks to Ram—and not Barasu—that you were able to free
everyone.”

“It waaaaas truly impressive, Emilia-sama!”

“I always had faith that you’d be the one to do it. And I’m glad you pulled it off in the end,
Emilia-sama.”

“My amazin’ self thinks ya did great… I guess.”

As everyone shared their praise, Subaru finally stepped forward, his voice calm and warm.
His eyes met Emilia’s, deep and steady in her amethyst gaze. His smile lit something in her
chest—and her stomach did that little flip again.

“See, Emilia?” he said gently. “We’re all proud of you. I’m proud of you. You stepped up
when it mattered most… and you did it just right. So you should be proud of what you
accomplished.”

Then, lifting his wine cup to eye level, he smiled.

“So what do you say? Shall we have a toast in your name?”

“…”

Emilia stayed silent, her mouth slightly agape, her expression frozen—but not from shock.

It was pure, radiant joy.

Hearing everyone’s encouragement, feeling their belief in her, knowing they recognized her
achievement and truly praised her—it filled her with a sense of pride she hadn’t known she
was craving so deeply.

But none of it compared to Subaru’s words.

He was the one she most wanted to prove herself to—the one she wanted to show she wasn’t
a burden to. She wanted to stand beside him… not behind him. And those were the words she
had been longing to hear.

“Y-yes… I’ll gladly accept,” she finally said, her voice soft and a little shaky. Her eyes were
slightly blurry now, with tears of joy gently threatening to spill.

“Well, you heard her, everyone! With me—For Emilia!”

“For Emilia!”



Voices rang out in perfect unison, cups raised and clinking together in a chorus of celebration
as everyone took a drink—

Except for Garfiel, who had already emptied his, of course.

All throughout the rest of the feast, as food and laughter flowed, Emilia’s million-volt smile
never faded.

Even when the celebration wound down and she returned to her room…

Even when she drifted off to sleep…

That same smile stayed with her.

Emilia was very happy.

 

---------------------------------

 

"Nnngh..."

With a soft groan, Emilia’s eyes slowly fluttered open, and she sluggishly sat up in her bed.
Her vision was blurry, and her thoughts still foggy—her brain not fully awake yet.

'Wha—where am I?' she wondered, blinking as she turned her head to take in the room.

The bed felt wrong. The mattress was rougher. The room was dim, smaller than what she
remembered falling asleep in.

It took her a few moments to catch up.

But when she finally did, her eyes widened slightly in quiet realization.

"Huh?" Emilia breathed, blinking again as she looked around slowly, glancing left and right,
needing to be sure she was seeing things correctly.

'This is... my room? In the Sanctuary? What am I doing here?' she thought, pressing her
hands to her temples, trying to remember what had happened.

She remembered lying down for the night... Puck had already wished her goodnight and
returned to his crystal. She’d had to give him plenty of mana to keep him outside past five.

She remembered the feast. The laughter. The joy. The toast in her honor. The warmth in her
chest and the happiness in her heart.

And then—

"Hgk!"



A small, pained sound escaped her lips as a sudden shudder ran through her body.

Because... Puck hadn’t come out of his crystal.

There hadn’t been a feast. No toast. No congratulations or warm smiles or laughter echoing in
her name.

She hadn’t even left the Sanctuary.

The truth came crashing down in one simple, heavy realization—

She had failed the first trial.

Emilia began to fidget in her bed, her chest growing tighter with each breath as all the painful
memories from the Sanctuary surged back—along with the ugly truth they carried.

Her eyes began to sting, and soon tears rolled freely down her cheeks. She hiccupped and
sobbed quietly now, curled inward as the full weight of reality crushed her.

What she’d seen... it was just a dream. A glimpse of what could have been—what might have
happened if only she had succeeded. The warm, beautiful moments. The laughter. The
celebration. The time shared with her friends.

But all of it was gone now. Faded like mist.

She had failed—and those moments would never be hers.

She wouldn’t get to eat the food Subaru had prepared for her.

She wouldn’t feel the unified support and praise from everyone at the table.

She wouldn’t see her father again—not when he still remained sealed in his crystal, silent and
unresponsive.

And she wouldn’t hear Subaru tell her how proud he was of her.

That thought alone made her cry harder.

All she could think of now was what waited for her.

Scorn—from the people of the Sanctuary who would surely continue to hate and mistrust her.
Maybe even the villagers from Arlam would, too, now that she had failed them.

Disappointment—from Roswaal, from Ram and Rem—who had believed in her, trusted her
to break the barrier. She had let them all down.

Hatred—she had wanted to win over Garfiel despite how aggressive he was. She had hoped
he’d see her for who she was... but that hope was shattered now, ruined by her own weakness.

Abandonment—she’d wished, so earnestly, that Puck would emerge again if she just
succeeded. A naive, childlike hope—but one she still clung to. That maybe, just maybe, he’d



be there to say "you did great."

And worst of all... disregard.

What would Subaru say now? When all he could see was her failure laid bare? When all her
speeches about determination and conviction ended up as nothing but hollow, empty words?

And so she cried.

She cried for what she’d lost. For what she now believed was out of reach.

Her quiet sobbing echoed in the small room, a soft, broken sound that slowly drowned out the
distant shouting and chaos just beyond her door...

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 55: I'm Back!!!
