blazing, and Isabella was dual-wielding chainsaws with the elegance of Priscilla. Together we
fought through the infernal horde, clashing with the demon lord himself in a battle so
explosive it probably knocked a few stars out of orbit, but I managed to get back home.

But somewhere down the road, I managed to break my limiter, so... Yay?

Okay, jokes aside—In the last chapter, I wrote that I'll be traveling abroad to spend time with
my family, which I did. I also did a ton of stuff and hit up some extracurriculars, and finally
decided it was time to stop being a stick figure and start going to the gym.

I also hung out with friends I hadn’t seen in forever, and it was an absolute blast.

I was only thinking I would be gone for a week, two at most. I didn’t expect the break to
snowball, though—my friends kept dragging me outside like it was their job to destroy any
shred of writing discipline I had left. Pure chaos.

But now we’re all broke, which means no more going outside my house. Yay! So I get to stay
home again, which means writing is officially back on the table.

You guys are waiting for a chapter drop, right? If so, then you're in luck. Expect it sometime
this weekend. If not, then by Sunday. This chapter is going to be intense! Subaru’s gonna
crash out hard because of a certain half-elf, The drama’s gonna be off the charts, I promise.

Anyway, Cio!!!



 



Chapter 56: Explanation/Yapping
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

…To be honest, when I first sat down to type this, I figured I’d come up with some
outlandish bullshit while role-playing as Zombieman about how I got dragged into some
multiversal shenanigans and whatnot, or at least open with some witty remark or something
like that.

 

But I feel like that would just come off as me goofing around, or being insensitive, or just
plain bad taste, so I’ll just say this.

 

Hey guys… I’m back, and I’m still alive.

 

Some of you may have wondered where I’ve been, why I disappeared and haven’t uploaded
in, what, 6 months? More? Some of you might be sad or disappointed that the story you’ve
been keeping up with for 54 chapters and 185K words has simply just stopped, especially
when the last chapter promised that I’m back.

 

The majority of you probably just moved on with your lives, and honestly, you should. I
mean, it’s just a fanfic at the end of the day. Nothing to get too invested in.

 

Well, regardless of whether you missed me or not, I suppose you guys deserve an
explanation.

 

As you’ve already read, I’m alive and well. I fortunately wasn’t subjected to an accident, I
wasn’t hospitalized, and I didn’t go through any major personal tragedies or anything like
that.

 

I’m physically and mentally fine. And I didn’t lose my password either, that’s honestly the
lamest excuse ever. Just press the “I forgot my password” button or something, bruh.

 



Ahem… I don’t wanna get sidetracked, so I’ll just say this.

 

The reason I stopped uploading and disappeared is because I… couldn’t get myself to write.

 

I know, I know… even I don’t really know how to describe it. It’s a pretty… bizarre excuse?
I guess?

 

And this didn’t just suddenly happen at the last chapter either. If you actually look at the
chapter history, you’d see how I went from uploading every day or every other day, to every
three days, then four, then five, then a week, and the last chapter took almost nine days.

 

The thing is, I just… I couldn't make myself write anymore. Whenever I had free time and sat
down to start, my mind would just go blank. Completely empty.

 

I couldn’t figure out how to start, what events to write, how characters should interact, or
how to move important plot points forward. Things that used to flow so easily into my mind
and translate into words just… dried up.

 

I think this is what people call “writer’s block”? I’m not exactly sure, but yeah, I guess that’s
what it is.

 

Like for example, in the last few chapters I’d maybe write 300 words, then stop because my
mind just empties out, or I get bored out of my mind, and I tell myself “Eh, I’ll continue
tomorrow.”

 

Then tomorrow comes, and the same thing happens… or worse, I don’t write anything at all.

 

And then you add the summer holiday into the equation, friends, family, and everything else,
and voilà… suddenly you haven’t posted a chapter in over a month, and then months after
that.

 



And throughout these months? I… couldn't bring myself to continue. And it’s not because I
didn't have free time, I actually had plenty of it.

 

It’s just that I lack the drive I once had. I lack the motivation to sit down and write. I lack the
ease I used to have when writing like I did before.

 

And there’s also real life stuff I had to deal with, like the painful process of getting my
driver’s license, getting my own car, my extracurriculars and just general uni stuff, and
helping take care of my pregnant sister and my niece.

 

So yeah… I guess that’s why I vanished off this site and stopped the story for months.

 

But that answers the “why” question. You might be asking now… what next? 

 

What will happen now? Will I continue the story? Will I go on another hiatus? Will I abandon
it entirely?

 

And the answer is… 

 

I want to continue.

 

I genuinely do.

 

You don’t just sink hundreds of hours into a story, you don’t write nearly 200K words on a
passion project just to drop it because motivation took a nose dive.

 

No… I don’t want that. Letting it go to waste would feel like insulting all the effort I poured
into it.

 



But I also can’t just come back and continue uploading normally.

 

Other than me having to address this disappearance, I recognized over these past months that
the story has its issues. Some plot points aren’t fully fleshed out, some things I straight up got
wrong, and some characters weren’t portrayed as well as they could’ve been. Or I butchered
them completely.

 

I’m going to be honest with you guys… I had no plans for Arc 4 when I finished Arc 3. Hell,
I hadn’t even watched Season 2 of the anime in years. There are so many details I definitely
missed or got wrong or just straight up forgotten 

 

haven’t even properly fleshed out the plot points on why Subaru is the Sage foretold in the
Dragon Stone, or why Echidna seems to know him, or the backstory surrounding all of that as
a whole. And that’s literally one of the core mysteries of the story.

 

And there are other elements I’m not satisfied with either. Like the Six Eyes’s (Eye of the
All-Seeing God) ability that lets Subaru instantly understand the mechanics and names of
anything with just a glance.

 

I may not have stated this before, but I know that this isn’t how the Six Eyes canonically
worked to begin with, and I probably should have clarified that earlier, but for some reason…
I just didn’t.

 

It wasn’t something I added completely willy nilly either, there were actual plot purposes
behind it that I had planned for. But in hindsight, it feels kinda moot that I added this power
in the first place.

 

It’s not that him being overpowered is what I have an issue with, that’s not really the
problem. Rather, it kinda robs him of potential interactions, discoveries, or just… good plot
in general.

 

For example, instead of learning about the world’s magic immediately after being summoned
in Arc 1, he could actually learn through Emilia, Puck, or hell, even Roswaal, instead of just
instantly knowing everything.



 

Imagine Subaru actually studying magic under Roswaal. The interactions between them
alone would be pretty damn interesting, right?

 

Like Roswaal trying to influence him, slowly pushing him, maybe even getting Subaru
trapped into some one sided contract that would absolutely screw him over in the future…
that kind of thing could never really happen with that ability around.

 

There’s also cursed mana… not its existence, but how I used it.

 

Did you know that I originally planned for it to be compatible with Re:Zero’s magic instead
of just cursed techniques.

 

Like imagine Shamak, but supercharged with cursed mana. Just imagine how that would
fundamentally change the spell.

 

Like, instead of just being a dark cloud that blocks senses, it could latch directly onto
someone’s head and only be dispelled by magic or after time passes!

 

Doesn’t that sound cool?

 

…Okay, maybe the exact effects need tweaking, but that’s the point. I want to flesh out and
develop the magical aspects of the Re:Zero world more, because compared to other isekai, I
kinda feel like it’s lacking.

 

take Diddy Tensei for example and how fleshed out the magic there is.

 

Subaru here is already a prodigy in the JJK world, so imagine the kinds of shit he could come
up with in Re:Zero. The different applications, the different spells, hell, even different
affinities he might develop over time, branching into other magic types like how Beatrice
uses healing magic despite being a Great Yin spirit. (I Think)



 

Also, I wanna be honest about a glaring issue I'm trying to fix… sometimes I didn’t properly
beta read my chapters before publishing them. The result was tons of spelling and writing
errors that I’d later spend hours fixing.

 

Me writing and Posting late at night is probably the root cause. I’d get exhausted and just
want to push the chapter out before going to sleep.

 

So yeah… these are some of the things I want to fix, along with other plot points and
character relationships that would honestly require rewriting the story from the ground up.

 

And I’m more than willing to do that.

 

But… that won’t happen anytime soon. I need to actually plan things out, catch up on
Re:Zero since I haven’t even finished Arc 7 and we’re already on Arc 10! And figure out
how I want to approach everything, especially with all the new plot developments I’d have to
add into my story.

 

Oh, and read JJK Modulo as well. Heard that one fun.

 

So the story probably won’t continue for… a month? Two? Three?

 

I’m not really sure.

 

And I know some of you might take this with a grain of salt, since I already said I’m back
once before, clearly, I wasn’t.

 

So why should this be any different?

 

Well… I don’t plan on leaving you guys hanging. Not at all



 

While I work on RE:Infinity Starting Life in Another World (yeah I might change the name,
it’s a bit of a mouthful) I’m planning to write another fic.

 

This one will be a crossover between One Punch Man and Re:Zero, two of my favourite
shows, where a certain guy (or gal?!?!?) gets plucked into the Re:Zero world and has a very
(Bad) good time there.

 

Take a guess who it is, you get a cookie (No you don’t) for your effort.

 

It won’t be a super convoluted story, hopefully, just something simple, lighthearted, and
comedy focused. (Hopefully. Sometimes I lose track of myself and straight up change the
core themes of works because I got too much into it)

 

Anyway… I think that’s everything I wanted to say.

 

Wow… I actually wrote 1600+ words, and I actually didn’t procrastinate writing this halfway
through.

 

I call that a victory.

 

Anyway, enough yapping. Sorry if this loops around or gets confusing, I didn’t plan any of
this beforehand, I just let my thoughts flow like they used to.

 

I’ll see you soon.

 

Goodbye.








Chapter End Notes

I promise you guys, I'll be back!



Chapter 57: Arc 4 - Anger (Incomplete)
Chapter Notes

This is the incomplete draft (2033 words) of chapter 54. Since I'm going to redo the
entire story, I figured I at least owe it to you guys to present you this draft since you
waited so long for an update.

It had been some time since Emilia had entered the Witch’s Graveyard and begun the trials,
and the party that had bid her good luck were now waiting, some patiently and one very
impatiently, for her to finish.

 

Ryuzu stood at the foot of the stone stairs, her staff gripped firmly in her hand as her focus
remained solely on the old ruin and its faint glow. Only her sharp, attentive eyes and strands
of her hair shifting gently in the air showed any sign of movement.

 

Finding a small crumbled pillar lying on its side, Subaru sat atop it with one hand under his
chin, already bored. It was an unfortunate trait of his that he became restless rather quickly
whenever he had to wait without any distractions to occupy him.

 

Seeing that Emilia would clearly be taking quite a while, Rem decided she needed
somewhere to sit as well. After putting what she considered to be her full mental effort into
the decision, she quickly concluded that the best possible seating arrangement would be one
that provided comfort, rest, and would help restore her energy completely.

 

That seat was, of course, the very same small pillar Subaru was sitting on.

 

Because of its small size, she would be forced to sit close to Subaru-kun, brushing against
him and even leaning slightly into him by pure coincidence. Such a situation would not only
allow her to remain close to the love of her life, but would also grant her access to his
comforting scent while she watched him manipulate small rocks floating in the air
surrounded by blue energy.

 



Overall, this pillar fulfilled every requirement of being an excellent seat for the cute oni, so in
her mind she gave it a rating of Subaru-kun out of ten.

 

While those two whose relationship status remained unresolved were comfortably seated,
Ram and Garfiel were handling things in their own way.

 

“Oh come o’ Ram, why won’cha listen t’ me? Ah’m sure yer gonna love it. Hell, ah’m even
sure tis betta for yer legs, so jus’ listen t’ me!”

 

“And how many times must Ram answer your persistent nagging, Garf? No is still no. Ram is
not moving from her spot.”

 

“Persis… what? What does tha’ even mean?”

 

“As expected of Garf. Words with more than two syllables are too large to fit inside that tiny,
pitiful skull of yours. Hmph.”

 

“Hey, can’tya jus’ be nice t’ me? Ah’m tryna look out fer yer health here!” he protested
before patting the stone beside him. “Come on, Ram. Standin’ like that waitin’ fer the half-elf
ain’t good fer yer legs, so why don’cha jus’ sit down over here?”

 

Ram stared at the pathetic demi-human with a flat, unimpressed expression. “Ram can clearly
see the lecherous  intentions behind your words, Garf. The answer remains no,” she said with
finality.

 

Garfiel clicked his tongue and folded his arms in surrender. “Tch. Nothin’ ah say ever gets
through that head, eh? Fine, tis yer loss.”

 

They were indeed going through that.

 



Garfiel stood atop a broken column while Ram remained perfectly content standing upright,
her shoes firmly planted on the ground and her arms folded.

 

After being rejected yet again by the pink-haired oni, Garfiel shifted his attention toward
Subaru and Rem, particularly at how close they were sitting together.

 

“Tch. Ya even got Rem hooked around yer finger? Lucky bastard…” he thought bitterly.

 

While his suggestion for Ram to sit had genuinely come from concern, her accusation of him
being lecherous was not entirely unfounded.

 

Garfiel had known Ram for quite some time, and over the years he had developed feelings for
her. A crush, plain and simple.

 

He would have liked to pursue those feelings, but despite his attempts the maid remained
blunt and indifferent toward him, causing all his efforts to fail.

 

Still, that did not deter him. Seeing Rem pressing herself close to the man he disliked only
slightly less than Roswaal, Garfiel had tried to imitate that behavior in hopes of achieving
similar results in his own romantic pursuits.

 

Naturally, it had ended in failure as always.

 

So he could only watch in jealousy as that man somehow managed to win Rem’s affection. It
surprised Garfiel greatly because from his limited interactions, Rem had always appeared
colder and more distant than her sister.

 

And yet there she was, looking completely like a girl in love, while he himself failed
miserably with Ram.

 



However, while Garfiel could only watch from afar, someone else had no intention of doing
so.

 

“…Nee-sama?” Rem called when she suddenly noticed her sister standing directly in front of
her. She had been so absorbed in watching Subaru’s magic display that she had not noticed
Ram approaching. She instinctively pulled back slightly, putting a bit of distance between
herself and Subaru as a faint blush spread across her face.

 

“Rammy?” Subaru said as well, the floating stones dropping with soft clatters as his attention
shifted to the pink-haired maid.

 

Ram did not respond immediately. She remained silent, but the fierce, narrowed look in her
dark red eyes made Subaru feel as if a pit had opened in his stomach.

 

After a tense moment of silence, Ram finally spoke.

 

“Barasu,” she began, “Ram would like to have a discussion with you.”

 

Subaru blinked behind his glasses. “A discussion?” he echoed.

 

Was that all she wanted? Just a talk? He silently exhaled in relief as he felt the pit in his
stomach eased slightly.

 

Whenever Ram looked at someone like that, it usually meant they were about to receive
either a scathing verbal lecture or a mountain of extra chores. depending on her mood.

 

Ever since the last incident, his body, much like a certain ugly shikigami, had adapted to send
out major alarm signals. The pit forming in his stomach was one such signal, its intensity
rising and falling depending entirely on the level of threat he was facing.

 

And what was that last incident, one might wonder?



 

Foolish question.

 

Some things were simply better left unasked.

 

“Sure, Rammy. Whatcha need—”

 

“A private discussion,” she interrupted calmly, turning and pointing toward the nearby forest.
“Alone. Just the two of us.”

 

‘...Ahh, crap’ The pit in his stomach immediately returned twice as strong.

 

Forcing a smile, Subaru nodded and stood. “Okay then.”

 

“Nee-sama…” Rem whispered anxiously as she watched him walk away.

 

“Rem, please remain here. We will return shortly,” Ram said before following after Subaru
without waiting for a reply.

 

Rem was left staring at the forest where two of the most important people in her life had just
disappeared.

 

What did Nee-sama want to discuss with Subaru-kun, and why did it have to be private?

 

Her curiosity quickly spiraled into overdrive.

 

Rem possessed a very vivid imagination, especially when it came to Subaru. Her mind began
drawing parallels between this situation and two past moments, when she and Subaru had



shared intimate conversations under the night sky.

 

When she compared those memories to what was happening now, her face suddenly turned
bright red.

 

“N-no way…” she whispered as she sprang to her feet.

 

The conclusion she reached filled her with a storm of conflicting emotions.

 

‘Does Nee-sama… like Subaru-kun?!’

 

It sounded absurd, and yet somehow it perfectly made sense. Subaru was undeniably
handsome, the kind of man whose charm could make any woman weak in the knees without
much effort at all. Her older, prideful sister was no exception to that.

 

That realization hurt far more than she had expected it to. Even so, Rem had always known
that Subaru’s heart was vast, far too vast to ever belong to only one person.

 

If her sister truly loved him, and if Subaru returned those feelings in kind…

 

Then Rem would simply accept it.

 

How could she not when this was her amazing nee-sama, her role model, the person she had
admired and looked up to ever since their childhood?

 

So she would accept it, as long as she herself could still hold a place within his heart, even if
it was only a piece of it.

 



With that heavy, tightening feeling settling deep in her chest, she slowly reached a quiet
resolve. If it truly came to that, then she would gather her courage and somehow persuade her
sister to share Subaru with her.

 

But while Rem remained lost in those spiraling thoughts, trying to process the overwhelming
implications of this new possibility, a certain blonde haired individual was most certainly not
taking the situation nearly as gracefully.

 

That very blonde haired person could only glare at the retreating figures disappearing into the
forest, his sharp eyes narrowing as a thick vein slowly bulged across his forehead.

 

‘Damn… even Ram too. Jus’ how does that bastard do it?’ he seethed.

 

<———>

 

Moving through the forest in the darkness, Subaru and Ram walked in silence, with Subaru
leading ahead while Ram followed closely behind him.

 

The silence between them was far from comfortable. Unlike the quiet he had shared earlier
with Rem, where he felt at ease, this one was the complete opposite when it came to the older
twin sister.

 

She’s staring at me, isn’t she? he thought uneasily as he felt Ram’s gaze boring into his back
while he walked forward. He was not exactly scared, but he was definitely confused and
uncomfortable.

 

He had no clue why Ram was acting like this, why she was staring at him so intensely, or
why she had insisted on having a private conversation with him. Those thoughts continued
swirling in his mind until they came to a stop in a small clearing, where a tree stump sat near
the centre.

 



Subaru sat down on the stump and straightened his posture as Ram stopped a couple of steps
away from him.

 

“Okay Ram, so what is it that you wanted to talk about?” he asked as he looked at the maid.

 

Ram did not answer right away. She simply continued staring at him for a few moments
before huffing quietly and turning her head to the side, breaking eye contact for the first time
and giving him her back as she appeared to stare off into the distance.

 

Subaru raised an eyebrow at her behaviour. Shouldn’t she be looking at him if they were
going to talk? That was basic conversation etiquette. Either she was feeling shy or she was
scanning the surroundings for mabeasts. The former would definitely get him gutted if he
voiced it, so he chose to assume it was the latter.

 

“Barasu, before we begin, Ram would like to ask you a simple question,” she started. “Both
Ram and Sissy are born with an ability called 'Synesthesia'. Do you know what that is?”

 

Subaru raised an eyebrow at the question before answering. “Yeah. I know what it is. Rem
told me about it.”

 

And he had also analysed it himself with his Six Eyes, but he had enough common sense not
to mention that part.

 

“And did Sissy explain what it can do? How it functions?”

 

“Yeah. You two share emotions. You can feel what the other is feeling at any given moment,
right?”

 

Ram nodded. “That is correct. It is not affected by distance whatsoever. Even if we were
worlds apart, we would still feel each other’s presence and emotions.”

 



Subaru followed along, though he remained confused about what she was trying to get at. He
already knew all of this, so what exactly was she leading up to?

 

The answer came soon enough, and he would immediately wish it had not.

 

Ram turned to fully face him this time, but her hands were no longer empty. Somehow, she
had produced a pair of shears, the kind a gardener would use to cut thick branches from
plants.

 

Except this one was enormous, nearly half her size. The metal blades gleamed under the faint
moonlight filtering through the trees, despite the patches of rust along its edges.

 

Subaru felt like he nearly choked on his own breath, his eyes widening to the point they
almost popped out of their sockets.

 

‘Where the fuck did she pull that thing from?!’

 

“Now, Barasu,” Ram said, her eyes narrowing into a fierce glare that pierced straight through
his sunglasses, “When you were away at the capital, separated from Ram and her precious
Sissy, there were several occasions when Sissy became… aroused. Very aroused. Those
sensations were transmitted through our Synesthesia, and Ram had the displeasure of
experiencing them.”

 

A shadow seemed to fall over the upper half of her face, leaving only her burning crimson
eyes visible as they stared holes into him.

 

“Ram will ask you this only once,” she said ominously.

 

“What exactly have you done to Rem?”

 

“…?!”
